<a id="archetype-228"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Alchemist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=228)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 175

You enjoy tinkering with alchemical formulas and substances in your spare time, and your studies have progressed beyond mere experimentation. You might throw bombs, drink mutagens, or carry an assortment of helpful elixirs and alchemical tools.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Alchemist Characters</title>

The free alchemical items from the alchemist archetype are extremely useful to characters of any class. The following are just some of the possible combinations. 
<ul><li>Barbarian alchemists can mix mutagens with their rage to ferocious effect. </li><li>Champion alchemists can focus on alchemical items that boost defenses and heal others, allowing their champion's reaction and _lay on hands_ to go further. </li><li>Fighter alchemists can use their alchemy to gain additional options in situations where their usual tactics don't work.</li><li>Ranger alchemists often focus on alchemy and snares, getting extra use out of their Crafting skill and supplying bombs for the bomb snare.</li><li>Rogue alchemists can combine a rogue's poison feats with free daily poisons, and bombs present an interesting way to sneak attack with various types of energy damage.</li><li>Spellcaster alchemists often use their alchemical items to take pressure off their repertoire or prepared spells. For instance, a wizard alchemist who can brew up darkvision elixirs to grant vision in darkness can prepare another spell instead of _darkvision_.</li></ul>

You put your alchemical interest into practice. You become trained in alchemical bombs, the alchemist class DC, and Crafting; if you were already trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You gain the [Quick Alchemy](/Rules.aspx?ID=3282) benefits, creating up to 4 versatile vials during your daily preparations. Add the formulas for four additional common alchemical items to your formula book, in addition to those you gain from [Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5117).

<a id="archetype-280"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Animist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=280)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 56

You have established a relationship with a spiritual entity known as an apparition, unlocking the ability to use animistic magic.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Animist Characters</title>

The animist archetype is a great way to create a character of another class who has a bond to a spiritual entity that they can draw powers from. The apparitions available to animists can open up opportunities to gain a variety of [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skills and unique [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) spells.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Animist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7219) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=659" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 56

**Archetype** [Animist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=280)

**Prerequisites**
Wisdom +2

</column>

---

You have formed a bond with an apparition and can cast [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) spells. Choose a single [apparition](Apparitions.aspx) from those available to the animist. You become bound to that apparition and can attune to it each day during your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575) to become trained in its apparition skills. If you are 8th level, you are expert in its apparition skills while attuned to it, and if you are 16th level, you are a master in its apparition skills while attuned to it. You can spend 1 day of downtime ending your relationship with this apparition and bonding to a new one. 

You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You can prepare two common cantrips each day from the [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell list or any other divine cantrips you have access to, including the cantrip listed in your apparition's apparition spells. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for animist archetype spells is Wisdom, and they are divine animist spells.

<title level="2">Animist Dedication leads to...</title>

<a id="archetype-229"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Barbarian](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=229)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 176

There's a rage deep inside you that sometimes breaks loose, granting you some of the might of a barbarian in addition to your other abilities.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Barbarian Characters</title>

The barbarian archetype is a great choice for characters who emphasize Strength and melee attacks more than usual for their class, as long as they can handle Rage's spellcasting restriction. It's especially good for characters looking to add more damage. 
<ul><li>Alchemist barbarians can enhance themselves with potent mutagens before releasing their fury.</li><li>Champion barbarians might enter a zealous rage when their deity is offended and diplomacy is no longer an option.</li><li>Druid barbarians transform into mighty beasts and monsters before entering a rage.</li><li>Monk barbarians can use the enhanced emotional state of rage to flow with their stance.</li><li>Rogue barbarians are ruffians who thrive in a scrap and are happy to let their anger take control.</li><li>Spellcaster barbarians might wait until they're out of better options, using rage as a last resort.</li></ul>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Barbarian Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6190) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=659" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 176

**Archetype** [Barbarian](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=229)

**Prerequisites**
Constitution +2; Strength +2

</column>

---

You become trained in Athletics; if you were already trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in barbarian class DC. You can use the Rage action. While raging, you take a –1 penalty to AC. Choose an instinct as you would if you were a barbarian. You have that instinct for all purposes, but you don’t gain any of the other abilities it grants. If that instinct has anathema, you’re bound by them.

<title level="3">Multiclass Bard Characters</title>

The bard archetype grants knowledge and powerful compositions that support your allies, whether from the front line or at a safe distance. These compositions use actions; making them a great choice if you have actions to spare.

You cast spells like a bard and gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common cantrips from the occult spell list or any other occult cantrips you’ve learned or discovered. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for bard archetype spells is Charisma, and they are occult bard spells. You become trained in Occultism and Performance; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

Choose a muse as you would if you were a bard. You can take that muse’s feats, but you don’t gain the starting feat, spell or any other abilities the choice of muse grants.

You've sworn a solemn oath to your deity, who has granted you champion powers to aid you in your cause.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Champion Characters</title>

The champion archetype greatly improves defenses, particularly armor. It's a great way for a character to gain armor proficiency or a powerful defensive reaction. You might choose a deity closely themed to your class, such as Nethys for a wizard. 

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Champion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6196) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=659" />
</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 177

**Archetype** [Champion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=230)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma +2; Strength +2

</column>

---

Choose a deity. You are bound by your deity’s anathema and gain the champion’s aura and sanctification as described in the [champion](/Classes.aspx?ID=58) class. Choose a cause as you would if you were a champion, with the same options a champion must abide by. You gain its edicts and anathema but don’t gain the other abilities.

You become trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) and your deity’s associated skill; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in champion class DC. If you later gain a devotion spell, you become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC. 

You become trained in light armor and medium armor. If you already were trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in heavy armor as well. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you have a class feature that grants you expert proficiency in unarmored defense and you’re 13th level or higher, you also become an expert in the armor types granted to you by this feat.

<title level="2">Champion Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Devotion](/Feats.aspx?ID=6197), [Champion Resiliency](/Feats.aspx?ID=6198), [Champion's Reaction](/Feats.aspx?ID=6201), [Devout Blessing](/Feats.aspx?ID=6202), [Devout Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=6199)

<a id="archetype-212"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Cleric](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=212)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 217

You are an ordained priest of your deity and have even learned how to cast a few divine spells. Though your main training lies elsewhere, your religious calling provides you divine gifts.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Cleric Characters</title>

<br />Although many characters profess faith in the gods, the cleric archetype represents a character of another class who’s been acknowledged by a particular deity and granted divine spellcasting. Before a character takes the cleric archetype, it’s important to consider the god’s anathema and whether they’ll be able to avoid it. The many domains available to clerics of different deities also present a variety of options for focus spells.
<ul><li>Martial clerics are typically looking for a potent domain spell or some healing to use in a pinch.</li><li>Divine witch clerics double down as the ultimate divine spellcasters.</li><li>Other spellcaster clerics diversify their options, becoming theurgic characters who combine two magical traditions.</li></ul>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>

</title>

</traits>

**Archetype** [Cleric](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=212)

**Prerequisites**
Wisdom +2

</column>

---

You cast spells like a cleric. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You can prepare two common cantrips each day from the divine spell list or any other divine cantrips you have access to. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for cleric archetype spells is Wisdom, and they are divine cleric spells.

Choose a deity as you would if you were a cleric. You become bound by that deity’s anathema and can receive that deity’s divine sanctification. You become trained in Religion and your deity’s associated skill; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You don’t gain any other abilities from your choice of deity.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

</traits>

Your knack for battlefield strategy and command has been honed into a fine skill, and you can use your keen intellect to help lead your allies to decisive victories.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Commander Characters</title>

<ul><li>[Bard](/Classes.aspx?ID=32) commanders are the ultimate leaders, enhancing and coordinating their allies to achieve peak effectiveness.</li><li>[Investigator](/Classes.aspx?ID=59) commanders are highly intelligent and highly educated, capable of evaluating their opponents and their battlefield with unrivaled efficiency while determining the best way to secure a victory.</li><li>[Wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=39) commanders often studied at a school of battle magic that included practical combat training alongside their more specialized magical training.</li><li>The [exemplar](/Classes.aspx?ID=65) commander grants access to great options for characters who want to help their party work together and maneuver around the battlefield effectively. It’s particularly useful for characters looking to coordinate with their allies to set up powerful attacks.</li></ul>

You can prepare one of these tactics whenever a commander would be able to prepare  tactics. You gain a commander's banner that grants you a 30-foot [aura](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=53) for the purposes of using your tactics, but the banner does not grant the commander's banner bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects. You become trained in commander class DC and Warfare [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41); if you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you become trained in another Lore skill of your choice.

You can prepare two common cantrips each day from the primal spell list or any other primal cantrips you learn or discover. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for druid archetype spells is Wisdom, and they are primal druid spells.

You learn the [Wildsong](/Languages.aspx?ID=116) language, and you are bound by the druid’s anathema. Choose a druidic order. You become a member of that order and are also bound by its specific anathema, allowing you to take the order’s feats. You become trained in Nature and your order’s associated skill; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You don’t gain any other abilities from your choice of order.

<a id="archetype-281"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Exemplar](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=281)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
</traits>

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 57

You have awakened a tiny spark of divinity within yourself, either through your deeds or through exposure to a source of divine power. As you nurture this spark, you can become a potent divine combatant

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Exemplar Characters</title>

The exemplar archetype grants access to great feats for characters who seek to gain a divine ikon and unlock a source of divine power that is not reliant on worship or spellcasting. It’s particularly helpful for characters looking to add a potent weapon or item to their arsenal and enhance their combat capabilities. 
<ul><li>[Bard](/Classes.aspx?ID=32) exemplars combine the bombastic and flashy combat options of the exemplar with selfaggrandizing performances.</li></ul> 
<ul><li>[Champion](/Classes.aspx?ID=58) exemplars double down on divine might, often preferring to pick up a weapon ikon to compliment the defensive capabilities of the champion chassis.</li></ul> 
<ul><li>[Rogue](/Classes.aspx?ID=37) exemplars are often deadly tricksters, combining divine combat techniques with cleverly deployed skills.</li></ul> 
<ul><li>Spellcaster exemplars often use magical spells to enhance their accuracy, maximizing the ability to deploy a single attack with a powerful ikon.</li></ul>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Exemplar Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7226) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=659" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 57

**Archetype** [Exemplar](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=281)

**Prerequisites**
Strength +2 or Dexterity +2

</column>

---

A spark of inherent divine power has lit itself within you. You become trained in martial weapons. You gain one ikon from those listed on [here](Ikons.aspx), the ability to use the ikon’s immanence and transcendence actions and effects, and the Shift Immanence action. Because you have only a single ikon, when you Spark Transcendence, your divine spark recedes back to the depths of your soul and must be recalled with Shift Immanence to re-empower your ikon. You become trained in exemplar class DC.

<a id="archetype-214"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Fighter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=214)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 219

You have spent time learning the art of warfare, increasing your skill with martial arms and at wearing armor. With further training, you can become a true combat specialist.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Fighter Characters</title>

The fighter archetype grants access to great feats for characters focusing on any combat style, and it’s particularly helpful for characters looking to diversify their offensive abilities or focus on more powerful weapons. 
<ul><li>[Bard](/Classes.aspx?ID=32) fighters lead warriors from the front, using their martial skills to stay in the thick of combat where their audience is.</li><li>[Cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=33) fighters focus on a style of combat exemplified by their deity. A shield-using [warpriest](/Doctrines.aspx?ID=3) benefits from the best of both worlds in shield feats.</li><li>[Ranger](/Classes.aspx?ID=36) fighters can either specialize in archery or use their fighter feats to pick up an unusual combat style combination.</li><li>[Rogue](/Classes.aspx?ID=37) fighters can make good use of fighter’s free hand, two-weapon fighting, or archery feats. Making multiple [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=89) can serve them well.</li><li>Spellcaster fighters benefit greatly from the additional weapon proficiencies, and fighter is a solid choice for any spellcaster of a particularly martial bent.</li></ul>

You become trained in guardian class DC. <br />You become trained in light armor and medium armor. If you already were trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in heavy armor as well. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also  gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you have a class feature that grants you expert  proficiency in unarmored defense and you're 13th level or higher, you also become an expert in the armor types granted  to you by this feat.  

You can use the [Taunt](/Actions.aspx?ID=3304) action.

<title level="3">Multiclass Gunslinger Characters</title>

Gunslinger is a great fit for dexterous characters who want a weapon that hits hard from a distance, especially [rangers](/Classes.aspx?ID=36) and [rogues](/Classes.aspx?ID=37). Spellcasters with [_sure strike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1709), especially [witches](/Classes.aspx?ID=38) and [bards](/Classes.aspx?ID=32) with their one-action cantrips, might favor firearms with the [fatal](/Traits.aspx?ID=597) property and gunslinger abilities that improve options for supporting their allies.

<a id="archetype-108"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Inventor](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=108)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Guns &amp; Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 49

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to the Inventor archetype._

You revel in the creation of clever inventions, deploying your brilliance to defeat your foes. Explosives, gadgets, and innovative technologies? You have ideas for all of them, and you're eager to test your theories.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Inventor Characters</title>

Inventor is a great fit for intelligent characters looking to branch out and learn new tricks, especially [alchemists](/Classes.aspx?ID=1), who are already good at [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) and may appreciate unstable options as an alternative to daily alchemical resources. If they meet the Intelligence requirements, [clerics](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) of deities who encourage invention and experimentation like [Brigh](/Deities.aspx?ID=33) are an amazing fit, both because it makes narrative sense and because such characters can usually [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) while fixing their innovation after using an unstable ability.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>

</title>

You’ve developed a keen eye for investigating mysteries.

<column gap="medium">

<title level="3">Multiclass Investigator Characters</title>

The investigator archetype is a good choice for a character who wants deeper investigations or to plan out their turns in advance; it's a particularly good match for Intelligence-based characters like alchemists, witches, and wizards. 
<ul><li>Alchemist investigators double down on science and alchemy to better search for clues.</li><li>Champion investigators can Devise a Stratagem to decide the optimal time to switch from defense to offense.</li><li>Fighter investigators are constantly searching for optimal stratagems in the heat of battle.</li><li>Ranger investigators can hunt down their prey in the deepest jungle and the busiest street corner.</li><li>Spellcaster investigators can use magic and practical skills in pursuit of their lead.</li></ul>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Investigator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6203) <actions string="" />
</title>

Intelligence +2

</column>

You become trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) and another skill of your choice. If you were already trained in Society, you instead become trained in an additional skill of your choice. You also become trained in investigator class DC.

<a id="archetype-206"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Kineticist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=206)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 57

You have, intentionally or accidentally, awoken a gateway to elemental power inside yourself and can now channel that power to devastating effect, adding an elemental arsenal to your abilities.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Kineticist Characters</title>

Kineticist is a great fit for characters with high Constitution who want to add some magical blasting to their repertoire without managing the complexity of spell slots. Kineticist impulses can also provide damage types that are useful against certain creatures and special utility abilities such as better movement or battlefield control.

 [Champions](/Classes.aspx?ID=4) looking to diversify their capabilities, [barbarians](/Classes.aspx?ID=2) with the [Moment of Clarity](/Feats.aspx?ID=131) feat, and particularly stout [druids](/Classes.aspx?ID=6) might all find suitable options.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Kineticist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4333) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 57

**Archetype** [Kineticist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=206)

**Prerequisites**
Constitution +2

</column>

---

You become trained in kineticist class DC and impulse attack rolls. Choose one element to be your kinetic element (air, earth, fire, metal, water, or wood). You gain a kinetic aura and the [Channel Elements](/Actions.aspx?ID=2124) action, though you don't get to use an Elemental Blast or stance impulse when you take that action. You gain the [Elemental Blast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) action. Your Elemental Blast does not automatically gain additional damage dice every four levels, instead requiring you to take the [Improved Elemental Blast](/Feats.aspx?ID=4337) feat. You become trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43); if you were already trained in Nature, you instead become trained in another skill of your choice.

<title level="2">Kineticist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Base Kinesis](/Feats.aspx?ID=4334), [Expert Kinetic Control](/Feats.aspx?ID=4339), [Improved Elemental Blast](/Feats.aspx?ID=4337), [Through the Gate](/Feats.aspx?ID=4335)

<title level="3">Multiclass Magus Characters</title>

The magus archetype grants you the ability to cast a limited amount spells, though you can learn more. It’s a good choice for martial characters who want to add a little magic to their repertoire. After some study, a magus multiclass character can learn the ability to combine their magic and their weapon strikes into a single devastating blow.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magus Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9284) <actions string="" />
</title>

</column>

You cast spells like a [magus](/Classes.aspx?ID=17), gaining a spellbook with four common [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) cantrips of your choice. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You can prepare two cantrips each day from your spellbook. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for magus archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are arcane magus spells. You become trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35); if you were already trained in Arcana, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 179

Monastic training has taught you martial arts and allowed you to hone your mind, body, and spirit.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Monk Characters</title>

The monk archetype is a strong choice for any character who fights unarmored or with unarmed attacks. Multiclassed monks are typically more centered, philosophical, and disciplined than other members of their class.  
<ul><li>Barbarian monks with the animal instinct can combine the barbarian's excellent unarmed damage with the monk's diverse unarmed special abilities.</li><li>Champion monks are perfect for champions of Irori or other deities who favor unarmed attacks.</li><li>Fighter monks can supplement free-hand fighting and add mobility to the fighter's toolkit.</li><li>Rogue monks are incredibly effective because stances grant some of the best agile finesse attacks and flurry gives more sneak attacks.</li><li>Spellcaster monks can augment their combat abilities with [_haste_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1553), [_runic body_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1657), or similar spells to mix magic and martial arts.</li></ul>

    pfs="Standard"

You become trained in monk class DC; if you later gain a qi spell from a monk class feat, you also become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC.

<row gap="medium">

</traits>

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 89

Your fascination with death has allowed you to delve, however shallowly, into the magic of the dead.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Necromancer Characters</title>

The necromancer archetype allows you to conjure thralls to fight for you on the battlefield. It allows you to support multiple fronts of a battle and is most useful to those who like to fight in or near the front lines. Additionally, further necromantic power allows you to control large areas at a time and take advantage of your enemy’s weakest angle.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Necromancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9292) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 89

**Archetype** [Necromancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=387)

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence +2

</column>

---

You can cast spells like a necromancer, gaining a dirge with four common occult cantrips of your choice. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=4180) activity. You can prepare two cantrips each day from your dirge. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for necromancer archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are occult necromancer spells. You become trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44); if you were already trained in Occultism, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. 

Once per turn you can use a single action to create a single thrall within 30 feet. This action has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [necromancer](/Traits.aspx?ID=950), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), and [thrall](/Traits.aspx?ID=955) traits. You can use the Command a Thrall action as described in the thrall trait.

<column gap="medium">

<title level="3">Multiclass Oracle Characters</title>

The oracle archetype is a great choice for characters who want to use powerful cursebound abilities that come at a cost. It's especially good for characters looking to add some high-risk, high-reward options. 
<ul><li>Martial oracles can use powerful cursebound abilities to access unique magical effects.</li><li>Spellcaster oracles can further flex their diverse pool of options at the cost of a curse.</li></ul>

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"

You cast spells like an oracle and gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two cantrips, either common divine cantrips or other divine cantrips you learn or discover. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for oracle archetype spells is Charisma, and they are divine oracle spells.

<title level="3">Multiclass Psychic Characters</title>

Psychic is a good fit for characters who want a touch of occult power. Intelligence-based characters like investigators and alchemists, as well as Charisma-based characters like bards, can choose the path that best suits their inherent abilities.

You feel something awaken within your mind. You become trained in Occultism; if you were already trained in Occultism, you become trained in a skill of your choice.

 You cast spells like a psychic and gain the Cast a Spell activity; as you don't have a subconscious mind class feature, your thoughtforms are simple intentions. Choose a [conscious mind](ConsciousMinds.aspx). You gain a spell repertoire with one standard psi cantrip of your choice from your conscious mind, which you cast as a psi cantrip. You gain the normal benefits for this psi cantrip, but not any other benefits from the conscious mind. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for psychic archetype spells is the attribute you used to qualify for the archetype, and they are occult psychic spells.

<a id="archetype-215"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Ranger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=215)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 220

You have studied hunting, tracking, and wilderness survival, adding a ranger’s tools to your skill set. Your keen eyes while hunting prey help gather more information.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Ranger characters</title>

The ranger archetype has access to excellent options to improve a character’s monster knowledge and survival skills, but ranger is of particular interest to any character wanting to become a dedicated archer. 
<ul><li>[Bard](/Classes.aspx?ID=32) rangers support their allies and animal companions with expanded combat options. The bard’s knowledge can also complement the ranger’s investigation of their foes.</li><li>[Cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=33) rangers are particularly fitting for deities who connect thematically to nature or have a bow as their favored weapon. (Or, in the case of [Erastil](/Deities.aspx?ID=6), both!)</li><li>[Druids](/Classes.aspx?ID=34) have the most thematic overlap with rangers among the spellcasters, allowing you to create a true master of the wilderness.</li><li>[Fighter](/Classes.aspx?ID=35) rangers are among the most fearsome archers, combining the feats from both classes to create a fighting style unique to each fighter ranger. Some warden spells can also be particularly helpful to a fighter.</li><li>[Rogue](/Classes.aspx?ID=37) rangers make excellent snipers or ranged skirmishers, with their rogue skills naturally playing into the ranger’s strengths.</li><li>[Witch](/Classes.aspx?ID=38) rangers add a new prowess scouting to the information they can gain through their familiar and patron.</li><li>[Wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=39) rangers benefit greatly from ranger’s feat support, backing up their spells with ranged weapon attacks.</li></ul>

    pfs="Standard"

You can use the [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=2257) action.

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 221

You’ve learned to sneak, steal, and disable traps. With time and luck, you’ll become capable of moving through the shadows, striking unseen, and escaping without notice.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Multiclass Rogue characters</title>

Nearly any character can benefit from the many skills and tricks the rogue archetype grants. 
<ul><li>[Bard](/Classes.aspx?ID=32) rogues expand their robust base of skills. They are also well-suited to take advantage of the distractions caused by their performances and otherwise apply their skills to combat.</li><li>[Cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=33) rogues often follow gods that support trickery in combat, such as [Calistria](/Deities.aspx?ID=3), learning a combat style that fits their god. However, many clerics might need stealth and trickery when their voices are unwelcome.</li><li>[Druid](/Classes.aspx?ID=34) rogues can ambush foes in other forms, seamlessly fading into the shadows of the natural world.</li><li>[Fighter](/Classes.aspx?ID=35) rogues combine the fighter’s accuracy with extra damage, a deadly combination for archers or finesse fighters.</li><li>[Ranger](/Classes.aspx?ID=36) rogues benefit from the shared focus on trailing foes and catching them off guard. The [flurry](/HuntersEdge.aspx?ID=1) edge can get you many sneak attacks, and the [precision](/HuntersEdge.aspx?ID=2) edge doubles down on precision damage.</li><li>[Witch](/Classes.aspx?ID=38) rogues apply the hexes of their patrons from the shadows and improve many of the simple weapons they’re trained in.</li><li>[Wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=39) rogues use the rogue multiclass to shore up skills or to pick up tricky rogue feats to help keep them safe.</li></ul>

You become trained in runesmith [class DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2051) and [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37). You gain a [runic repertoire](RunesmithRunes.aspx) with two 1st-level runes of your choice. You choose these from the common runes on the rune list as well as uncommon or rarer runes you have access to. 

You can etch runes. An etched rune is carved, inked, or branded; this application does not damage the creature or item. Etching a rune requires an artisan's toolkit. Your magic can sustain up to one etched rune at a time. If you're at least 9th level, increase the maximum number of etched runes you can sustain at a time to 2, and if you're at least 17th level, increase it to 3. You can etch any number of runes up to your maximum during your daily preparations or by spending 10 minutes in exploration mode. Your etched runes remain indefinitely until they're expended or removed or until you etch more runes than your maximum, which causes your oldest rune to fade. Additionally, you gain the Solitary Invocation action. 

**Solitary Invocation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([invocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=956), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [runesmith](/Traits.aspx?ID=952)) You utter the name of one of your runes within 30 feet, which blazes with power, applying the effect in its Invocation entry. An invoked rune then fades away, its task complete.

You can now create runes in the midst of combat. You gain the Trace Rune action.

**Trace Rune** <actions string="Single Action" /> or <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [runesmith](/Traits.aspx?ID=952)) **Requirements** You're holding or wearing an [artisan's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2703); **Effect** You apply one rune to an adjacent target matching the rune's usage entry. You can have any number of runes traced at a time, but each rune remains only until the end of your next turn. If you spend 2 actions to Trace a Rune, you draw the rune in the air, causing it to appear on a target within 30 feet.

<title level="3">Multiclass Sorcerer Characters</title>

The sorcerer archetype is a method for anyone to pick up commonly useful spells, such as _[_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577)_ and _[_haste_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1553)_. You might choose to become a sorcerer with a bloodline that matches other aspects of your character, such as the dragon bloodline if you have the dragonblood versatile heritage or the undead bloodline if you're a dhampir.

Choose a bloodline. You become trained in the bloodline’s two skills; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice.

You cast spells like a sorcerer. You gain access to the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common cantrips from the spell list associated with your bloodline, from the spells granted by your bloodline, or any other cantrips of that tradition you learn or discover. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for sorcerer archetype spells is Charisma, and they are sorcerer spells of your bloodline’s tradition. You don’t gain any other abilities from your choice of bloodline.

You’ve formed a bond with an eidolon, an entity that manifests in a physical body only through their link to your life force. You gain an [eidolon](Eidolons.aspx) as well as the [Manifest Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757) activity. Due to your tenuous link, you can’t gain or use [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) actions. Because you don’t have [Act Together](/Actions.aspx?ID=758), only you or your eidolon can perform an [exploration](/Rules.aspx?ID=2006) activity at one time. 

Your eidolon is trained in unarmed attacks and unarmored defense, and shares your proficiency rank for [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040), saving throws, and skill checks. Choose an eidolon type. You become trained in your eidolon’s listed skills. For each of those skills that you’re already trained in, you become trained in a different skill of your choice. Your eidolon’s initial attributes are reduced. Instead of starting with a +4 attribute modifier in Strength or Dexterity and +2 in the other, your eidolon starts with a +3 in Strength or Dexterity and +2 in the other attribute. They otherwise gain the statistics listed for an eidolon of that type. 

At 5th level, the eidolon’s attribute modifier that was reduced to +3 increases to +4, before applying attribute boosts. At levels 5, 10, 15, and 20, your eidolon also gets four attribute boosts, which follow the same rules as yours.

<title level="2">Summoner Dedication leads to...</title>

<title level="3">Multiclass Swashbuckler Characters</title>

The swashbuckler archetype is a great fit for martial characters who want to be a bit flashier or for Charismabased spellcasters who want to add a bit of dramatic flair to their routine. Multiclass swashbucklers work especially well for characters who already want to incorporate skill-based action and seek out daring deeds to do in the heat of battle. 
<ul><li>Barbarian swashbucklers love to show off their strength and brutality with devastating finishers.</li><li>Champion swashbucklers can show off the powers of their deity to inspire awe in potential converts and fear in enemies of the faith.</li><li>Investigator swashbucklers might love to solve big cases with an audience to show off their prowess.</li><li>Monk swashbucklers can take full advantage of their perfectly trained bodies to perform impressive feats.</li><li>Rogue swashbucklers might hide in the shadows before emerging to put on a flashy show.</li><li>Spellcaster swashbucklers might want to show off their mastery of both martial and magical arts.</li></ul>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Swashbuckler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6233) <actions string="" />
</title>

You gain the [panache and stylish combatant](/Classes.aspx?ID=63) class features, and you apply the bravado trait to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) and any actions indicated in your swashbuckler style, allowing you to gain panache. You become trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) or the skill associated with your style. If you were already trained in both skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You also become trained in swashbuckler class DC. You don't gain any other effects of your chosen style.

<title level="3">Multiclass Thaumaturge Characters</title>

Thaumaturge suits characters who want to glean strange knowledge. It's especially useful for those who tend to fight with one-handed weapons, like swashbucklers or rogues, since they have their other hand free for an implement.

---

You've uncovered basic thaumaturgy. You become trained in thaumaturge class DC. Choose an [implement](Implements.aspx); you can use it to Glimpse Vulnerability, but don't gain its benefits. You also gain a few esoterica, allowing you to use [esoterica](/Traits.aspx?ID=899) actions. You become trained in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46); if you were already trained in these, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the Glimpse Vulnerability action. 

 **Glimpse Vulnerability** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([esoterica](/Traits.aspx?ID=899), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per round; **Requirement** You are holding your implement; **Effect** You glimpse a hidden vulnerability and then strengthen it to aid you. Select a creature you can see. Until you Glimpse Vulnerability again, that target gains weakness 2 against your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) and weapon Strikes.

Your mask carries the legacy of Verdant Spider, the Speaker of Needs, allowing you to deceive and outwit your foes. You can attempt to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) a target from up to 30 feet away, and if you succeed or critically succeed in your Feint attempt, the target of your Feint takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saving throws against your spells until the start of your next turn. If you don't have the [Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=640) feat, you gain it as a bonus feat, allowing you to disguise your spellcasting from others' eyes. If you already have the Conceal Spell feat, you can use Conceal Spell once per round as a free action instead of as a single action.

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. Your mask grants you the abilities of Whistling Kite, the Vigilant Seer, who emancipated thousands. When you are attempting a check to free someone else from an effect that [immobilizes](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24), [paralyzes](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), or [controls](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) them, roll twice and take the higher result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. The GM might decide that this fortune effect applies when attempting checks to remove other conditions or effects to free another. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one creature, you can choose to permit the target to make an attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79).

Your mask is infused with restorative magic associated with Ibex, the Flourishing Field, so it constantly repairs itself. You gain [fast healing 5](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15). If you lose a limb or other body part, it regrows within 1 day. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one creature, you can choose to have the spell also give that creature temporary Hit Points equal to the spell's level until the start of your next turn.

Your mask carries the protective instincts of White Bull, the Horn Forger, and no one will hurt your allies while you have anything to say about it. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one ally, you can choose to have the spell also give that creature a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn. You also gain the Protector's Interdiction reaction.

**Protector's Interdiction** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An adjacent ally is hit or critically hit by an attack; **Effect** You interpose yourself between your ally and the attack. The attack hits you instead, or critically hits you if it critically hit your ally.

Your mask holds the legacy of Black Heron, the Wings of Knowledge, who united the aeromancers of the Shory Empire. You can harness residual magical power to fly. You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only you, your fly Speed doubles until your next turn.

Like Azure Leopard, the Patient Warden, your mask makes you most at home in the night and teaches you how to use the darkness to hunt. You gain [greater darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415). Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell with the [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=143) or [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) trait, you can attempt to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) as a free action. You must still meet the usual requirements of the action you choose, such as having cover or [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) to Hide and being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to Sneak.

Your mask remembers the stories of Shifting Frog, Storyteller of the Past and Future. You can cast [_foresight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=127) once per day as an innate spell, either [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11) if you have Wizard Dedication or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134) if you have Druid Dedication, but the duration is 10 minutes instead of 1 hour. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only a single foe, you can [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about that foe.

Your mask hosts the legacy of Golden Snake, the Tireless Guide, allowing you to guide others with ease. Your allies can use [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) to follow you for any of your trained skills, in addition to skills in which you are an expert or better. When they follow you when you use a trained skill, their circumstance bonus is +1. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one ally, that ally can Stride as a free action.

Your mask grants the extraordinary magical senses of Carmine Jaws, the Hyena who Looks Between. You gain [scent](/Rules.aspx?ID=417) as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406)  to a range of 60 feet. If you already have scent as a precise sense, increase its range by 60 feet. You can sometimes catch a faint whiff of magic itself. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell, your scent extends between worlds, like Carmine Jaws's own. This causes you to be able to smell [ethereal](/Traits.aspx?ID=63) creatures, those in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space with an aperture that's within your scent range, [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creatures and objects, and other creatures and objects that are insubstantial or not fully in phase with reality. Unlike your normal scent, this is an [imprecise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=413).

<a id="archetype-236"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Acrobat](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=236)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 183

You have trained your body to perform incredible, seemingly superhuman feats of grace and agility. You move in ways that leave your opponents fumbling for a response, turning every fight into a nimble piece of performance art.

 Often underestimated, such mastery over the body is useful both on a stage and a battlefield. In fact, acrobatics is an often-practiced art among thieves, assassins, and explorers.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

You become an expert in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34). At 7th level, you become a master in Acrobatics, and at 15th level, you become legendary in Acrobatics. Whenever you critically succeed at an Acrobatics check to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) an enemy's space, you don't treat the enemy's space as difficult terrain.

<title level="2">Acrobat Dedication leads to...</title>
[Contortionist](/Feats.aspx?ID=6241), [Costume Change](/Feats.aspx?ID=7640), [Dodge Away](/Feats.aspx?ID=6242), [Fight Choreography](/Feats.aspx?ID=7644), [Fit for the Role](/Feats.aspx?ID=7641), [Graceful Leaper](/Feats.aspx?ID=6243), [More Real than Real](/Feats.aspx?ID=7646), [Operatic Adventurer](/Feats.aspx?ID=7635), [Tumbling Opportunist](/Feats.aspx?ID=6245), [Tumbling Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=6244), [Virtuosic Dancer](/Feats.aspx?ID=7639)

You can squeeze out of tight situations by twisting and bending your body into unnatural positions, gaining an advantage against foes that try to pin you down. You gain the [Quick Squeeze](/Feats.aspx?ID=5199) skill feat, and if you're a master in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), you can Squeeze at full Speed. Whenever you successfully [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) using Acrobatics, the creature you Escaped from is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the next attack you make against it before the end of your next turn.

You use your acrobatic prowess to evade an attack, using momentum to keep yourself moving if you choose. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses you, you can Step after the Strike. If you're a master in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), you can move 10 feet for this Step instead of 5 feet.

Mass and muscle are meaningless when you propel yourself through the air; only grace and balance matter. You can roll an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check instead of an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check when making a [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378).

once per minute

Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

</column>

---

As is the tradition with many Firebrands, you call your shot and look to impress with an extra bit of panache or a greater stunt. Attempt the triggering check again, using the second result. On a success, you gain the normal results of the check, plus you feel invigorated by your stunt and gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level (double your level on a critical success). You lose any remaining temporary Hit Points after 1 minute. Typically, a challenging task is one with at least a [standard DC for your level](/Rules.aspx?ID=554), though the difficulty may be higher depending on the situation. A meaningful context is one where the action's success or failure is relevant to the pursuit of your goals.

---

You deftly dive through a gap left by a foe to deliver an advantageous blow. Attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check against the Reflex DC of an enemy adjacent to you.

**Critical Success** You move through the enemy’s space to an unoccupied space on the other side of the enemy from your starting position. This movement doesn’t trigger reactions. You can’t move farther than your Speed, and you must end your movement adjacent to the enemy whose space you moved through. After moving, you make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against the enemy whose space you moved through, and the enemy is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against that Strike.<br />
**Success** As critical success, but the enemy isn’t off-guard against the Strike.<br />
**Failure** You remain in your original space but can still Strike.<br />
**Critical Failure** You neither move nor Strike.

The Mockingbird is a master at running into foes and coming away with their weapons. Mimicking their skill, you strike at a foe's wrist while tumbling past them, weakening their grip. You attempt to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) the enemy whose space you moved through. You can use [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) instead of [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) for this check.

Your training has focused you for the opera, and it certainly shows. You become master in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45), and at 15th level your skill in Performance increases to Legendary. You also become expert in [Theater Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) or become master in Theater Lore if you were already expert. When you’re on a stage, in an arena, or otherwise at the focus of a crowd there to see you perform, your eagerness to begin grants a +3 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls if you roll [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40), or Performance for initiative.

You're so fond of using your Acrobatic feats on the stage that you've begun adding your own flair to these dances on the big stage. When you Perform, if you do a performance that is either related to dance, acting or opera, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the roll. If you're legendary in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), this increases to a +2 circumstance bonus. You gain the Dancing Dodge reaction. 

**Dancing Dodge** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658)) **Trigger** You're hit by a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) during the first round of combat; **Effect** You take advantage of the fact that your foe isn't ready to anticipate your dance-like moves in combat. Add a +3 circumstance bonus to your Armor Class against the triggering Strike to determine the Strike's actual result.

If you succeed at an Acrobatics check to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29) an enemy's space, you can Stride again as a free action after you complete your current movement.

Enough of your life has been spent performing that you’ve mastered the art of the quick change—especially when it comes to armor or invested items. You can remove any armor as a 3-action Interact activity. You can don light armor in 2 rounds, or in 1 minute for medium or heavy armor. You gain the Impromptu Investment activity. 

**Impromptu Investment** (1 minute) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** You can remove [investiture](/Rules.aspx?ID=3163) from an item you currently have invested, and this investiture does not count against your daily limit. You can invest a new item in this item’s place.

You are always ready to embrace to a change in tempo and adapt your actions to take advantage of unforeseen developments. When you return to the initiative order after you Delay, you do so in an unpredictable way. All enemies are [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to you until the start of your next turn, and you become [Quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for the current round but can only use the extra action to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

You’ve spent enough time training in stage fighting and teaching a wide range of stunts that you can prepare your companions with directions on how to avoid peril in battle. You can [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2292) an ally’s [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) or [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check with a [Theater Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) check. You gain the Swift Choreography reaction.

**Swift Choreography** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642)) **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet would become [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90); **Effect** You call out a quick reminder to your ally about a special move you’d suggested to them at some point in the past, allowing the ally to avoid the triggering effect completely.

Your performances aren’t just well-known, they’re famous across the land and beyond. Your ability to make people believe the stories you perform has taken on supernatural power. You gain the ability to cast [_fabricated truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1520) once per day as an [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232).

<a id="archetype-324"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Aldori Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=324)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 54

You have sworn the Aldori swordpact and studied the art of Aldori dueling, a famed school of bladecraft that has been passed down for over a millennium from the teachings of Baron Sirian Aldori. The Aldori Academy, widely regarded as the region’s finest war college, is the pride and joy of Restov. You’re filled with pride and determined to challenge yourself at every opportunity. One day, you hope to demonstrate your skill at swordplay to become acknowledged as a true swordlord.

Aldori duelists have much in common with [swashbucklers](/Classes.aspx?ID=63), and many Aldori duelists have the swashbuckler class or [archetype](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=235). Much like a swashbuckler’s daring deeds, classic Aldori duelist maneuvers are often showy feats intended to impress or intimidate.

 Many feats in this section refer to being in a duel or dueling actions. For more information about duels and dueling actions, see the [dueling subsystem](/Rules.aspx?ID=3084).

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

    level="1"

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Aldori Duelist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7899) <actions string="" />
</title>

<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

trained in martial weapons

**Access**
You are from the Broken Lands region.

</column>

---

Your Aldori duelist training teaches you martial techniques and increases your dedication to the Aldori dueling sword. You  become trained in your choice of [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) or [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36); if you were already trained in that skill, you become an expert instead. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) feat for Dueling Lore; if you were already trained in Dueling Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice. 

You have familiarity with [Aldori dueling swords](/Weapons.aspx?ID=535), treating them as martial weapons for the purposes of  proficiency. You gain access to Aldori dueling swords.

<title level="2">Aldori Duelist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Aldori Parry](/Feats.aspx?ID=7901), [Aldori Swordlord](/Feats.aspx?ID=7911), [Aldori's Retort](/Feats.aspx?ID=7907), [Devastating Duelist](/Feats.aspx?ID=7910), [Dueling Acumen](/Feats.aspx?ID=7900), [Duelist's Edge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7902), [Duelist's Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=7908), [One-on-One](/Feats.aspx?ID=7906), [Saving Slash](/Feats.aspx?ID=7905), [Swordlord Exile](/Feats.aspx?ID=7912), [Tempo Duelist](/Feats.aspx?ID=7909), [Unnerving Prowess](/Feats.aspx?ID=7904)

    pfs="Standard"
>

</title>

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

You're always ready for a new [duel](/Rules.aspx?ID=3084), and you've been trained to start and end fights quickly. When you're in a duel or can see exactly one creature, you can always roll Dueling [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for initiative. If you do so while in a duel, you must choose from either Deception, Intimidation, or Perception when you roll for initiative; you're considered to have rolled the chosen skill for initiative for the purpose of dueling actions.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"

If you have your other hand or hands free while wielding an Aldori dueling sword, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC while parrying instead of the usual +1.

You attempt to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) and then Strike an adjacent creature with an [Aldori dueling sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=535). ---

Many assume that a duelist's habit of fighting with one hand behind their back or on their hip is an insult or self-restriction. This could not be further from the truth. Fighting with a single hand dictates mastery and heightens the duelist's focus by narrowing points of interest, allowing them to move and react to changing situations with unnatural speed. While in this stance, you are [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89). You can use this extra action only to [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) or use a single-action activity gained from the Aldori duelist archetype. If you use your free hand for anything, this stance ends. When this stance ends, you become [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) until you rest for at least 10  minutes.

You pointedly note your enemy's deficiencies, filling them with fear and dismay. Strike an opponent with your [Aldori dueling sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=535). 

If the Strike is successful, attempt a Dueling [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) check against the target's Will DC. On a success, the target becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2. This is an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect.

</title>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 55

**Archetype** [Aldori Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=324)

**Prerequisites**
[Aldori Duelist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7899); you have taken the last name of Aldori, sworn to the Aldori swordpact, and demonstrated skill at swordplay by winning a duel using only a sword in the presence of an Aldori swordlord.

</column>

---

You are an Aldori swordlord. You can always obtain free room and board at the Aldori Academy for yourself and your allies.  You can use Dueling [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) instead of Diplomacy to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) provided that the target you are Making an Impression on would be aware of the Aldori swordlords or your Request is related to your standing as a swordlord. Whenever you successfully Strike a creature with an [Aldori dueling sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=535), you gain 5 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) (or 10 temporary Hit Point on a critical success) that last for 1 round.

**Special** You can’t take both this feat and [Swordlord Exile](/Feats.aspx?ID=7912).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Swordlord Exile](/Feats.aspx?ID=7912) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 55

**Archetype** [Aldori Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=324)

**Prerequisites**
[Aldori Duelist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7899); you have broken or forsaken the Aldori swordpact.

</column>

---

You are a swordlord exile. You have abandoned or been abandoned by the Aldori Academy. Aldori swordlords are honor-bound to challenge you on sight. Additionally, your unbridled skill strikes terror in those around you. You can use Dueling [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) instead of Intimidation to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394) and [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) while your [Aldori dueling sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=535) is visible to the target of your attempt. 

With broken pride, your blade is now a disgraced tool used to remove obstacles between you and your goals, whatever they may be. The first time you hit a creature with an Aldori dueling sword each round, you deal 5 additional precision damage.

**Special** You can’t take both this feat and [Aldori Swordlord](/Feats.aspx?ID=7913).

You put on the persona of a rough and tumble outlaw, but your real goals are to report threats to Alkenstar back to the grand duchess. You become an expert in Deception and trained in your choice of Underworld [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Legal Lore; if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. You gain the [Lie to Me](/Feats.aspx?ID=811) skill feat.

Your unpredictable gunfire often catches enemies off guard or hits unprotected areas. Make a ranged Strike with a firearm against a creature that you haven't already attacked on this turn. You gain a circumstance bonus to damage on this Strike equal to the number of weapon damage dice. The Strike gains the following failure effect.

**Failure** The firearm [misfires](/Rules.aspx?ID=1649), but it doesn't cause the other critical failure effects listed below.<br />
**Critical Failure** The firearm misfires and also explodes. It becomes [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2), and it deals its normal weapon damage to all creatures in a 20-foot burst centered on the firearm, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. This damage includes any from the weapon's [fundamental](/Equipment.aspx?Category=23&amp;Subcategory=25) and [property](/Equipment.aspx?Category=23&amp;Subcategory=27) runes.

You’ve learned to react with ranged weapons when a creature is in close quarters. You can use a reaction that normally allows you to make a melee weapon Strike to instead make a ranged weapon Strike. You must be Striking an adjacent target. If necessary for the reaction’s trigger, you treat your ranged weapon as if it had a reach of 5 feet. If the reaction has other requirements, such as wielding a specific kind of weapon, Snap Shot doesn’t allow you to ignore them; it allows you only to replace a melee weapon Strike with a ranged weapon Strike.

<a id="archetype-344"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=344)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
</traits>

**Source** [Dark Archives (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 126

A highly guarded castle in the middle of an extravagant ball, the headquarters of a city's infamous thieves' guild, the locked room in the back of a cultist hideout—all perfect targets for you to use your expertise at blending in. Rather than skulking through the shadows, you use your training and latent supernatural abilities to become a mirror, playing on the perceptions of others and taking on whatever role necessary to get in and out of your destination before anyone has a chance to think something is amiss.

 Performing as an alter ego means going unregarded. Passing as just a face in the crowd is crucial, and accolades come as the gratitude from your leaders or coin from your clients, rather than the awed adoration from a crowd. This arrangement might suit you fine, as you thrive in a job well done and subsist on the thrill of walking flagrantly past your duped adversaries. Or you might find your lack of acclaim festers, a knot of pent- up underappreciation that grows until you can't resist a dramatic reveal or a signature calling card that shows you were there. One final word before speeding away from the castle, a gloating message left behind, or some other sign reveals your skill—usually too late for your victims to do anything about it.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">Alter Egos in Golarion</title>

While some alter egos work independently as freelancers, they're especially popular in all sorts of espionage and intelligence agencies throughout the Inner Sea and beyond. The Lion Blades of Taldor, Twilight Talons of Andoran, Silver Ravens of Ravounel, and various Chelaxian secret police use alter egos to keep abreast of situations throughout the Shining Kingdoms and Old Cheliax. Meanwhile, powerful mercantile groups, like the Golden League in Tian Xia or the Aspis Consortium, employ alter egos for corporate espionage, making sure they always stay one step ahead of the competition. In Mzali in the Mwangi Expanse, the rebels known as the Bright Lions often seek the aid of alter egos to escape the notice of the mummified child god [Walkena](/Deities.aspx?ID=683).
</aside>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archives (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 126

**Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=344)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38); Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48)

</column>

---

You make yourself into a living mirror, becoming a double of someone unremarkable, and you slip into exactly the role that can get you past security or into a sensitive facility. You become an expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38). You gain the Assume a Role activity.

 **Assume a Role** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Requirements** You've spent at least 1 hour studying a creature whose role you intend to copy and have done so within the last 3 days. This could include meeting and learning from someone in that role, tailing and spying on someone, using magic to observe them at work, or some other method, as long as you have a visual source of information; **Effect** You quickly and accurately learn how to do mundane jobs or at least copy the movements enough to appear as if you do. A chosen role can take many forms—from cook, cleaner, or librarian to cult member, priest, or duke—but it's always a role and never a specific individual.

 You perform the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) activity to pass as a member of the role you observed and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks you attempt in your impersonation. This takes the normal amount of time it takes you to Impersonate. You also choose one Lore skill relevant to that role (such as Farming [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for a farmer). While in your role, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks for that Lore skill, and if you're untrained in it, you can use your level as your proficiency bonus. You stop assuming the role after 24 hours, if you start studying for a new role, or if you choose to.

When you [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388), you don't need a disguise kit; instead, simple illusions or temporary transformations ripple over your body like mirror shards, providing the supplies that the kit ordinarily would. When you Impersonate in this way, your Impersonate activity gains the [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) trait.

You can cast silence on yourself as a 2nd- rank innate occult spell and [_ventriloquism_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1740) as a 1st-rank innate occult spell, each once per day. <trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=596" />

**Source** [Dark Archives (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=344)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Alter Ego Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8448)

</column>

---

You've learned how to use even your reflection to your advantage. You send your own reflection to forcibly swap places with the reflection of an enemy, pulling each of you through opposite ends and switching places. The enemy must be within 120 feet, you must both be adjacent to reflective surfaces (such as glass, mirrors, or calm water), and you must be able to see the target's reflection and have line of effect to it. The target attempts a Will save against your spell DC or class DC, whichever is higher.

**Critical Success** The spell has no effect.<br />
**Success** You swap positions with your target or arrive adjacent to your target, whichever your target prefers.<br />
**Failure** You swap positions with your target or arrive adjacent to your target, whichever you prefer.<br />
**Critical Failure** You instantaneously swap positions with your target, and the target becomes trapped in its own reflection for 1 minute. Once on each of its turns, the target can spend 1 action to attempt another Will save to escape. If the save succeeds, the effect ends early.

Knowing how someone thinks makes it much easier to know where they'll be, or even replace them altogether. You can cast mind probe as an innate occult spell once per day, using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

 If you cast mind probe on a target you're studying for the purpose of Assuming their Role, and the target fails their save, you can delay the spell from coming into effect until you Assume their Role. When you use the spell this way, you can Sustain it up to 10 times during its duration, asking a question each time. The spell lasts until you ask all 10 questions or are no longer Assuming the Role, whichever comes first. You don't need to Sustain the Spell to extend its duration—only when asking a question—nor do you need to be in range or have line of effect to Sustain it.

<a id="archetype-237"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Archaeologist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=237)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 184

Adventurers raid tombs for material gain, but true archaeologists treasure the knowledge attained from such sites. You might accomplish your goals with scholarly learning, by training to overcome the tricks and traps set by ancient peoples and rivals, through magical training, or even with a bit of inexplicable luck. Many archaeologists practice a combination of all these approaches. Regardless of method, all archaeologists possess a deep desire to learn more about sapient history and prehistory. Adventuring through tombs, dodging traps, and studying magic are all means to better understand ancient sites, analyze artifacts, and decipher the meaning of any remains that can be found from previous inhabitants. You decide how you will uncover the secrets of the past and what to do with the answers you find.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<a id="archetype-238"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Archer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=238)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 185

Bows of all types are powerful weapons. Generals and hunters alike recognize the power in dealing death from a distance, and from behind safe cover. Those dedicated to the bow—from mysterious cloaked strangers to heartless snipers—are often viewed with a mixture of respect and fear. Like any weapons adept, the archer's skill is forged through experience and constant practice. A true archer becomes one with their bow and is able to make incredible shots with their weapon that most would consider impossible, or at the very least magical.

</column>
