<a id="archetype-172"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Hallowed Necromancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=172)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 24

It's quite common for mages of all sorts to study [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)—the surprisingly diverse school holds the secrets of [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128) and [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) energy, as well as life and death. Many tap into these powers with no consideration of the morality of their use. For these unscrupulous magic users, it's simply another avenue in their never-ending pursuit of power, and the abilities learned are turned to the caster's personal ends, whatever they may be.

 Others choose a different path. Through spiritual study and introspection, they have come to recognize the evil intrinsic in the existence of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), the fundamental wrongness of using the universal energy of death to create an appearance of life. To combat this evil, these casters learn to conduct positive energy and direct it to great effect against the undead they encounter. They may also engage in ongoing study to learn of the nature of life, death, and undeath, and the precise relationship between each state. These scholars and mages are commonly known as hallowed necromancers—a slightly misrepresentative name, as many of them don't use religious methods, but a frequently used shorthand regardless.

 The exact origin of hallowed necromancers' abilities may vary from one to the next. Some are granted their gifts directly by a sympathetic deity such as [Sarenrae](/Deities.aspx?ID=16) or [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14), while others might use their knowledge of religion and the planes to learn such abilities on their own. Though rarer, it's even possible these practitioners might discover they possess an intuitive understanding and control over abilities that manifest spontaneously as their capabilities grow. Despite this variance, all share a fundamental understanding that undeath is an aberration to be quickly remedied.

 Though the majority of hallowed necromancers have similar goals and are willing to work together, they tend not to form their own organizations. More often, these necromancers attach themselves to existing groups—such as the Knights of Lastwall or Voices of the Spire—and use their powers in support of those groups' causes. Otherwise, they plan and carry out their own personal vendettas against the forces of undeath, often enlisting the help of trusted friends and allies.

</column>

</column>

</row>

You've studied techniques allowing you to blend so-called hallowed necromancy into your own spellcasting to bolster the living and destroy the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). You gain the [_hallowed ground_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1103) focus spell. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus spell. This feat grants a focus pool of 1 Focus Point that you can recover using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity. You can Refocus by meditating or praying to connect yourself to conduits of positive energy. Focus spells from the hallowed necromancer archetype have the same tradition as your spell slots.

 Casting spells that create, heal, or otherwise aid or promote undead is anathema to you, as is cooperation with undead. Using negative energy isn't anathema, as it serves a natural purpose, but twisting that negative energy for creation is blasphemous to you. If you perform acts that are anathema to your principles, you lose access to all feats from this archetype. These abilities can be regained only with an [_atone_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=2) ritual.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the hallowed necromancer archetype.

You can either prepare these spells or add them to your repertoire just like the spells normally on your tradition's spell list. When you gain this feat, you can retrain existing spells to replace them with ones on this list. 

In addition, your knowledge of the conduits to the [Positive Energy Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=3) allows you more flexibility with these spells. Choose one of these two benefits. 
<ul><li>If you're a prepared spellcaster, you can spend 10 minutes to replace one of the spells you've prepared with a spell of the same level from the list of sacred spells. You can do this while [Refocusing](/Actions.aspx?ID=71).</li><li>If you're a spontaneous spellcaster with the signature spells class feature, add two of the spells from the list of sacred spells to your repertoire. They are signature spells for you, in addition to your normal signature spells. When you gain the ability to cast a new level of spells, you can choose to switch the spells from this feat to any other spells from the list.</li></ul>

The effect plays upon the instincts flowing through their bodies from negative energy and can thus affect even [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) creatures. <a id="archetype-204"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Limited">[Harrower](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=204)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Stolen Fate Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=197) pg. 13

Whether or not the revelations and divinations of a typical harrow card reading are trustworthy, none can deny that the strange powers wielded by the harrower are real. The harrower uses the ancient art of fortune-telling to harness destiny and augment their spellcasting abilities, infusing them with power by drawing cards from their harrow deck and letting fate decide what elements of their magic need augmentation. For many years, the traditions of the harrower were limited to regions like Varisia and Ustalav, where the Varisian people had more deeply established traditions. But recently, particularly as Varisia's importance in Avistan has grown, harrowers have begun to spread across the world of Golarion.

</column>

You become trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11); if you are already trained in this skill, you become trained in a different skill of your choice instead. You also become trained in [Fortune-Telling Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8), and you learn the [_harrowing_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=100) ritual.

 In addition, once a day when you perform your daily preparations, you can perform a harrow reading for yourself if you have access to a [harrow deck](/Equipment.aspx?ID=824). Draw a card from your harrow deck—that card's suit becomes your active harrow omen for the next 24 hours and modifies several other harrower feats as detailed on the following pages. You gain the Avoid Dire Fate reaction.

 **Avoid Dire Fate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76)) **Requirements** you have an active harrow omen; **Trigger** you fail or critically fail a check associated with your harrow omen's suit; **Effect** Treat the failure as a success or a critical failure as a failure. You no longer have an active harrow omen.

<row gap="tiny">

You draw a card from your harrow deck just before you cast a spell to infuse your magic with its destined potential. If your next action is to Cast a Spell, the suit of the card you draw enhances the spell in one of the following ways. If the card you draw matches the suit of your active harrow omen, the effect is enhanced further as detailed below. When you Harrow Cast, attempt a DC 11 flat check. If you fail this check, you lose your active harrow omen at the end of your turn.

 
<ul><li>**Hammer** The force of the spell is enhanced. This effect only enhances single-target offensive spells that require you to make a successful spell attack or require a saving throw from the target to resist. If you hit the target, or if  they fail their saving throw, the spell inflicts additional force damage equal to the spell's level. This additional damage doubles if your harrow omen is Hammers.</li><li>**Key** Some of the magic remains behind, infusing your defenses. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 status bonus to your AC and all saving throws. If your harrow omen is Keys, this increases to a +2 status bonus.</li><li>**Shield** As the spell's magic takes effect, it heals you as well, restoring Hit Points equal to 2d6 + the spell's level. If your harrow omen is Shields, the Hit Points restored increases to 4d6 + twice the spell's level.</li><li>**Book** The spell's magic infuses your mind with sudden insights about the target. You can attempt to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about the target as a free action, using your spell attack roll to make the check. You gain a +2 status bonus to this roll if Books is your harrow omen.</li><li>**Star** The spell's magic bolsters those it aids. This effect only enhances single-target spells cast on willing subjects. The magic restores Hit Points to the affected target equal to 2d6 + the spell's level. If your harrow omen is Stars, the magic also grants the target a +2 status bonus to all saving throws until the start of your next turn.</li><li>**Crown** The spell's magic is hidden and subtle, and observers may not realize you're doing anything more than manipulating cards in your harrow deck. Attempt a [Fortune-Telling Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check against all observer's Perception DCs. If your check is successful against an observer's Perception DC, that observer doesn't notice you are Casting a Spell, even though normally spells have sensory manifestations. This hides only the spell's spellcasting actions and manifestations, not its effects. If your harrow omen is Crowns, you gain a +2 status bonus to your Fortune-Telling Lore check.</li></ul>

You manifest a ghostly deck of harrow cards that seek to protect you or an ally. Select one willing target within 30 feet; the cards move through the air to surround that target, protecting them from harm and granting a +1 status bonus to AC and resistance 5 to a type of damage associated with your active harrow omen (see below). This resistance increases to 10 if you're at least 10th level and 15 if you're 15th level. This effect lasts as long as you sustain it, up to 1 minute, or until you no longer have an active harrow omen. Once the effect ends, you lose your active harrow omen. 
<ul><li>**Hammers**: cold damage</li><li>**Keys**: fire damage</li><li>**Shields**: poison damage</li><li>**Books**: electricity damage</li><li>**Stars**: mental damage</li><li>**Crowns**: acid damage</li></ul>

You manifest a ghostly deck of harrow cards. Draw a card from a harrow deck, then select a target within 60 feet. The card flies through the air to strike at that target, inflicting 4d6 damage, with a [basic saving throw](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) against your class DC. The type of damage inflicted is determined by your active harrow omen; if the card drawn is in the same suit as your active harrow omen, the target takes a –2 status penalty to its saving throw. The damage increases to 6d6 if you're 10th level and 8d6 if you're 15th level. You can continue to throw cards at targets on your turn as long as you Sustain the Vengeful Spirit Deck—throwing a card takes two actions. This effect lasts as long as you Sustain it, up to 1 minute, or until you no longer have an active harrow omen. Once the effect ends, you lose your active harrow omen.
<ul><li>**Hammers**: cold damage</li><li>**Keys**: fire damage</li><li>**Shields**: poison damage</li><li>**Books**: electricity damage</li><li>**Stars**: mental damage</li><li>**Crowns**: acid damage</li></ul>

You have a knack for drawing the right card, be it from a harrow deck, in a game of cards, or even when drawing from a [_Deck of Many Things_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=610). When you're attempting a skill check involving the drawing of cards or resolving the effects of a [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) effect (including attempting a saving throw against a hostile divination effect against you), you gain a +2 status bonus to the check. When you draw a card to determine your harrow omen, perform [Harrow Casting](/Feats.aspx?ID=4155), cast [_harrowing_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=100), or if you activate a magical deck of cards, draw 2 cards, and choose the one you prefer as your actual card drawn. You can even use this ability when drawing from a _Deck of Many Things_, but only once per deck. The unused card is shuffled back into the stack.

<a id="archetype-391"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Hedge Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=391)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 94

The study of magic isn’t solely the province of tenured faculty who extend propositions or refutations in stately halls of ivory; neither is its practice limited to the dominions of hierophants atop ancient duskwood edifices or wish-apported towers of basalt. Despite their claims to authority, the eminent and elite do not define magic’s purview or purpose. Within quiet, overlooked places, magical inquiry flourishes in countless ways. Provincial villages and remote countrysides are the bailiwicks of so-called “hedge mages.” Away from the stifling support of prelates or provosts, a hedge mage may experiment with old methods in new ways, working with the quotidian in the quest to further hone practical and pragmatic spells into mighty tools.

Hedge mages tend to be a rugged, individualistic lot, whose practicality might seem an odd fit with the idiosyncrasies and idealism so common to their number. Without comforts of station or stipend, hedge mages must make do with what’s readily accessible or easily available, mastering unremarkable materials and processes to achieve extraordinary magical effects. With practice, everyday cantrips and catalysts become reliable and versatile tools. Many hedge mages apply a mixture of simple spells, scholastic application, and hands-on knowledge to solve their communities’ problems, be it blighted crops and plagued cattle or hauntings and monster attacks. Those few who become adventurer find their self-sufficient and resourceful lifestyles to be ample training for that career’s challenges and uncertainties, bringing their unorthodox, yet undeniably effective, blend of magic and common sense to face the dangers of battlefield and dungeon.

Most hedge mages come from the ranks of classes that don’t inherently grant spellcasting. Many of them begin their adventuring careers as [fighters](/Classes.aspx?ID=35), [rangers](/Classes.aspx?ID=36), and [rogues](/Classes.aspx?ID=37), though a few [investigators](/Classes.aspx?ID=59) and [swashbucklers](/Classes.aspx?ID=63) round out the mix. Occasionally, a rural [alchemist](/Classes.aspx?ID=56) will add hedge mage spellcasting to their repertoire. Hedge mages who delve deep into the practice of momentary magic might also become [scroll tricksters](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=262) or [talisman dabblers](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=266).

</column>

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence +2 or Wisdom +2

</column>

---

[The Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26) is your laboratory and altar, and the world your workshop and study. Grounding your theoretical studies in honest labor, you work with the mundane to draw forth their hidden magic. When you take this dedication, choose [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46). You become trained in that skill, or you become expert if you were already trained. You also gain a keepsake that helps your magical studies; this keepsake is something that has perhaps been handed down to you but to which you’ve contributed a few personal touches, though it can be anything appropriate to your personal magical style. Sample keepsakes include a folio or binder of magical observations, a walking stick with mnemonic grooves, a bracelet of assorted charms and baubles, or a planchette carved into shape of a coffin. If it’s destroyed or lost, you can create a new keepsake with 1 day of downtime.

You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=3521) activity. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for hedge mage archetype spells is your choice of Intelligence or Wisdom, and they are hedge mage spells of a tradition associated with the skill chosen for this dedication ([arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) for Arcana, [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) for Nature, [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) for Occultism, and [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) for Religion).

Your keepsake holds 4 common cantrips of your choice from your appropriate tradition. You prepare spells each day by meditating with your keepsake. You can prepare two cantrips from your keepsake each day. You can only add cantrips to your keepsake with the [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) activity or by other similar means.

Want not, waste not; through a mix of frugality, inspiration, and sheer resourcefulness, you maintain a catalog of materials with ambient, lingering magic, which you can transform into temporary [spell catalysts](/Rules.aspx?ID=1509). Be it powder ground from the burnt remains of hippogriff feathers or yarn drawn from the locks of an [alicorn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3320), you have these materials at hand and, perhaps more importantly, know how to bend them toward practical effects. These [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=564) items can change or enhance the effects of specific spells. To get the most out of a spell catalyst, you or an ally should be able to cast the affected spell.

You know the formulas for all common spell catalysts of your level or lower. You remember spell catalyst formulas and don’t need a formula book for them. Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two spell catalysts with an item level no higher than half your level. You must know each spell catalyst’s formula. A spell catalyst created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575) if you haven’t already used it.

You can spend 10 minutes to empty one of your prepared spell slots and prepare a different spell from your keepsake in its place. If you’re interrupted during such a swap, the original spell remains prepared and can still be cast. You can try again to swap out the spell later, but you must start the process over again.

<a id="archetype-262"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Scroll Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=262)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 213

Magic has been written down in myriad forms for a very long time. From the classic rolled parchment to strings tied with a hundred intricate knots, from baked clay tablets covered with incisions to bound collections of bamboo slips, magic is everywhere. You just need to know how to read it. You have studied the art of reading magical scrolls of various kinds. The language of magic is yours to use and manipulate, however unstable and archaic such writing tends to be.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title
    level="1"

    pfs="Standard"

</column>

---

You've studied [scrolls](/Equipment.aspx?Category=52) in depth. This might have been a comprehensive education in a formal setting or the sort of education where you somehow obtain a number of scrolls and try not to explode anything you didn't mean to explode. You gain the [Trick Magic Item](/Feats.aspx?ID=5229) feat, and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to skill checks to Trick scrolls. If you roll a critical failure to Trick a Magic Item that's a scroll, you get a failure instead.

<title level="2">Scroll Trickster Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Scroll Cache](/Feats.aspx?ID=6401), [Skim Scroll](/Feats.aspx?ID=6402)

You have a vast and overflowing collection of [scroll](/Equipment.aspx?Category=52)  scraps, riddled with errors and misspellings and leaking energy like a sieve. With enough care, you can coax these scroll scraps into functioning—briefly. Each day during your daily preparations, you can create a single temporary scroll containing a 1st-rank spell. The spell must be a common spell, a spell to which you have access, or a spell you are able to cast, and you must be trained in the skill corresponding to at least one of the spell's traditions. You can use [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) to add spells to those you can use with this feat, even if you aren't a spellcaster. This scroll is an unstable, temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used it. This temporary scroll can't be used to Learn the Spell. <br />At 8th level, add a second temporary scroll containing a 2nd-rank spell.

Your scroll collection has vastly grown, both in size and potency. In addition to your daily scrolls from Basic Scroll Cache, add a scroll with a 3rd-rank spell. At 14th level, add a scroll with a 4th-rank spell. At 16th level, add a scroll with a 5th-rank spell.

In addition to your daily scrolls from the [Basic](/Feats.aspx?ID=2054) and Expert Scroll Caches, add a single scroll with a 6th-rank spell. At 20th level, add a scroll with a 7th-rank spell.

<a id="archetype-266"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Talisman Dabbler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=266)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 217

The classic idea of magic is that of a hoary wizard, poring over a crumbling book of spells as years pass. But magic is so much more than that—it's thought, will, and action, and with the right talismans, you can make even the cut of a sword a deeply magical act. This all hinges on the small magical talismans you affix to your gear. You know how to make and use the perfect talisman for any job. The utility of talismans seems endless. They can help swords to swing harder, shields to block better, grant a burst of speed in a desperate situation, and even save one from a lethal fall. This all excites you, but no more than exploring just how far you can push your talent. What are the true limits of these baubles? You've heard rumors and tales of great dabblers like yourself mastering the art of creating and affixing fantastical magical memorabilia. Some say that these great sages have found a way to affix multiple talismans to a single object, circumventing the most fundamental limitation of the art. Whether you were formally trained or picked up the skill as a hobby, your talent is undeniable, and the usefulness of talismans is apparent. Take advantage of every ounce of magic you can manipulate and master these mystical trinkets.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Talisman Dabbler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6420) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 217

**Archetype** [Talisman Dabbler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=266)

</column>

---

You are trained in the use of [talismans](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&amp;Subcategory=19) and similar magical paraphernalia. This training might have occurred in a formal classroom or been an accumulation of folk magic picked up over time. You can craft talismans and know the formulas for all common talismans of your level or lower. You remember talisman formulas and don't need a formula book for them. <br />Additionally, you carry a vast collection of magical baubles you can turn into temporary talismans. Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two talismans with an item level no higher than half your level. You must know each talisman's formula. A talisman created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used it. Any saving throw DC required by a temporary talisman you create uses the highest of your class DC, spell DC, or the talisman's DC. <br />Finally, when you [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=2632), you can (in any combination) affix or remove up to four talismans in the 10-minute span.

<title level="2">Talisman Dabbler Dedication leads to...</title>
[Deeper Dabbler](/Feats.aspx?ID=6422), [Quick Fix](/Feats.aspx?ID=6421), [Talismanic Sage](/Feats.aspx?ID=6423)

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

</column>

---

You can attach a [talisman](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&amp;Subcategory=19) using only a bit of glue and some string. You gain the [Rapid Affixture](/Feats.aspx?ID=2145) skill feat, even if you don't meet the prerequisites. When you use it, you can affix or remove up to four talismans in 1 minute instead of just one.<br />You gain the ability to [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=2632) as a 3-action activity from that feat at 12th level, regardless of your [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) proficiency.

<title

>
[Deeper Dabbler](/Feats.aspx?ID=6422) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 217

**Archetype** [Talisman Dabbler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=266)

**Prerequisites**
[Talisman Dabbler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6420)

</column>

---

With some streamlining to your process and a deeper collection of [talisman](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&amp;Subcategory=19) materials, you make a greater number of talismans every day. You can create two additional talismans during your daily preparations.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time if you are 14th level or higher.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"

**Archetype** [Talisman Dabbler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=266)

**Prerequisites**
[Talisman Dabbler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6420)

</column>

---

Normally, affixing more than one [talisman](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&amp;Subcategory=19) to an item causes the talismans to be suppressed, but when you [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=2632), you can specially treat one item you're working on, allowing it to have two active talismans at once. This special treatment ends if you use Affix a Talisman to treat a new item for this ability.

<a id="archetype-353"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Limited">[Hellbreaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=353)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hellbreakers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
</traits>

**Source** [Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers](/Sources.aspx?ID=307) pg. 216

Founded in Isger to protest against the injustice and apathy of their faraway rulers in Cheliax, the Hellbreakers League is a young but growing rebel organization determined to make its mark. Members of the League swear themselves as agents of rebellion to topple the Chelaxian regime and free its vassal states from its oppressive rule, starting with Isger.

 The Hellbreakers League knows it's at a heavy disadvantage in its war against Cheliax as a still- developing group challenging one of the world's most powerful nations. Hellbreaker tactics rely on wit and daring as well as knowledge of the fiendish forces their enemies might use against them. Through sword, spell, and subterfuge, they work tirelessly to liberate the oppressed and remove tyrants from power.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">Hellbreakers' Regimen</title>

Hellbreakers work around the clock, as they know their opposition won't be taking a moment off either. Training is vigorous and frequent, constantly testing Hellbreakers' abilities and almost always bringing them to the brink of exhaustion. That being said, discipline in a Hellbreaker station is certainly less painful than in their Chelaxian counterpart's.
</aside>

<title level="3">Additional Feats</title>

This archetype has some feats at a level other than their original level.
Such feats are marked with a \*.

You’re a member of the Hellbreakers league.

---

By joining the League, you've taken on the responsibilities of a Hellbreaker. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for both Devil Lore and Hellknight Lore. If you were already trained in one or both of those Lore skills, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice. When you roll initiative, you can attempt a Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore, or Society check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about one enemy you can see as a free action, if that skill would be applicable. The GM is the final arbiter of whether or not one of those skills would be appropriate to Recall Knowledge about the enemy.

<title level="2">Hellbreaker Dedication leads to...</title>
[Battle Scars](/Feats.aspx?ID=8541), [Defy Hell](/Feats.aspx?ID=8542), [Devil you Know](/Feats.aspx?ID=8535), [Hellbreaker's Resolve](/Feats.aspx?ID=8536), [High Alert](/Feats.aspx?ID=8537), [Oppurtune Trickster](/Feats.aspx?ID=8538), [Rend Armor](/Feats.aspx?ID=8540), [Return to the Pit!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8543)

You make a telegraphed attack to learn about your foe. Make a melee Strike. On a hit, you can immediately attempt a check to Recall Knowledge about the target. On a critical hit, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the check to Recall Knowledge. The target is temporarily immune to Combat Assessment for 1 day.

Your knowledge of your enemies gives you an advantage against them, granting you a swift reaction to their devilry. If you know you're fighting against any devils or Hellknights at the beginning of an encounter, you can roll the respective [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill for your initiative roll.

 In addition, whenever you successfully [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about a creature using Devil Lore or Hellknight Lore, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next skill check against that creature before the end of your next turn. If you're a master in Devil Lore or Hellknight Lore, the bonus increases to +2.

You gird yourself in both mind and body for danger, steeling your resolve. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 minute. While you have those temporary Hit Points, you gain a +1 status bonus to Will saves.

You're constantly on guard, keeping watch over your allies against fiendish forces—no one can get the jump on your group while you're around. Choose an ally you can see within 30 feet. They gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their AC and Reflex saving throws against devils and creatures allied with the Chelaxian government (as determined by the GM) until the beginning of your next turn. This action gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait, the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait, or both, depending on how you alert your ally.

[Hellbreaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8534); Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)

**Trigger**
An adjacent ally makes a melee Strike against a creature.

**Requirements**
You’re adjacent to both your ally and the creature.

</column>

---

You aren't above using underhanded tactics to gain an advantage, easily routing your opponents when they attack. Attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check against the Perception DC of the creature that's the target of the triggering attack. Regardless of the result, the target is temporarily immune to your attempts to use Opportune Trickster for the next 10 minutes.

**Special** If you have the [Dirty Trick](/Feats.aspx?ID=6472) skill feat, you can attempt a [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) check instead of a Deception check; if you do, this action loses the mental trait.

**Critical Success** The target is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) (including against the triggering attack) until the end of your ally's turn.<br />
**Success** The target is off-guard against the triggering attack.<br />
**Critical Failure** You lose your balance in your attempt to assist your ally and fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

Your in-depth knowledge of your foes grants you insight into their weaknesses, granting you an advantage when fighting against them. When you critically succeed at a skill check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about a devil or Hellknight, you gain a +4 status bonus to damage against that creature for 1 minute.

The creature can also Interact to adjust their armor, which removes this penalty for 1 minute.

Your battle instincts make you more aware of concealed and invisible opponents. You don’t need to succeed at a flat check to target concealed creatures. You’re not off-guard to creatures that are hidden from you (unless you’re off-guard to them for reasons other than the hidden condition), and you need only a successful DC 5 flat check to target a hidden creature.

While you’re adjacent to an undetected creature of your level or lower, it is instead only hidden from you

Your devotion to your cause gives you endless strength and courage to withstand the enemy's attacks. As long as you're in this stance, you gain a +2 status bonus to saves against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects and can make Hellbreaker Strikes.

**Hellbreaker Strike** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517)) Make a weapon or unarmed Strike. This counts as two attacks when determining your multiple attack penalty. If your Strike hits, you deal an additional 2d8 spirit damage. At 18th level, this increases to 3d8 spirit damage.

Your attack can ground an airborne foe. Make a Strike. If it hits and deals damage to a flying target, the target falls up to 120 feet. The fall is gradual enough that if it causes the target to hit the ground, the target takes no damage from the fall.

If the attack is a critical hit, the target can’t Fly, Leap, levitate, or otherwise leave the ground until the end of your next turn.

Your devotion to the ideals of justice, freedom, and revolution allow you to truly punish those who stand in your way. When you critically succeed at a Hellbreaker Strike, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, or become [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1 (stunned 2 on a critical failure). This effect has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

<a id="archetype-372"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Hellknight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=372)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
</traits>

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 24

You've presented yourself to a Hellknight citadel as a candidate to become a fearsome Hellknight. You believe that all who live must be forced to obey the law, and you adventure as a test of your loyalty, discipline, and courage. You might aspire to become part of a specific order of Hellknights, or you might instead present yourself to any law-abiding authorities as an enforcer and quietly menacing emblem of order.

 As such, you begin this career as an armiger. You hope to eventually take the Hellknight Test and battle a devil in single combat to prove your strength and fully join the Hellknight ranks. Until then, you prepare yourself for that day, training with your weapons and armor and meditating on the precepts of the Measure and the Chain.

 Once you become a Hellknight, you're considered to be among the fiercest warriors in the Inner Sea region. You become a bastion of law wherever chaos threatens to rear. You've likely officially joined one of the many [Hellknight orders](HellknightOrders.aspx), following their agenda and favoring their preferred weapon. Each order usually operates in a specific geographical region, but it isn't unheard of for a Hellknight from any order to travel across the world to deal with threats.

 Instead of focusing on martial prowess, you can follow the path of the Hellknight signifer instead. These powerful and enigmatic Hellknight spellcasters support and sometimes lead their fellow knights on missions to enforce unwavering law. You're formidable in your own right, keeping your emotions hidden behind an unmistakable faceless mask and wielding magic as a force of order and authority.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">Edicts and Anathema</title>

Hellknights hold fiercely to their edicts and anathema. Although no magical force binds them to these strictures, Hellknights seen as falling short are cast out by their orders. Those suspected of bending the rules often volunteer for infernal contracts, the geas ritual, or mental probing by signifers to prove their innocence.

 **Edicts** apply the lessons of Hell to bring order to the mortal world, uphold the law<br /> **Anathema** undermine the Measure and the Chain
</aside>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">Lesser Order Benefits</title>

Lesser orders of Hellknights typically haven't moved far enough from their predecessors to receive their own benefits, though current events might grant them the opportunity to truly form their identities. Until then, use the benefits of the order listed below for their benefits. 
<ul><li>**Order of the Glyph** [Pyre](/HellknightOrders.aspx?ID=12) benefits</li><li>**Order of the Pike** [Nail](/HellknightOrders.aspx?ID=11) benefits</li><li>**Order of the Scar** [Chain](/HellknightOrders.aspx?ID=8) benefits</li><li>**Order of the Torrent** [Scourge](/HellknightOrders.aspx?ID=14) benefits</li><li>**Order of the Wall** [Rack](/HellknightOrders.aspx?ID=13) benefits</li></ul>
</aside>

You've started walking the path toward becoming a true Hellknight, though you're currently considered only an armiger. You've been taught how to terrorize others into compliance, but you also continually study the structure and hierarchy of [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=42). You must survive painful tests of your body and mind called reckonings that steady your willpower against all sorts of trauma. You gain resistance to mental damage equal to 1 + your number of archetype class feats from the Hellknight archetype. You become trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. 

In addition, you gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for Hell Lore; if you were already trained in Hell Lore, you also become trained in a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill of your choice.

You've trained to resist the manipulations of [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), and your Hellknight discipline makes you difficult to influence. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against effects that could inflict the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) conditions.

 If a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect would compel you to act in a way that violates your Hellknight order's tenets (as determined by the GM), you can attempt to break free from the effect as a free action triggered by receiving the violating order, and you gain a new Will save against the effect. You can attempt this save even if the effect would normally prevent you from acting of your own volition. You can attempt this new save only once for a given effect, even if you're compelled to violate your order's tenets multiple times. You can't receive a worse result on this Will save than you originally got against the compelling mental effect.

You've learned to wear the iconic Hellknight armor. You become trained in light armor and [Hellknight breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=23), a medium armor. If you were already trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in [Hellknight half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=24) and [Hellknight plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=25). Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you have a class feature that grants you expert proficiency in unarmored defense and you're 13th level or higher, you also become an expert in the armor types granted to you by this feat.

 In addition, when you choose this feat, you receive a non-magical suit of Hellknight armor of a type you become trained in (Hellknight breastplate, Hellknight half plate, or Hellknight plate).

You've forged your body to be able to stand toe-to-toe with a devil, and your mind has been shaped by the strictures of the Measure and the Chain. You've become a true Hellknight. You gain expert proficiency rank in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (or in another skill in which you're trained of your choice, if you were already an expert in Intimidation). You gain the armor specialization effects of [Hellknight breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=23), [Hellknight half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=24), and [Hellknight plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=25), and your resistance from that armor specialization is 1 higher than normal. In addition, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Intimidation checks while wearing any Hellknight armor.

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight-Errant](/Feats.aspx?ID=8817) or [Hellknight Signifer Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8819).

You've bolstered your force of will with the power of the Measure and the Chain. You've officially joined the ranks of Hellknight signifers, and you receive a signifer's mask, often devoid of eyeholes or other decorative features. The mask doesn't obscure your vision, though it makes it impossible for others to see your eyes. While wearing your signifer's mask, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394), and Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302). You gain expert proficiency rank in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (or in another skill in which you're trained of your choice, if you were already an expert in Intimidation), as well as in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46).

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight-Errant](/Feats.aspx?ID=8817) or [Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818).

You likely take on an adventuring life with a group of like-minded individuals who aren't Hellknights. The resistance to mental damage you gained from the Hellknight Dedication feat increases to 5 + your number of archetype class feats from the Hellknight archetype.

 You also gain the Warding Shift action, which allows you to keep your allies from harm.

 **Warding Shift** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Requirements** You're adjacent to a willing ally; **Effect** You move the adjacent willing ally 5 feet in any direction and can Step into the space the ally vacated.

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818) or [Hellknight Signifer Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8819).

---

Your Hellknight training gives you the ability to focus your senses and root out those who would attempt to deceive or hide from you. For 1 minute, you gain a +2 status bonus to your Perception DC against attempts to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387), [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) you, or [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) to you. During this time, if you [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) to locate a [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) creature or to see through a creature's [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) attempt, you gain a +2 status bonus to the Perception check.

A frightened creature is in your melee reach

---

Your offense exploits your enemy’s fear. Make a melee Strike against a frightened creature. If you hit and deal damage, the target becomes off-guard until its frightened condition ends. If the target was already off-guard to you when you damaged it with this Strike, it can’t reduce its frightened value below 1 until the start of your next turn.

You don’t lose spells easily. If a reaction would disrupt your spellcasting action, attempt a DC 15 flat check. If you succeed, your action isn’t disrupted.

You call upon the power of law against a foe who would dare stand against you. Make a weapon or unarmed Strike against the target. This counts as two Strikes for your multiple attack penalty. The Strike deals one extra weapon damage die and 1d8 spirit damage. At 18th level, this spirit damage increases to 2d8.

You can channel your mask's power to pierce through lies and see the truth in any situation. You learn the [_glimpse the truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1843) focus spell. This has the same tradition trait as the spellcasting class feature used as a prerequisite for Hellknight Signifer Preferment. You gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point if you don't already have a focus pool or increase your focus pool by 1 (to a maximum of 3). You can [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) by studying tomes of law or by contemplating the Measure and the Chain.

The magic flowing through your signifer's mask allows you to see in the dark, and the mask dampens the distraction caused by sudden flashes of bright light. While wearing your signifer's mask, you gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415); if you already have darkvision, you instead gain greater darkvision. Additionally, if you're [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) while wearing your signifer's mask and the target is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) only because you're dazzled, you reduce the flat check DC to target that creature from 5 to 3.

---

Though you might not worship [Asmodeus](/Deities.aspx?ID=278) or other devils, you've studied enough of Hell to call forth a brief burst of its fire. Each creature in a 15-foot burst within 120 feet takes 9d6 fire damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your spell DC. This fire damage ignores an amount of fire resistance equal to your level, but not immunity to fire. A creature that fails its save also has its soul set aflame, taking 2d6 [persistent spirit damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) (or 4d6 persistent spirit damage on a critical failure). At 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the initial fire damage increases by 2d6.

>

</title>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />

[Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818); expert in at least one of your [order's favored weapons](HellknightOrders.aspx)

</column>

---

You've trained relentlessly with your order's weapon to maximize their deadliness. When you get a critical success on a Strike with one of your order's favored weapons, the target must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC. If you have access to that weapon's [critical specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203), you must choose whether to use that effect or this one.

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.<br />
**Success** The target takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until the end of your next turn.<br />
**Failure** As success, and the target is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) until the end of your next turn.<br />
**Critical Failure** As success, and the target is slowed 2 until the end of your next turn.

You gain the lesser order benefit of a Hellknight order other than the one to which you belong. This represents your time spent training with members of that order to learn their techniques and teachings. If you aren't in good standing with a given order, you can't receive their training.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, gaining the lesser order benefit from a different order each time by training with members of that order.

When faced with lawbreakers, you become almost unstoppable, and your purposeful steps instill terror. Stride toward the required target with a +10-foot status bonus to your Speeds and ignoring [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=451). If you end your movement adjacent to the required target, each enemy adjacent to you who saw your movement becomes [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). You can use March of Law while Burrowing, Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

You release the magic within your mask in an invisible burst, allowing it to temporarily flow into your allies' minds. Each of your allies within a 30-foot emanation gains the benefits of Signifer's Sight for 1 minute, as if they were wearing a signifer's mask.

The flames of your magic mark a target as an enemy of order. If your next action is to Cast a non-cantrip Spell that deals fire damage, that spell brands the target with a mark only you can see if it fails its saving throw. This brand lasts for 1 week. For as long as the target is branded, you always know the general direction and approximate distance of the target's current location, as long as it's on the same plane. You also know the direction the branded target is currently moving, if any, as well as any conditions affecting it. You can have only one brand active at a time.

Your attacks force a foe to glimpse the iron, soul-wrenching landscapes of [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=42). Strike an enemy with the required weapon twice. If either Strike hits, the target is [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) and can't use reactions until the beginning of your next turn. If both Strikes hit, the target is stupefied 3 instead.

---

<a id="archetype-252"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=252)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 202

The plants around you can provide more remedies than the finest hospital or temple, and you are skilled in their use. Nature always provides to those who know how to look, and you have always had a talent for seeing these gifts before you. You can put it to good use, healing those around you with nothing more than what the world provides.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Herbalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6339) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 202

**Archetype** [Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=252)

**Prerequisites**
[Natural Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=5182); Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

You can create natural remedies. You gain the [advanced alchemy benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=3282). You can use advanced alchemy to create 4 [alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528) [consumables](/Traits.aspx?ID=564) with the [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) trait, though the number is reduced by 2 if you didn’t make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575) in the wilderness. These consumables are called your herbal items. You remember herbal item [formulas](/Rules.aspx?ID=2214) and don’t need a [formula book](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2724) for them.

You become an expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) and can use Nature instead of [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) alchemical consumables with the healing trait. You don’t need to be trained in Crafting to do so, and you can use [healer’s tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727) instead of [alchemist’s tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702).

<title level="2">Herbalist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Advanced Herbalism](/Feats.aspx?ID=6342), [Endemic Herbs](/Feats.aspx?ID=6343), [Fresh Ingredients](/Feats.aspx?ID=6340), [Poultice Preparation](/Feats.aspx?ID=6341)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fresh Ingredients](/Feats.aspx?ID=6340) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 202

**Archetype** [Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=252)

**Prerequisites**
[Herbalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6339)

</column>

---

It is amazing the difference fresh herbs can make. When using [Natural Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=5182) to [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399), you gain the +2 circumstance bonus from having fresh ingredients, even if not in wilderness. If you do this in the wilderness, you gain a +4 circumstance bonus instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Poultice Preparation](/Feats.aspx?ID=6341) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 202

**Archetype** [Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=252)

**Prerequisites**
[Herbalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6339)

</column>

---

When you create an [elixir](/Traits.aspx?ID=589) as an herbal item, you can prepare it as a poultice instead. A poultice gains the [oil](/Traits.aspx?ID=663) trait (but remains [alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528), not [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) and loses the elixir trait. You can apply a poultice by [Interacting](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) with one hand. When you apply a poultice, in addition to the item’s normal effects, the recipient can attempt an immediate flat check to recover from a single source of [persistent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) acid, bleed, or fire damage, with the DC reduction from appropriate assistance.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Advanced Herbalism](/Feats.aspx?ID=6342) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 202

**Archetype** [Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=252)

**Prerequisites**
[Herbalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6339); Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

Your herbalist talents continue to grow with use and you have become potent at making even more remedies from less. You can create up to 6 herbal items per day with advanced alchemy.

**Special** At 10th level or higher, you can select this feat a second time to increase the number to 8.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Endemic Herbs](/Feats.aspx?ID=6343) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Additive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=795" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 202

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) For Pathfinder Society play, Endemic Herbs does not have the additive trait._

**Archetype** [Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=252)

**Prerequisites**
[Herbalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6339); Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49)

</column>

---

The herbal items you create use medicinal plants endemic to your location. When a creature consumes one of your herbal items, that creature gains the benefit matching the location where you created that item. If the benefit is not immediate, it lasts for 1 minute unless otherwise stated. 
<ul><li>**Aquatic** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves.</li><li>**Arctic** For 1 hour, treat [environmental cold effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2769) as if they were one step less severe.</li><li>**Desert** For 1 hour, treat environmental heat effects as if they were one step less severe.</li><li>**Forest** Gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) and [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) effects.</li><li>**Mountain** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saves.</li><li>**Plains** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves.</li><li>**Swamp** Remove one source of [persistent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) bleed damage.</li><li>**Underground** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298).</li></ul>

---

<a id="archetype-63"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Horizon Walker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=63)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 177

Many long for the open road, but you prefer the trackless wild. You can find safe passage through the most inhospitable terrain in the world—icecaps, deserts, and similar environs are where you're comfortable. Your talents open untrod paths for you and help guide others through the wilderness.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Additional Feats</title>

This archetype has some feats at a level other than their original level.
Such feats are marked with a \*.

[Click here for the full rules on Additional Feats](/Rules.aspx?ID=1432).

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Horizon Walker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1987) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You've mastered travel within a specific type of terrain. You gain the [Favored Terrain](/Feats.aspx?ID=495) feat. When in your favored terrain, you gain a +10-foot circumstance bonus to your travel Speed. When other creatures [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) with you as a guide in your favored terrain, they gain both the ability to ignore non-magical difficult terrain for the purpose of their travel Speed and the bonus to travel Speed.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the horizon walker archetype.

<title level="2">Horizon Walker Dedication leads to...</title>
[Acclimatization](/Feats.aspx?ID=1988), [Magical Adaptation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1991), [Perpetual Scout](/Feats.aspx?ID=1990), [Rebel's Map](/Feats.aspx?ID=4135), [Sure Foot](/Feats.aspx?ID=1989), [Wild Strider](/Feats.aspx?ID=1992)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Acclimatization](/Feats.aspx?ID=1988) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 177

**Archetype** [Horizon Walker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=63)

**Prerequisites**
[Horizon Walker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1987)

</column>

Your time spent in the hostile parts of the world has inured you to extreme climates. In your favored terrain, you gain resistance equal to half your level to all [environmental damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) and are affected by temperature effects as though they were one step less severe (incredible heat or cold becomes extreme, extreme heat or cold becomes severe, and so on). When other creatures [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) with you as a guide in your favored terrain, they too treat temperature effects as one step less severe.

Rebellions require an intricate knowledge of one's surroundings—because you might need to escape at any moment. You remember the locations of escape routes, ambush spots, and cover from a scouting expedition or a previous visit to the area. Roll a d20. At any point during the subsequent combat, you can substitute the result of this roll instead of rolling a d20 on one [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=45) or on one [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62).

 While you're adjacent to an [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) creature of your level or lower, it is instead only hidden from you.

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Iridian Choirmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=328)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 62

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) A character who takes the Iridian Choirmaster archetype must choose another character as their student. Note this character by Organized Play ID and character number in their records._

When the Iridian Fold disbanded, a splinter sect of this philosophical group called the Iridian Choir, which originated within the city of Ular Kel in Casmaron, rose to prominence in Kaer Maga. You are a member of this school of ideology and martial prowess, seeking another to form a bonded pair called a szerik. Together, you practice moving, fighting, and even speaking in complete harmony so that your souls may unite into one, a single spirit in two bodies. While this relationship can be quite intimate, the Iridian Choir believes any type of bond can bring a szerik to the true enlightenment known as “shared mind, shared heart,” whether it be romantic or platonic.

You’ve chosen a student to train in the Iridian Choir’s philosophy, which teaches that two people battling together are greater than the sum of their parts. You and your student share a deep connection, the nature of which is up to the two of you. As a symbol of your bond, you might each wear small, identical chains somewhere on your body. You and your student spend a lot of time practicing, seeking to achieve that perfect blending of souls to lead to enlightenment.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

---

When you take this dedication, choose one willing, non-minion ally to be your student in the ways of the Iridian Choir. As part  of your training in this archetype, you teach your student the necessary mindset and techniques; they gain the benefits of  your abilities without having to take any feats of their own. You gain the benefits of your Iridian Choirmaster archetype feats only if both you and your student are alive and conscious.  <br />You and your student can trade nonverbal messages as  a single action, which have the effects of the [_message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1598) spell but are non-magical. This requires a single action, has the  [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), and [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642) traits, and requires that  you be able to see each other.  

If your student dies, or if you and your student choose to part ways, you can choose and develop a new student by spending 1 week of downtime training another willing, non minion ally.

---

Your thoughts and dreams are your student's thoughts and dreams, and vice versa. You develop a permanent mental  connection, allowing you to communicate telepathically as long as you're on the same plane. When one of you fails a save against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, the other can choose to take the results of the failed save instead. If both of you are targeted by the same mental effect requiring a saving throw, you and your student take the better of each of your die rolls for the save. You each still add your own save modifier to the die result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect.

You become trained in either [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11); if you were already trained in both these skills, you become an expert in one of them instead. You gain either the [Ki Rush](/Feats.aspx?ID=432) or [Ki Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=433) monk feat, which grants you a ki spell and a focus pool of 1 Focus Point that you can recover using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity as a [monk](/Classes.aspx?ID=8) does. If you already have both feats, you can instead choose a single 1st-level [monk feat](/Feats.aspx?Traits=112).

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you gain two other feats from the Jalmeri Heavenseeker or [Student of Perfection](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=18) archetypes.

Until the end of your next turn, your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks and any [monk](/Traits.aspx?ID=112) weapons you wield deal additional electricity and sonic damage; the amount of each damage type is equal to the number of damage dice for the weapon or unarmed attack. Any creature who successfully [Grapples](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) you or is successfully Grappled by you takes this damage immediately after the Grapple check is resolved (using the number of damage dice of your unarmed attack to determine the damage dealt).

 If you also know the [_ki blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=484) ki spell, you can choose to deal either electricity or sonic damage with the spell instead of force while this effect is active (_ki blast_ loses the [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) trait and gains the [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147) trait instead).

Your jagged blows are like lightning. The only Strikes you can make are skyward slash unarmed attacks. These unarmed attacks deal 1d10 slashing damage; are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group; and have the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199), and [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200) traits. While in Sky and Heaven Stance, you gain resistance 2 to electricity and resistance 2 to sonic damage. These resistances increase to 5 at 12th level and to 8 at 18th level.

You [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81) toward an opponent. At any point in the Leap, you can make a single Strike against a creature within your reach. At 12th level, if you hit with this Strike, instead of finishing your Leap, you can immediately attempt a second Leap from the space where you struck the target of your Strike. You can make a single Strike against a target within your reach during this second Leap as well. At 16th level, you can attempt a third Leap if your second Strike hits, and you can attack a target at any point during this third Leap. All Leaps made during this activity gain a +10-foot status bonus to the total height or distance of your leap, and no two Strikes can target the same creature.

You Stride up to your Speed, and your ki enshrouds your limbs in terrifying stormy energy, increasing the [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) of your Sky and Heaven Stance [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks by 5 feet. At the end of your movement, make up to three Strikes against a target you can reach, each at a –2 penalty. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after you've made all your attacks. Instead of the usual slashing or piercing damage, the damage for these Strikes is either electricity or sonic, as you choose with each Strike. If you successfully hit with all three Strikes, the target is [drained 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10).

**Source** [Pathfinder #158: Sixty Feet Under](/Sources.aspx?ID=47) pg. 78, [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 224

Certain martial artists dedicate themselves to fighting in Jalmeray's Challenge of Sky and Heaven; these individuals devote themselves to the esoteric mysteries of the sky and incorporate these lofty abilities into their martial arts maneuvers. You may have learned these skills from the Houses of Perfection in Jalmeray, or from a practitioner of this style who left Jalmeray bearing its secrets (such as Shristi Melipdra). The Houses of Perfection focus on honing elemental powers, but the Jalmeri heavenseeker isn't limited by the powers of air alone. This style's attacks emulate darting flashes of lightning and the crash of thunder from roiling storm clouds. A true practitioner masters control even over dense matter, causing the air to support its weight or bring it crashing down.

You gain either the [Ki Rush](/Feats.aspx?ID=432) or [Ki Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=433) monk feat, which grants you a ki spell and a focus pool of 1 Focus Point that you can recover using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) activity as a monk does. If you already have both these feats, you can instead choose a single 1st-level monk feat.

You [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) toward an opponent. At any point in the Leap, you can make a single Strike against a creature within your reach. At 12th level, if you hit with this Strike, instead of finishing your Leap, you can immediately attempt a second Leap from the space where you struck the target of your Strike. You can make a single Strike against a target within your reach during this second Leap as well. At 16th level, you can attempt a third Leap if your second Strike hits, and you can attack a target at any point during this third Leap. All Leaps made during this activity gain a +10-foot status bonus to the total height or distance of your leap, and no two Strikes can target the same creature.

 At the end of your movement, make up to three Strikes against a target you can reach, each at a –2 penalty. <a id="archetype-301"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Kitharodian Actor](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=301)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
</traits>

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 58

Some performers at Kitharodian Academy are so dedicated to method acting that they can completely disappear into roles in a manner that’s almost magical. These thespians are capable of mimicking Taldor’s vast array of stage-immortalized luminaries via vivid impressions, awe-inspiring vocal performances, and wild stunts that defy all expectations. The Academy’s foremost instructors and senior Lion Blades agents keep a close eye on all prodigies who show a sliver of this potential, helping them harness their talents for use in both the acting world and the world of spycraft.

 Through Taldor’s long history, a handful of classic roles have been repeated and hammered into shape until they became icons and metaphors that define the art of Taldor. Although some of these are symbols of national strength, like First Emperor Taldaris, many are tragic or even comedic figures like Emperor Beldam I. Accepting any one of these roles in a high-profile production can be the highlight of an actor’s career, but the best of the best gather these roles like trophies.

 Newer roles are added to the canon very slowly, with modern figures like Grand Princess Eutropia usually alluded to with references from other roles. Many performances with Cyricas and his animal friends now feature a dog at his side, for example, as a reference to the grand princess’s beloved pet.

 Although the most famous internationally, Kitharodian Academy is not the sole repository of Taldor’s stories. Many other schools in Taldor, like the nearby Rhapsodic College, teach the classics. But these plays and songs are such a deeply rooted part of Taldor’s culture that prodigies arise from the soldiers of Zimar to the dwarven enclaves in Maheto.

</column>

</column>

You’ve studied classic Taldan theater and learned to embody various roles to a sublime degree. You become trained in Society and in Theater Lore; if you were already trained in either, you become an expert in that skill instead. In addition, when you attempt a Deception or Performance check to portray a famous figure, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check. This bonus changes to +3 at 10th level and +4 at 17th level. However, you don’t gain this bonus while [Impersonating](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) a figure whose death is common knowledge (as determined by the GM).

You become trained in Nature and a Lore skill related to a particular type of animal commonly used in show business (such as Canine Lore, Ursine Lore, or Primate Lore); if you were already trained in either, you become an expert in that skill instead. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all checks to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) and [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures with the animal trait. You can use your chosen animal Lore to Command an Animal of that type.

You’ve watched dozens of morbid comedies depicting Beldam I, Taldor’s prankster emperor whose wife accidentally killed him when she struck him with a marble bust after he jumped out from behind curtains to frighten her. You are reminded of this depressing yet perversely comical tale whenever you are near death, and in your final moments of consciousness you murmur a bleak joke to the creature who reduced you to 0 Hit Points. The creature must attempt a Will save against your class DC. 

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.<br />
**Success** The target is distracted by giggles and can’t use reactions until the beginning of your next turn.<br />
**Failure** The target laughs uncontrollably. It can’t use reactions until the beginning of your next turn and is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1.<br />
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the target also immediately falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

You portrayed Grand Prince Stavian III in _Fall of the Troubled King_, a production dedicated to the life and times of the paranoid Taldan ruler whose violent resistance to new policies on succession kicked off the War for the Crown. Your acting won rave reviews for recasting Stavian’s paranoia and political machinations in a sympathetic light, and you’ve learned to apply these subtle techniques outside of the stage to win others over. Whenever you succeed at a Deception or Performance check to portray a famous figure, you can select one creature within 60 feet who observed your performance. As long as this creature isn’t hostile, its attitude toward you automatically improves by two steps (three steps if your check was a critical success). If it’s hostile, it’s [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 2 for 1 minute as it tries to reconcile its desire to harm you with its newfound sympathy for you.

You were once cast in the role of Daronlyr XII, one of Taldor’s most ambitious rulers who slew his cousin to seize the crown, yet somehow still managed to convince the entire Ulfen Guard to swear loyalty to him simply through his powers of oration. You attempt a Performance check to launch into a powerful monologue, pulling lines from Daronlyr’s playbook to win respect from everyone around you, even your enemies. The DC of this check is a [hard difficulty DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2627) of your level. On a success, any hostile creatures within 20 feet take a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and spell attack rolls that target you until the beginning of your next turn, and any allies within 20 feet are quickened until the beginning of your next turn. The additional action can be only used to Strike or Stride.

<title level="1" right="Archetype 6" pfs="Standard">[Knight Reclaimant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=28)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 95

Knights reclaimant spend much of their time amid the horrors of the Gravelands, rescuing civilians that remain and striking back against the Whispering Tyrant’s agents. Accomplishing these goals requires the adoption of subtle tactics, with a focus on stealth and survival.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Knights of Lastwall Archetypes</title>

The following archetypes are uncommon but are available to members of the Knights of Lastwall. Qualifying characters with the [Lastwall sentry](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=15) archetype can select one of these dedications even without gaining three feats from the Lastwall sentry archetype, and each of these archetypes’ feats fulfills the [Lastwall Sentry Dedication’s](/Feats.aspx?ID=882) special requirement despite not being from the Lastwall sentry archetype.

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">The Crimson Oath</title>

_We swear with voices cold as death,<br /> While yet we stand and yet draw breath,<br /> We shall not let the dead endure,<br /> Nor let them taint our lands verdure,<br /> We shall not falter, shall not rout,<br /> But cut them down and burn them out,<br /> We swear on Vigil's shattered walls,<br /> Our Crimson Oath: The Tyrant falls!_
</aside>

<title level="3">Additional Feats</title>

This archetype has some feats at a level other than their original level.
Such feats are marked with a \*.

[Click here for the full rules on Additional Feats](/Rules.aspx?ID=1432).

>
[Knight Reclaimant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1097) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 95

**Archetype** [Knight Reclaimant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=28)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15); Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16); any non-evil alignment; member of the Knights of Lastwall of knight rank

**Access**
A character who is a member of the Knights of Lastwall has access to this option.

</column>

---

You have sworn the Crimson Oath and become a full member of the Crimson Reclaimers. You gain expert proficiency in Stealth and Survival. Whenever you roll a success on a saving throw against an undead’s special ability, you get a critical success instead. This applies to any abilities that come from being undead, including an undead’s innate spells (but not its prepared or spontaneous spells).

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Knight Reclaimant archetype.

<title level="2">Knight Reclaimant Dedication leads to...</title>
[Ashen Veil](/Feats.aspx?ID=3589), [Blade of the Crimson Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=1101), [Crimson Oath Devotion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3595), [Cut them Down, Burn them Out](/Feats.aspx?ID=7748), [For Love, For Lightning](/Feats.aspx?ID=3592), [Hilt Hammer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3591), [Invoke the Crimson Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=1098), [Reaper of Repose](/Feats.aspx?ID=1100), [Reclaimant Plea](/Feats.aspx?ID=3593), [Shall Not Falter, Shall Not Rout](/Feats.aspx?ID=2168), [Shepherd of Desolation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3594), [Survivor of Desolation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1099), [The Tyrant Falls!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3596), [Voice Cold as Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3590)

---

By smearing ash or tainted earth over your skin and armor, you shroud yourself from the dead. You become concealed to [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) using vision or [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21), allowing you to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) without other sources of [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) or concealment. This effect lasts only as long as you continue to take no actions other than to Hide, Sneak, or other surreptitious actions. The GM determines which actions end the effect, but attacking, casting spells, activating items, and the like always do.
