Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

**Requirements**
A rope is within your reach, or you have a [rope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=44) or [grappling](/Traits.aspx?ID=184) weapon in your hand.

</column>

---

The Salt Breakers learned to use whatever they could during the Vidric Revolution, and they quickly mastered the art of making a rope into a useful tool in combat. You take hold of a nearby rope, throw a rope from your hand, or fire a grappling weapon at a solid surface—and then swing up to twice your Speed. If you end your movement next to an enemy, attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) that enemy, tying them up in your rope.

---

<a id="archetype-120"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=120)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Guns &amp; Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 136

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with a Home Region of Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or the Shackles have access to this archetype_

You treat combat as an art and your pistol as an extension of your performance. You might wield a single pistol, a pair of pistols, or a pistol paired with a melee weapon to pull off showy maneuvers. However you slice it, though, the use of pistols or other one-handed firearms is crucial to your technique and style.

 To you, everything is a show, and you use your gun as a prop and instrument, not just to kill opponents but to trick, mislead, hinder, and even bully them into doing what you want them to do. While others tend to focus on delivering as much devastation downrange as possible, your style is all about control. By controlling a foe's attention and actions, you can bolster your own attacks and mitigate the foe's potential for mayhem. You control the tempo of the battle much as you would a staged performance, carefully ensuring your foe's actions don't fall outside of your intended script. You're both the director and the star of this show, and your enemies dance to the tune you play with your pistol... sometimes quite literally!

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">What Makes a Phenom?</title>

Many gunslingers can learn how to twirl a pistol or intimidate a foe, but it's not just your skills that make you a phenom, it's your style and attitude. As a pistol phenom, you understand how to grab everyone's attention with everything you do, especially the way you talk, the way you walk, and the way you use your gun. But what's more, you're well aware of that fact and the power you have over others, and you aren't afraid to flaunt it.

 Despite this attitude, or perhaps because of it, as a pistol phenom you likely tend to get along well with groups of allies, understanding both how to take the spotlight to protect your allies and how to share it to make sure they get their time in the sun. The one exception to this can be other pistol phenoms. When two or more pistol phenoms gather in the same group, it's almost inevitable for a duel or other contest to arise. However, such a contest need not end in enmity. Depending on your temperament, and that of the other pistol phenom, the result of the exhilarating rivalry expressed during competition could be a lifelong friendship, albeit one in which you both keep score of your greatest achievements to compare exploits.
</aside>

You gain the [Pistol Twirl](/Feats.aspx?ID=3162) gunslinger feat, enabling you to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) against creatures within your weapon's first range increment. This otherwise serves as Pistol Twirl for the purpose of meeting prerequisites, although as normal, it doesn't count as another pistol phenom feat for the purpose of meeting Pistol Phenom Dedication's special entry and taking another archetype. Whenever you Feint with a one-handed firearm, you can choose to attempt a Performance check instead of a Deception check.

Either of these benefits is lost if not used by the end of your next turn.

You shoot not at your foe but at an object nearby. Make a Strike with your firearm against an AC equal to an easy DC for your level. On a success, instead of hitting your foe, your attack hits an object behind or to the side of your target, creating one of the following effects. The GM might determine that a different AC is appropriate or that a particular effect isn't a valid option, such as using the explosive barrel option when there's no such object on the battlefield. The GM should inform you if a Trick Shot is feasible before you spend your actions, since your trained eye can easily recognize loose or volatile objects. 
<ul><li>**Dislodge Object** Your attack knocks an unattended object of no more than 2 Bulk out of position, moving it up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice. For example, the weapon could knock a wizard's crystal ball off a table.</li><li>**Explosive Barrel** Your attack strikes a barrel of expensive rum, a vial of volatile alchemical fluids, a demonic pustule erupting from the earth, or some other explosive object. The object explodes in a 20-foot burst, and creatures in the area take 6d6 damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. The damage type is chosen by the GM, based on the exploding object. Increase the damage by 1d6 for every 2 levels you have above 10th.</li></ul>

You fire your gun while throwing off a target's balance with your melee weapon. Then, you topple your foe to the ground with the quick orchestrated combination. You don't need to use brute force to do so, or even necessarily to hit with your gunshot; the effect is all about performing perfectly and eliminating your target's movements and options, leaving them no choice but to fall.

 Make a ranged firearm Strike against a creature within the reach of your melee weapon and then attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check against the creature's Reflex DC. If the Strike critically succeeds, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its Reflex DC against this check. The Performance check has the following effects.

**Critical Success** The target falls and lands [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). It takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.<br />
**Success** The target falls and lands prone.<br />
**Critical Failure** Your plans backfired on you, and you're forced to drop your melee weapon in your space.

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Poisoner](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=259)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 210

People are so delightfully fragile when exposed to the insidious power of nature. The bite of a certain serpent makes the blood congeal to jelly. A particular stone, suitably powdered, induces powerful hallucinations and delirium. The sap of a rare tree inflicts such agony that death seems preferable. The deadly medicines of nature have been molded to create concoctions capable of both killing and debilitating. Neither option is pleasant for the unfortunate recipient. You are a student of such dark wonders, making you a dangerous foe indeed.

</column>

</column>

You can capably deliver toxins with a [blowgun](/Weapons.aspx?ID=424). Your blowgun [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) can apply [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=635) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) even if they deal no damage due to a creature's resistance. If you critically succeed at a blowgun Strike using a poisoned dart, the target's initial save against the poison is one degree of success worse than the creature rolls; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.

 In addition, if you make a blowgun Strike while [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96), you don't automatically become [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=84). Instead, immediately attempt a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) check against the Perception DC of the target. If you succeed, you don't become observed, and are hidden (if you were undetected, you still become hidden rather than remaining undetected).

In nature, certain animals are covered in venomous spines, and just brushing against them can prove deadly. You expend a [contact](/Traits.aspx?ID=565) or [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=635) poison and spend 10 minutes brushing that poison onto your clothing or weaving sharp, poisoned needles into the garment's fabric. You can have only one poison suffused into your clothing at a time. You can use the Once Bitten reaction while you have a poison suffused in this way.

**Once Bitten** <actions string="Reaction" />A creature adjacent to you hits you with a melee unarmed [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306); **Requirements** You have prepared your clothing to poison attackers; **Effect** The triggering creature is exposed to the suffused poison, and the poison becomes inert.

You apply a contact poison or injury poison to the required weapon; if you have a free hand, you can Interact to draw a poison as part of this action. This poison can be one of the simple injury poisons you can create due to this feat (see Special), or another contact or injury poison you’ve acquired (such as those in GM Core).

**Special** During your daily preparations, you can prepare a number of simple injury poisons equal to your level. These follow the rules for injury poisons (GM Core, page 248), except that they deal 1d4 poison damage with no saving throw. Only you can apply these poisons properly, and they expire the next time you prepare.

</column>

---

Your victims tend to expire long before your poisons, since the latter have been specifically formulated to last longer. The maximum duration of any poison you create increases by an amount equal to the poison's stage 1 interval, to a maximum of twice the poison's maximum duration.

    pfs="Standard"

[Poisoner Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6382)

**Trigger**
You fail a save against a poison.

</column>

---

A small amount of poison taken at nonlethal doses, can help the body build up resistance against a more deadly dosage. Reroll the triggering check and use the second result. Once you use Acquired Tolerance, you can continue to use it against the same type of poison that day, but you can't use it against a different type of poison until after you make your next daily preparations. For instance, if you used the reaction on a save against [giant scorpion venom](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3335), you could use it again against giant scorpion venom even if it came from a different source, but you couldn't use it against [wyvern poison](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3350).

</column>

---

A combination of additional viscosity and careful application keeps your weapons poisoned even when suffering significant wear and tear. If your Strike with a poisoned weapon would expend its poison without your target attempting an initial save (due to [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) or your Strike being a critical failure, for example), attempt a DC 5 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). On a success, your weapon remains poisoned. If your Strike with a poisoned weapon succeeds, attempt a DC 17 flat check. On a success, your weapon remains poisoned until the end of your next turn.

You deliver poisons in ways that maximize their harmful effects. When you apply a simple poison with Poison Weapon, the poison deals 2d4 poison damage instead of 1d4 poison damage. You don’t waste a poison you apply with Poison Weapon on a critically failed attack roll.

When you successfully Strike an [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) creature with a poisoned weapon or expose an off-guard creature to an [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=634) poison, that creature takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its initial save against that poison.

<a id="archetype-315"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Prophet of Kalistrade](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=315)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 74

You’ve dedicated your life to the teachings of [Kalistrade](/Deities.aspx?ID=23), a mystic whose writings promise success through a restrictive set of practices. When you joined the Prophets of Kalistrade, you agreed to abide by the edicts of its eponymous founder. You follow a diet that prizes certain virtuous foods and avoids impure sustenance. You frequently meditate to keep yourself sharp. You value finding clever loopholes and making good deals as long as you don’t ruin another’s fortune entirely. 

Dedicating yourself to Kalistocratic ways opened many doors when it comes to business connections and entrepreneurial knowledge. Like any good Kalistocrat, you turn one advantage into a stepping stone toward the next. Between your connections, your social skills, and (of course) your wealth, it’s hard to get one over on you.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Additional Feats</title>

This archetype has some feats at a level other than their original level.
Such feats are marked with a \*.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 74

**Archetype** [Prophet of Kalistrade](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=315)

**Prerequisites**
trained in [Mercantile Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41); Trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47); Charisma +2

**Access**
You’re from Druma.

</column>

---

After induction into the ranks of the Kalistocrats, you learned the skills necessary to succeed in business and rise above others by following a set of detailed strictures. Unless you take measures to hide your affiliation, anyone who has heard of the [Prophets of Kalistrade](/Deities.aspx?ID=23) will know you’re one of them when they see you. You become an expert in Society and can use Society instead of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on merchants and traders. 

Additionally, if you don’t already cast spells from spell slots, you learn to cast [spontaneous spells](/Rules.aspx?ID=2224) and gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) cantrips, plus either [_prestidigitation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1639) or [_read aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1646). You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for these spells is Charisma, and they’re occult spells.

<title level="2">Prophet of Kalistrade Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Prophet Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=7681), [Fortune's Favor](/Feats.aspx?ID=7683), [Master Merchant](/Feats.aspx?ID=7687), [Prophet's Lockbox](/Feats.aspx?ID=7685), [Smile at Failure](/Feats.aspx?ID=7682)

Your time gossiping in fashionable salons keeps you informed on every topic. You are trained in Gossip Lore, a special Lore skill that can be used only to [Recall Knowledge](/Skills.aspx?General=true&amp;ID=24), but on any topic. If you fail a check to Recall Knowledge with Gossip Lore, you get the effects of the [Dubious Knowledge](/Feats.aspx?ID=5142) skill feat. If you have legendary proficiency in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47), you gain expert proficiency in Gossip Lore, but you can’t increase your proficiency rank in Gossip Lore by any other means.

When a creature you’re interacting with decreases its attitude from [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=82) to [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=97) or from unfriendly to [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=80), you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to any attempts to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on the creature for the next hour. If this decrease in attitude leads to combat, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the subsequent initiative roll instead.

The mental landscape of the psychic duel rises to meet your steps and reshapes at your touch. Shattered minds and broken wills from your previous duels exhibit your prowess. You understand that the binary mindscape of a duel links two minds, making its foundation only as strong as the wills of those involved. Two psychic castles in a siege—patch every loose brick in your walls and single out every flaw in your foe's defenses.

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Psychic Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=350)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44); you have been in a [psychic duel](/Rules.aspx?ID=3514)

</column>

---

Through experience and in-depth visualizations of mental battles, you've grown adept at psychic duels. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your initiative rolls for psychic duels. Each time you enter a psychic duel, choose one of the following benefits for the duration of that duel. 
<ul><li>**Mind Mace** You gain a status bonus to mental damage with spells you cast equal to the spell's rank.</li><li>**Psychic Fist** You can use your standard attribute modifier for Strike damage instead of your highest mental modifier, and you can use your full AC instead of using your Will DC in place of your AC.</li></ul>

<title level="2">Psychic Duelist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Duel Spell Advantage](/Feats.aspx?ID=8501), [Instigate Psychic Duel](/Feats.aspx?ID=8503), [Supreme Psychic Center](/Feats.aspx?ID=8502)

When you start a psychic duel, you gain a third natural psychic spell. You can't choose the same spell twice.

 If you're 9th level or higher, add the following spells to the list of natural psychic spells you can choose: [_confusion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1471), [_hallucination_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1551), [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1693), [_synaptic pulse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1710), [_synesthesia_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2035), and [_wave of despair_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1757).

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archives (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 203

**Archetype** [Psychic Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=350)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Psychic Duelist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8500)

</column>

---

You attempt to enter a psychic duel with a creature within 100 feet. The target can attempt a Will save against the higher of your spell DC or class DC. If it enters the duel willingly, use the result for a critical failure.

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.<br />
**Success** The two of you enter a [psychic duel](/Rules.aspx?ID=3514), but it ends automatically at the end of your next turn. As normal for a psychic duel, the duel ends if one participant is knocked out, as well as under any other conditions to which both participants agree. If you're in initiative when you Instigate the Psychic Duel, you keep the same initiative positions. You can each choose a psychic center for any skill in which you're trained, as you would if you were using that skill to roll initiative for the duel.<br />
**Failure** As a success, except instead of ending at the end of your next turn, the target can attempt a new save to end the duel at the end of each of your turns, starting with your next turn.<br />
**Critical Failure** As a success, except the duel doesn't end until it reaches one of the normal end conditions for a psychic duel.

<a id="archetype-377"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 6" pfs="Standard">[Pure Legion Enforcer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=377)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
</traits>

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 60

Pure Legion enforcers stand against the encroachment of religion into Rahadoum. You sniff out illegal divine magic and take care of those who carry it into your country. To protect yourself and carry out your duties, you ward yourself against gods-given abilities. Outside of Rahadoum, you probably still find the divine to be distasteful but are not obliged to destroy it at all costs.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

This archetype has some feats at a level other than their original level.
Such feats are marked with a \*.

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 60

**Archetype** [Pure Legion Enforcer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=377)

**Prerequisites**
member of the Pure Legion

</column>

---

You are sworn to uphold the Laws of Mortality within the borders of Rahadoum. As part of your commissioning, you learned about the different types of worship and divine magic that you might encounter. You become trained in Intimidation and Religion. If you are already trained in one or both of these skills, you become an expert in that skill. If you are already an expert in both skills, you become trained in a skill of your choice.

 You also gain the Recognize Spell skill feat. Whenever you attempt to recognize a divine spell, you always learn it is divine and gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the Religion skill check. Finally, you gain the following edicts and anathema.

 Knowingly committing acts that violate the anathema result in you losing access to abilities granted by this archetype, as determined by your GM. You can regain these lost abilities by spending an appropriate amount of time rededicating yourself to the Pure Legion, typically by donating an amount equal to 20 gp × your level to appropriate causes and eschewing all divine magic (including spells cast by others) for at least 1 day.

 **Edicts** confiscate, contain, or destroy all divine objects in Rahadoum; drive out divine casters from Rahadoum<br /> **Anathema** use divine abilities, items, or spells; permit proselytizing of religion in Rahadoum; worship a deity

<title level="2">Pure Legion Enforcer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Edict of Mortality](/Feats.aspx?ID=8892), [Mortal Possibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=8900), [No Gods, Only Mortals!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8894), [Repelling Enforcer](/Feats.aspx?ID=8899), [Shake Off the Gods](/Feats.aspx?ID=8896), [Throttle the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=8897), [Traces of the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=8895), [Unassailable Enforcer](/Feats.aspx?ID=8893), [Wrath Against the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=8898)

    level="1"

[Godless Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=8888) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

You recover an additional 5 Hit Points from a successful attempt to Treat your Wounds or use Battle Medicine on you. After you or an ally use Battle Medicine on you, you become temporarily immune to that Battle Medicine for only 1 hour, instead of 1 day.

You grant greater healing when the gods don't interfere. When you roll a success to [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399) for a creature that hasn't regained Hit Points from divine magic in the past 24 hours, you get a critical success on your check instead and restore the corresponding amount of Hit Points.

---

You've learned the modern uses of Battle Medicine originated by Kassi Aziril. When you successfully use Battle Medicine, you can also reduce the target's [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), or [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) condition by 1 (this has no effect if you are subject to an effect continually applying the clumsy condition, like enlarge). If you are legendary in Medicine, you can choose to reduce the target's [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) condition by 1 instead, and if you have the [Godless Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=8888) feat, you can choose to reduce the target's [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) or [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition by 1 instead. If you have the [Mortal Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=8889) feat, you can reduce all available conditions by 1 for a target who hasn't benefited from [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) or [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) magic in the last 24 hours, and if you roll a critical success before applying the effects of the feat, you reduce all available conditions by 2 for that target instead.

You recite an excerpt of the Laws of Mortality, often the first law: “Let no mortal be beholden to a god.” Attempt an Intimidation check against all enemies within 60 feet that worship a deity, comparing your result against each target's Will DC. Targets are then temporarily immune to your use of this ability for 24 hours.

**Critical Success** The target becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2. Until the start of your next turn, if the target attempts to Cast a Spell with the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) trait, it must succeed at a DC 7 flat check or the action is lost.<br />
**Success** As critical success, but frightened 1, and the DC of the flat check is 5.

You channel your commitment to removing the divine from the world as you recite the Laws of Mortality. Strike a foe that can cast divine spells. The Strike deals two extra weapon damage dice. The target must also attempt a Will save against your class DC. On a failure, it loses its highest-rank available divine spell prepared or its highest unused spell slot to cast a divine spell. If it has multiple spells at its highest rank available, it randomly selects which spell is lost. On a critical failure, it also can't cast divine spells until the start of your next turn.

<a id="archetype-307"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 290

You are a Razmiran priest, initiated in the 31 Steps, the doctrines of [Razmir's](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) religion. You were trained at the Exalted Lodge or another of the temples where the priests specialize in crafting masks that also serve as Razmir's religious symbol, and you are charged with spreading and enforcing Razmir's faith. Razmiran priests are zealous worshippers of their god and use the magical techniques that they are taught to spread his word and his will. You have placed service to the Living God above all other duties and entrusted your wealth, prosperity, and ambitions to his teachings, while availing yourself of the knowledge and wisdom that only his most blessed servants are ever bestowed with, accepting the power and authority that is the right of the Living God's priests. Perhaps this is a pure zealousness, or perhaps you are motivated by Razmir's promises of wealth and authority. Either way, you have donned the mask and wield the power reserved for those who follow in Razmir's footsteps.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 290

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37); Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)

</column>

---

You have earned entry to the priesthood of Razmir, either at the Exalted Lodge or another temple where Razmir’s holy masks are forged. You gain a [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593) and can [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) a replacement in 4 hours if yours is ever damaged or lost. There is no value in selling your Razmiri mask, and only you gain its benefits. The abilities of your Razmiri mask use the higher of your class DC or spell DC.

You can take the [Cleric Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5066) feat without needing to meet its prerequisites and before you take two other feats from the Razmiran priest archetype, but you must choose [Razmir](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) as your deity. All spells granted by the cleric archetype when gained in this way are [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spells instead of [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells, and cleric feats that normally have the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) trait instead have the [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) trait. Your key spellcasting attribute for these spells is Charisma, rather than Wisdom.

<title level="2">Razmiran Priest Dedication leads to...</title>
[Living God](/Feats.aspx?ID=7570), [Mask of The 12th Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7568), [Mask of The 15th Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7569), [Perfect Truths](/Feats.aspx?ID=7567)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Perfect Truths](/Feats.aspx?ID=7567) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 290

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566)

</column>

---

Your knowledge of Razmir’s faith and doctrines has grown. You excel in debating priests of rival faiths, wielding truths as subtly and deftly as any charlatan might wield a lie. When you use [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389), you can carefully structure your deceits so that each individual statement you make is the truth, from a certain perspective. As long as you are wearing your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3592), you don’t take a penalty to Deception checks while subject to the [_ring of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1656) spell or similar effects. Whenever you are subject to _ring of truth_ or a similar effect, you can attempt a Deception check when you first begin speaking to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the spell’s effects, with a counteract rank equal to half your level (rounded up); succeeding at this check doesn’t end the spell or effect, but it does cause it to indicate that you are speaking the truth, even when you are actually lying, as you weave a web of words so delicate that even you can’t be certain where the truth ends and deception begins.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mask of The 12th Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7568) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 291

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566); Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)

</column>

---

You have reached the 12th Step and been instructed in greater secrets of [Razmir’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) doctrine. You can [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593) out of [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920) or upgrade your existing mask to a silver one in the same time it takes to Craft one made of iron . A silver Razmiri mask grants a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), is a 10th-level item, and gains the following activation in addition to that possessed by the standard mask.

**Activate—Call Upon Razmir’s Mercy** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** Exhorting Razmir to purge impurities from your target, you lay hands on a creature within reach and cast [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) as an [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell with a spell rank equal to half your level. Unlike a normal _cleanse affliction_ spell, this doesn’t reduce the stage of the affliction; instead, if the counteract check is successful, the [affliction’s](/Rules.aspx?ID=2389) stage is temporarily reduced by 1 and its effects are suppressed for 24 hours, after which the affliction resumes in full force. If the target would have been required to attempt additional saves against the affliction during the 24 hours it was suppressed, they must attempt all of those saving throws as soon as the 24-hour duration ends. This could mean that the target saves successfully and it is as if the affliction were truly healed, or it could mean that the affliction returns and advances multiple stages all at once.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mask of The 15th Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7569) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 291

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566); Master in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)

</column>

---

You have ascended to the 15th Step and stand among the greatest of [Razmir’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) priests. You can [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593) out of gold or upgrade your existing mask to a gold one in the same time it takes to Craft one made of iron. A gold Razmiri mask grants a +3 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), is a 14th-level item, and gains the following activation in addition to those possessed by the standard and silver masks. 

**Activate—Call Upon Razmir’s Wrath** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cry out to Razmir to reveal his fiery wrath, as he did upon the unbelievers at Melcat. You cast [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1707) as an 8th-rank [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell, but for [undead](/MonsterTemplates.aspx?ID=3) targets the spell has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Living God](/Feats.aspx?ID=7570) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 291

**Archetype** [Razmiran Priest](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=307)

**Prerequisites**
[Razmiran Priest Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7566); Legendary in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)

</column>

---

You have reached heights of power equaling [Razmir’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) himself. You can [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593)  out of porcelain laced with precious metals, or upgrade your existing mask to a porcelain one in the same time it takes to Craft one made of iron. A porcelain Razmiri mask grants a +4 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), is an 18th-level item, and is an apex item that increases your Charisma modifier by 1 or increases it to +4, whichever would give you a higher score. It also gives you the following activation in addition to those granted by the standard, silver, and gold masks.

**Activate—Power of the Living God** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You demand power from the world, using your mask as a locus to force reality to bend to your will. You cast [_manifestation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1592) as a 10th-rank [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell, but no matter what spell you emulate with it, that spell has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

---

<a id="archetype-175"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Limited">[Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 34

Most cultures revere the bodies of the deceased, laying to rest the mortal remains of their companions according to tradition formed generations before. Such customs assume a common conclusion: once the spirit that inhabited it has gone on to the Boneyard, the empty shell of a corpse has no purpose beyond its eventual return to the elements that formed it. You know differently. As the vessels that once housed immortal souls, corpses hold great power and potential, perfect construction materials for creations of unsurpassed wonder. As a reanimator, you have chosen to focus your study of the necromantic arts on the transformation of dead flesh into innumerable varieties of undead, from the lowliest shuffling corpses and brittle skeletons to abominations of ghastly splendor barely conceived of by only the most fanatical—or brilliant— mortal minds.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Additional Feats</title>

This archetype has some feats at a level other than their original level.
Such feats are marked with a \*.

[Click here for the full rules on Additional Feats](/Rules.aspx?ID=1432).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 34

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)

**Prerequisites**
able to cast [_animate dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=666) with a spell slot

</column>

---

You have dedicated your studies to the art of raising and commanding undead. If you're a spontaneous spellcaster with _animate dead_ in your repertoire, it becomes a signature spell in addition to your usual signature spells. If you're a prepared spellcaster with _animate dead_ in your spells known, spellbook, or the like, you can spend 10 minutes contemplating undeath to replace one of the spells you've prepared in your spell slots with an animate dead spell of the same level. In addition, if you're able to target the mostly intact remains of an appropriate type of dead creature when casting _animate dead_, the undead you animate gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, AC, saving throws, and skill checks for the duration of _animate dead_.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the reanimator archetype.

<title level="2">Reanimator Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bonds of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3489), [Deathly Secrets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3487), [Macabre Virtuoso](/Feats.aspx?ID=3488)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Undying Conviction](/Feats.aspx?ID=3483) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Aura" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=206" />
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />

<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 33

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175) (Level 4)

**Prerequisites**
able to create or control [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160); [cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) with a negative font, [oracle](/Classes.aspx?ID=14) of [bones](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=3), or [necromancer](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=7) [wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

Your presence has a bolstering effect on your undead [minions](/Traits.aspx?ID=109). Undead creatures under your control and within a 30-foot emanation around you gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws to resist [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128) damage and to Will saving throws to resist effects that would make them [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6).

**Special** This feat has the trait matching your spellcasting tradition.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Deathly Secrets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3487) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 34

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)

**Prerequisites**
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486)

</column>

---

No means of creating or ruling the undead is beyond your grasp, even those of magical traditions not your own. You learn either the [_eyes of the dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1104) or [_subjugate undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1106) focus spell. If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can Refocus by meditating over the earthly remains of a dead sentient creature. The rules for focus spells appear [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=276). Focus spells granted by the reanimator archetype are from the same tradition as those used to meet the archetype's prerequisite.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you learn a different spell and your focus pool increases by 1 Focus Point.

<title level="2">Deathly Secrets leads to...</title>
[Greater Deathly Secrets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3490), [Master of the Dead](/Feats.aspx?ID=3491)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Macabre Virtuoso](/Feats.aspx?ID=3488) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 34

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)

**Prerequisites**
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486); Expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

Any necromancer can create [zombie](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=103) and [skeleton](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=92), but you know the secrets behind the creation of far more advanced undead monstrosities. You learn the [_create undead_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=10) rituals to create two types of common [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) for which you meet the prerequisites. (Your GM might give you access to additional types of undead.) You can't teach these rituals to anyone else and you can't participate in either ritual while allowing someone else to serve as the primary caster unless they also know the ritual. When you reach a new level, you can change either or both of these rituals to a different type of undead for which you now meet the prerequisites.

 When acting as primary caster, you can perform all _create undead_ rituals in 4 hours instead of 1 day and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your primary check. You can also perform the ritual without the aid of a secondary caster, in which case you attempt the secondary check.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you learn the rituals to create two more types of undead creatures.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Bonds of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3489) <actions string="Free Action" />

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 35

once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486)

You have cast [_animate dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=666) this turn.

</column>

---

You sway with the motions of your spells that animate the dead, channeling your power to sustain two at the same time. You Sustain your previous casting of _animate dead_, binding the necromantic energy of the two spells together with metaphysical twine. On subsequent rounds, you can Sustain both _animate dead_ spells with a single action to Sustain the Spell. This benefit lasts until either of the spells ends.

Your undead secrets grow stronger still. You learn either the [_malignant sustenance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=432) or [_grasping grave_](/Spells.aspx?ID=512) focus spell. Your focus pool increases by 1 point.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you learn a different spell and your focus pool increases by 1 Focus Point.

You have reached the pinnacle of the reanimator's craft: the ability to raise nearly any corpse or skeleton as a gruesome mockery of the creature it once was. You learn the [_shambling horror_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1105) focus spell. Your focus pool increases by 1 Focus Point.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Necromancer's Visage](/Feats.aspx?ID=3484) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 33

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175) (Level 12)

**Prerequisites**
ability to create or control [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160); [cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) with a negative font, [oracle](/Classes.aspx?ID=14) of [bones](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=3), or [necromancer](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=7) [wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

Necromantic energy demonstrates your power over undead, creating a demeanor that commands their fear and respect. Undead creatures can immediately sense your Necromancer's Visage and tend to act accordingly. If you take a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against an undead creature, it becomes permanently immune to your Necromancer's Visage, and your Necromancer's Visage ends. You can spend 10 minutes to restore your Necromancer's Visage, though any creatures that became permanently immune remain so.

 Each time an undead creature 2 or more levels lower than you attacks you, it must attempt a Will save against your spell DC. If you're also affected by [_sanctuary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=266) or a similar effect, only one affects the attacker (you choose which).<br />

**Critical Success** The creature is permanently immune to your Necromancer's Visage.<br />
**Success** The creature can attempt its attack and any other attacks against you this turn.<br />
**Failure** The creature can't attack you and wastes the action. It can't attempt further attacks against you this turn.<br />
**Critical Failure** The creature wastes the action and can't attempt to attack you as long as your Necromancer's Visage persists.

**Special** This feat has the trait matching your spellcasting tradition.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sepulchral Sublimation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3485) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 33

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175) (Level 14)

**Prerequisites**
ability to create or control [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160); [cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) with a negative font, [oracle](/Classes.aspx?ID=14) of [bones](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=3), or [necromancer](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=7) [wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=12)

**Requirements**
You have at least one undead [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) that you permanently control.

</column>

---

You repurpose the negative energy that flows through your minions at a moment's notice. Instantly destroy one undead minion within 60 feet that is permanently under your control. If your next action is to cast a [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spell from a spell slot, you don't expend the slot. The spell's level must be half the destroyed minion's level or lower and the spell can't have a duration.

**Special** This feat has the trait matching your spellcasting tradition.

---

<a id="archetype-271"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Limited">[Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=271)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Prey for Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
</traits>

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 108

You are a Red Mantis assassin, inducted by [Achaekek](/Deities.aspx?ID=325), He Who, and sworn to chase your prey to the end of the world and beyond. While many Red Mantis assassins hail from the city of Ilizmagorti and regard it as their hometown, the Red Mantis has agents throughout the world, some of whom have yet to visit their so- called capital city. Still, those who have never been to Ilizmagorti eventually realize that they should at least pay a the city visit at some point in their lives.

 As a Red Mantis assassin, you'll periodically be asked to perform assassinations—but the organization is not without rules. The information presented on the previous page is important to understand if you choose to play a Red Mantis assassin as a result. This, plus the fact that the pursuit of murder-for-hire is generally seen as a criminal act that draws the interest of society's less-reputable and more sadistic members, means that this archetype may not be appropriate for all groups. More than most archetypes, this one requires the consent and permission of not just the GM, but of your fellow players. For an adventure like Prey for Death, though, this archetype can be considered to be unlocked for all who wish to join.

 The rare feats presented in the archetype are typically available only for assassins who have received permission from the Blood Mistress to undergo the appropriate training.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 108

**Archetype** [Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=271)

trained in [sawtooth sabers](/Weapons.aspx?ID=423); worshipper of [Achaekek](/Deities.aspx?ID=325); member of the Red Mantis assassins

**Access**
You are from Mediogalti Island.

</column>

---

You have learned how to stalk your foes and slay them with a sawtooth saber. You become trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) and [Assassin Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. Whenever your proficiency in any weapon increases to expert or beyond, you also gain that new proficiency with sawtooth sabers.

 You become bound by [Achaekek's](/Deities.aspx?ID=325) anathema and can receive his sanctification.

<title level="2">Red Mantis Assassin Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Red Mantis Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=6520), [Crimson Shroud](/Feats.aspx?ID=6521), [Prayer Attack](/Feats.aspx?ID=6528)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twin Feint](/Feats.aspx?ID=4921) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 170

**Archetype** [Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=271) (Level 2)

**Requirements**
You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand

</column>

---

You use an attack with one weapon to distract your foe from a second attack coming at a different angle. Make one Strike with each of your two melee weapons, both against the same target. The target is automatically off-guard against the second attack. Apply your multiple attack penalty to the Strikes normally.

<title level="2">Twin Feint leads to...</title>
[Twin Distraction](/Feats.aspx?ID=4939)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Basic Red Mantis Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=6520) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 108

**Archetype** [Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=271)

**Prerequisites**
[Red Mantis Assassin Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6519)

</column>

---

You have learned limited divine magic from your Red Mantis training. You gain the Cast a Spell activity. You can prepare two common cantrips each day from the divine spell list or any other divine cantrips you have access to. You also gain the basic [spellcasting benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2132). You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for the Red Mantis archetype spells is Charisma, and they are divine Red Mantis spells. If you gain a Focus Pool from any Red Mantis Assassin class feats, you can Refocus by praying to Achaekek or researching your assigned kill.

 You also have access to the [Red Mantis magic school](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=23). In addition to preparing spells from the divine spell list, you can prepare spells from this school. Regardless of their usual magic tradition, when you prepare spells from this school, they are divine spells, as are any Red Mantis focus spells you gain.

<title level="2">Basic Red Mantis Magic leads to...</title>
[Achaekek's Grip](/Feats.aspx?ID=6523), [Expert Red Mantis Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=6526), [Mantis Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6524), [Master Red Mantis Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=6529), [Red Mantis School Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=6522), [Vernai Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=6527)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"

If your Stealth check against the chosen foe succeeds, you can make a melee Strike against that foe at the end of your Sneak.

You swathe yourself in a veil of red mist for 1 minute. While the shroud is active, you gain fast healing equal to half your level. You can Interact with your shroud, swirling it around you, to gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the beginning of your next turn. Finally, if you die while the shroud is active, you can choose to have your entire body vanish into red mist, leaving behind only your gear; you make this choice when you activate Crimson Shroud.

 At 10th level, you can use this ability once per hour instead of once per day.

You apply a contact poison or injury poison to the required weapon; if you have a free hand, you can Interact to draw a poison as part of this action. This poison can be one of the simple injury poisons you can create due to this feat (see Special), or another contact or injury poison you’ve acquired (such as those in GM Core).

**Special** During your daily preparations, you can prepare a number of simple injury poisons equal to your level. These follow the rules for injury poisons (GM Core, page 248), except that they deal 1d4 poison damage with no saving throw. Only you can apply these poisons properly, and they expire the next time you prepare.

<title level="1" right="Archetype 4" pfs="Standard">[Ritualist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=260)</title>

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 211

While some learn the art of ritual casting through rigorous study, other gifted individuals may find that a combination of natural talent and luck grants them surprising skill at performing rituals, whether they want that power or not. Undertaking rituals always carries an element of risk, but the potential rewards are undeniable and difficult to resist. You have learned how to perform rituals and can decide how to best use their powerful benefits.

</column>

You have begun to master the difficult art of casting [rituals](Rituals.aspx). You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all checks to perform a ritual. You learn two [uncommon](/Traits.aspx?ID=721) rituals of 2nd rank or lower. You must meet all prerequisites to be the primary caster of a ritual to select it, and you can't teach it to anyone else or allow someone else to serve as primary caster unless they know the ritual as well. <br />At 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter, you learn two more rituals with the same restrictions and with a maximum rank of half that level.

You can't replace a secondary caster who is the target of the spell (as in the [_atone_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=108) ritual).

Elegant and expensive components are no replacement for your skill and practice at [ritual](Rituals.aspx) casting. If a ritual has a Cost entry that has a value in gp, reduce the amount you need to spend by 10%. If you critically succeed at the primary check for a ritual, the gp value of components the ritual consumes is reduced by the same amount. For example, using [_resurrect_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=123) to bring back a 14th-level creature normally costs 1,050 gp, but would cost you only 945 gp; and if you critically succeeded at the primary [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) check, you would spend only 840 gp.

<a id="archetype-308"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Rivethun Emissary](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=308)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 292

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Rivethun is a philosophy which characters may choose as their religion. Doing so fulfills the “follower of Rivethun” access condition for relevant options._

Rivethun emissaries form bonds with external spirits, using their own spiritual power as an anchor. This is a diplomatic endeavor, not a sycophantic one; they form mutual alliances and bonds of friendship and respect, they don't swear their service. In this way, Rivethun emissaries serve as intermediaries between the Universe and the spirit world.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Additional Feats</title>

This archetype has some feats at a level other than their original level.
Such feats are marked with a \*.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rivethun Emissary Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7571) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 292

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) [Rivethun](/Deities.aspx?ID=388) is a philosophy which characters may choose as their religion. Doing so fulfills the “follower of Rivethun” access condition._

**Archetype** [Rivethun Emissary](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=308)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39); Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

**Access**
Followers of Rivethun have access to this feat.

</column>

---

You’re a practicing Rivethun emissary, skilled at interacting and bonding with the spirits of living creatures. You become an expert in Diplomacy and Religion. You also gain the Bond with Spirit activity and the [_entreat spirit_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2432) focus spell. If you don’t already have one, you gain a [focus pool](/Rules.aspx?ID=285), which you can regain using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) activity to nurture your personal well of spiritual power. Your Rivethun focus spells are [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells; when you gain this feat, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for Rivethun focus spells is Wisdom.

Bond with Spirit ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=595)) You can forge a spiritual bond with a creature that is at least friendly toward you or with a terrain that you’re currently in. Forming this bond takes 10 minutes, during which time you must remain adjacent to the creature or within that terrain. If the creature is intelligent, this also requires that creature’s consent, and that intelligent creature can choose to sever this bond with you at any time as a free action, which has the concentrate trait. This bond lasts as long as you are within a mile of the creature or terrain, until you use Bond with Spirit again, or until you make your daily preparations. You must be Bonded with a Spirit to cast the entreat spirit focus spell.

You forge a mystical bond with a spirit or create a spirit from a fragment of your own soul. You gain a familiar. If you already have a familiar, you gain the [Enhanced Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=4717) feat.

Your familiar gains two additional [familiar abilities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2125) each day, one of which must be used to select the following master ability.

**Synchronize Spirit** You can synchronize your spiritual energy with that of your familiar to temporarily become part spirit yourself. Once per round, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) to synchronize your spirit with that of your familiar. You remain synchronized with your spirit until the beginning of your next turn. While synchronized, whenever you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) without a duration that deals damage, you deal spirit damage instead of your normal damage.

You forge an intense spiritual bond of mutual trust and appreciation with a single spirit that you have already bonded with using Bond with Spirit. Forming this bond takes 24 hours of communion, during which time you must remain within 30 feet of the creature or within that terrain. If the creature is intelligent, this also requires that creature’s consent, and that intelligent creature can choose to sever this bond with you at any time as a free action, which has the concentrate trait. This spirit is your domain spirit. The bond between you and your domain spirit is not weakened by time or distance, but you can only maintain one such bond at a time, regardless of how many bonded spirits you can maintain.

Select one domain related to your domain spirit. You always have the option to select the [healing](/Domains.aspx?ID=78) or [soul](/Domains.aspx?ID=51) domain. If your spirit is a creature, select your domain from the following: [ambition](/Domains.aspx?ID=64), [confidence](/Domains.aspx?ID=67), [family](/Domains.aspx?ID=74), [might](/Domains.aspx?ID=83), [protection](/Domains.aspx?ID=90), or [trickery](/Domains.aspx?ID=94). If your spirit is a terrain, select your domain from the following: [air](/Domains.aspx?ID=65), [cities](/Domains.aspx?ID=66), [darkness](/Domains.aspx?ID=69), [earth](/Domains.aspx?ID=73), [nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=85), [travel](/Domains.aspx?ID=93), [water](/Domains.aspx?ID=98), or [wood](/Domains.aspx?ID=63). If your spirit has a trait that shares a name with a domain, you can add that domain to your list of available options. Your GM can choose to add domains to your list of available options, to represent your domain spirit’s unique interests. The domain you select from among your available options must have a clear connection to your domain spirit. For example, if you bond with a [fire elemental](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=410), you add the [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76) domain to the list of options available to you, but if you bond with a deserted tropical island, you can’t select the cities domain, even though it’s among the options usually available to terrain spirits. Your GM is the final arbiter of which domains you can select from. You gain the initial domain spell for that domain. This domain spell is a Rivethun focus spell.

You can choose to bond with a new domain spirit, ending your bond with your current domain spirit and bonding with a different one, to change your selected domain. This process takes 24 hours and follows all the same requirements for forming a bond with your initial domain spirit. During this time of communion, you do not have access to your domain spells granted by your domain spirit. When this bond is formed with your new domain spirit, select one domain related to your new spirit, following the above rules for selecting a domain.

Each creature in the area must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC with the following results.

**Failure** The creature is dazzled for 1 minute.<br />

You spend 1 hour communing with powerful spirits of the world to gain insight, information, or advice. Select advice or answers.

If you selected advice, choose a particular goal or activity you plan to engage in today, or an event you might expect to happen today. The spirits share with you a cryptic clue or piece of advice that could help with the chosen event, often in the form of a rhyme or omen. 

If you selected answers, ask two clear and concise questions. The spirits answer your questions. If the question is easy for the spirits to answer accurately, they answer clearly. Otherwise, they answer cryptically, often in the form of a rhyme or omen.

Regardless of your choice, the spirits additionally bless you, granting you a +1 status bonus with a skill that the spirits believe will be of use to you today. The GM selects this skill on behalf of the spirits. This bonus lasts until the end of the day.

Communing with powerful spirits of the world and other powers far greater than yourself fills your heart with purpose and inspires you to strive for greater accomplishments. Whenever you Consult the Spirits, you gain a +1 status bonus to Will saving throws until the next time you make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575). This bonus increases to +2 against emotion and fear effects. In addition, until the next time you make your daily preparations, you can do each of the following once. 
<ul><li>Roll a Will save twice and use the better result.</li><li>Roll an attack roll twice and use the better result.</li><li>Roll a skill check twice and use the better result; this skill check must be made with the skill that the spirits blessed during Consult the Spirits.</li></ul>

You’re a practicing Rivethun invoker, able to enter a trance that connects you physically and mentally to surrounding spirits. You become an expert in Athletics and Religion. You also gain the [Diehard](/Feats.aspx?ID=5140) general feat and the Enter Spirit Trance ability. 

**Enter Spirit Trance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) You enter a self-imposed trance that helps you push the physical limits of your body. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level plus your Constitution modifier. The trance lasts for 1 minute, until you fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), or until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it, whichever comes first. While in this trance, you gain a +1 status bonus to Fortitude and Will saving throws and your melee [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) deal 1 additional [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. Other abilities may require you to be in a spirit trance. When the trace ends, you lose any remaining [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) from Enter Spirit Trance, and you can’t Enter a Spirit Trance for 1 minute.

You gain an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack that deals 1d8 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage for the duration of your spirit trance. At 5th level, this unarmed attack gains the benefits of a [_striking_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) rune. At 12th level, this unarmed attack gains the benefits of a _greater striking_ rune. At 20th level, this unarmed attack gains the benefits of a _major striking_ rune.

You rush forward, moving enemies aside to reach your foe. You [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305), attempting to move through your enemies’ spaces. Roll an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check and compare the result to the Fortitude DC of each creature whose space you attempt to move through during your Stride, moving through its space on a success but ending your movement before entering its space on a failure. You can then [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), regardless of how your Stride ended. You can use Barreling Charge to [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.

You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) equal to half your level to that damage type for the duration of your spirit trance. If you use Invoke Defense again, you can choose a different type of damage, but you lose the previous resistance.

You can dash your foe to the ground with a single blow. When you use Slam Down, instead of making a Strike followed by a Trip, you can attempt a single Strike. If the Strike you make with Slam Down hits, you can automatically get a critical success on your Trip instead of rolling a check. (Both the Strike and Trip still count toward your multiple attack penalty.) If you used a two-handed melee weapon for the Strike, you can use the weapon’s damage die size instead of the regular die size for the damage from a critical Trip.

The spirits you’ve invoked throughout your life have left behind echoes and spiritual fragments, which you can manifest across your own flesh, temporarily transforming you into something more akin to spirit than mortal. For 1 minute, you gain [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 5 and you become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62). You can’t use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404). Your [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) gain the benefits of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) property rune. Whenever you deal damage with a Strike, you can choose to have that Strike deal [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, rather than its usual damage type.

If you would be knocked [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) value would increase while One with the Spirits is active, the spirits revive you at the beginning of your next turn, restoring you to 30 Hit Points. One with the Spirits then immediately ends.

You're a practicing Rivethun involutionist, with a deep well of inner power. You become an expert in Nature and Religion. You cast spells and gain the Cast a Spell activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common cantrips from the divine spell list or any other divine cantrips you've learned or discovered. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for Rivethun involutionist archetype spells is Wisdom.

If you already have an animal companion, your current animal companion becomes blessed by the spirits instead. This animal companion follows all the usual rules for animal companions. When you activate this blessing, all damage dealt by your animal companion’s Strikes deal [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, rather than the usual damage those Strikes would deal. This blessing remains active until the beginning of your next turn.

Your animal companion has grown up over the course of your adventures, becoming a mature animal companion and gaining [additional capabilities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2117).

Your animal companion has greater independence. During an encounter, even if you don't use the Command an Animal action, your animal companion can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Strike or Stride (or Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim if it has that Speed). It can do this at any point during your turn, as long as you aren’t currently taking an action. If it does, that’s all the actions it gets that round—you can’t Command it later.

<a id="archetype-378"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Rose Warden](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=378)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
</traits>

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 84

Tyrants may try to destroy the seeds of dissent before they can bloom, but the goddess Milani and her followers strive to cultivate the hope that helps nourish those seeds, allowing them to one day sprout into revolution. As a rose warden, you advocate for such change, perhaps emerging from the ranks of the downtrodden yourself to defend your fellow citizens and push to unseat all tyrants everywhere. You tend not to seek personal fame or glory and perhaps even work as a swift blade from the shadows that strikes at the heart of oppression.

 But you are no mere criminal or anarchist. You would rather that innocent people not be harmed as part of your quest for societal revolution. So that rightful demonstrations do not turn into destructive riots, you intercept those who would spark that explosive powder, perhaps even taking on the ire of the authorities solely on yourself. You also look to gain allies in these fights, but you still try to protect those friends from being captured or shackled. The sound of freedom rings out in your every word and deed.

 More and more individuals calling themselves rose wardens have begun to appear in Nirmathas recently, possibly bolstered by Courage Heart's arrival. She is a herald of Milani who has aided Nirmathas's army in its battles against Molthuni invaders.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">Milani's Edicts and Anathema</title>

The Everbloom's faith concerns hope and those who war against oppression. Her edicts and anathema are printed below for convenience. 

**Edicts** confront oppression in all its forms, defend the common folk, overcome despair to seize victory

 **Anathema** abandon those in need, enslave or oppress others, harm the innocent through direct or inadvertent action

 Edicts and anathema are intended as tools for roleplay. You, the GM, and other players should work together to determine how they'll influence your game.
</aside>

---

As a follower of the Everbloom, you stand up against tyranny and oppression, understanding that revolution against an unjust ruler must sometimes be enacted in secret. You become trained in Deception. If you're already trained in Deception, you become an expert in your choice of Deception or Stealth. When you get a critical success to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) to a figure of authority, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC and saving throws against being [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by that figure of authority for 24 hours.

 You add the edicts and anathema of Milani to your own (see sidebar). Failing to uphold edicts or committing acts that violate the anathema result in you losing access to any abilities granted by this archetype, as determined by your GM. You can regain these lost abilities through the atone ritual as normal.

<a id="archetype-303"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=303)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
</traits>

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 114

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Runelords refocus by indulging in their sin. Players are reminded that the community guidelines still apply and should take caution if roleplaying this refocus activity._

You’ve learned arcane magic, following the path of the runelords. You learn the secrets of runic magic, the building blocks of magic. But be warned: You might succumb to sin in your pursuit of power. The seven runes held in highest regard by the runelords echo the addictive power of the seven sins.

 Beyond the runes themselves, you also learn the techniques of the ancient runelords. You learn to use their signature weapons and can acquire the secrets of the ancient magic items called aeon stones, embedding them into your skin.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Runelord</title>

You draw untold power from runes, sometimes called sin magic. You associate with one of the seven sins, also known as the seven rewards of rule: envy, gluttony, greed, lust, pride, sloth, and wrath. If you choose this class archetype, you must select Runelord Dedication as your 2nd-level class feat.

**Prerequisites:** You must be a wizard.<br />**Runelord Adjustments:** You become trained in martial polearms and spears. When your proficiency for simple weapons increases, your proficiencies in these weapons increases as well. You learn the Thassilonian language. Instead of an arcane thesis, you gain a personal rune. Your personal rune also affects your arcane bond. You must select the [School of Thassilonian Rune Magic ](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=25)as your arcane school, and you must choose one sin to specialize in. When you cast any curriculum spell or school spell from the School of Thassilonian Rune Magic, you do so simply by tracing runes of power in the air. This removes the need to speak incantations aloud. When you Refocus, you do so by contemplating or indulging in your sin.

Each sin is opposed by two others. The incompatibility of these sins means that casting magic philosophically appropriate to those opposing sins, as represented by each school's anathema, interrupts your connection to your own sin and personal rune. If you violate your sin's anathema, you lose the benefits of your personal rune, and whenever you attempt to cast a curriculum spell or school spell, you must succeed at a DC 15 flat check or the spell is lost. This disruption lasts until you complete an [atone](/Rituals.aspx?ID=108) ritual; unlike a normal atone ritual, Arcana can be used for both the primary and secondary checks.

Your curriculum spells (including spells of your own sin) never violate this anathema, sometimes providing alternatives to prohibited magic.

You gain [Advanced School Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=5036) as a bonus feat at 8th level, gaining the advanced school spell for the School of Thassilonian Rune Magic; once you've begun your studies of sin magic, there is no turning back from its allure.

<title level="3">Arcane Bond and Personal Rune</title>

Runelords hail from an era where even a scholar was expected to be able to defend themself with arms if necessary, leading to the practice of attaching a blade to the typical wizard's staff. You must choose a [polearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11) or [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14) as your arcane bond. In place of an arcane thesis, you have a personal rune, which appears on your bonded weapon. The weapon functions as a staff only you can prepare and contains the sin spells from your sin up to the highest rank of spell you can cast (including your cantrips). Your personal rune isn't a property rune and doesn't count against the weapon's limit of such runes.

When you prepare your bonded weapon as a staff, you can physically merge one other staff in your possession into it, adding the staff's spells to your bonded weapon until your next daily preparations. While merged, the weapons haft takes on aesthetic aspects of the staff.

 You can also use this activity to safely remove an embedded _aeon stone_ in 1 day. Someone without this feat can attempt to surgically remove it safely by spending 1 day and succeeding at a DC 30 Medicine check, or hastily by simply ripping it from a corpse.
