You strive to change the outcome with sheer zeal. You gain a +1 status bonus to your attack roll if making an attack or to your AC if you were hit. This can change the outcome of the roll. If this bonus turns your missed attack into a hit or the hit against you into a miss, attempt a DC 5 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). If you fail, your soulforged armament is [Dismissed](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311)—your weapon if you attacked or your armor or shield if you were defending.

Choose an additional soulforged armament of a different type than you already chose, and choose one essence power for it. Upgrade or change your armaments individually.

When you Manifest Soulforged Armament, you can summon any number of your armaments (you must meet the requirements for each), and when you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the effect, you can choose to Dismiss some and not others. You can choose to manifest the essence form of any number of your armaments when you take the action. Each armament can manifest its essence form only once per day.

When you gain soulforged corruption, you choose one armament’s corruption flaw to affect you for stage 1. At stage 2, you take the flaws of all your soulforged armaments. While you have the curse, each armament gets a separate [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) if you try to manifest its essence form, and failing the check prevents you from manifesting only that armament’s essence form.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time at 12th level, choosing the final item type.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Devastating Manifestation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9354) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 98

**Archetype** [Soulforger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=393)

**Prerequisites**
[Soulforger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9350)

**Requirements**
At least one of your soulforged armaments is not manifested.

</column>

---

Your armaments are especially powerful the moment after you manifest them. You Manifest Soulforged Armament. If you manifested a weapon, make up to two [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with that weapon, each targeting a different creature and each dealing an additional 1d6 spirit damage. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but your penalty doesn’t increase until you have made all your attacks. If you Manifested an armor or shield, you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 5 to all damage until the start of your next turn. If you manifested both a weapon and an armor or shield, you gain both effects.

<title level="1">Essence Powers</title>

Your soulforged armament has an essence power you choose when you first bind it. It
gains the power temporarily when you manifest its essence form. Each power has a
corruption flaw that affects you if you have _soulforged corruption_. Essence powers
that only apply to some types of armament indicate which.

<title level="2">Adaptable Persona</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 236

Armor only. When you manifest the essence form, gain your choice of a climb Speed or swim Speed equal to your land Speed. If you're 8th level or higher, you can choose a fly Speed instead.

**Corruption Flaw** You take a –10-foot penalty to all your Speeds.

<title level="2">Bounding Spirit</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 236

Melee weapon only. The weapon gains the [thrown 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) trait and has the [_returning_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301) rune (even if it already has its maximum number of property runes).

**Corruption Flaw** When you make a Strike with a thrown or ranged weapon and miss, reroll the Strike, targeting your ally nearest to the target. This Strike uses the same multiple attack penalty as the missed Strike and doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty.

<title level="2">Deep-Seeded Fear</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 236

You gain a +2 status bonus to your [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks and don't take any penalties for not sharing a language when [Demoralizing](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) foes who can perceive your armament's essence form. When you manifest the essence form, you can attempt to Demoralize an enemy who can perceive the manifestation.

**Corruption Flaw** If you attempt to Demoralize an enemy, your Demoralize also targets the ally closest to you.

<title level="2">Determined Toughness</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 236

Any status penalties you take from the following conditions are 1 less than their condition's value: [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37). This doesn't change the actual condition value, or any other effects of the condition (such as stupefied's disruption and its DC).

**Corruption Flaw** Whenever you take a status penalty from the listed conditions, you also take a –1 penalty to the same statistics.

<title level="2">Harmful Malice</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Negative" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=118" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

Your Strikes deal an additional 1d4 negative damage. Once while the armament is manifested, you can cast [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=146) as an innate spell, with a level equal to half your level rounded up.

**Corruption Flaw** Reduce any damage you would deal by half your level.

<title level="2">Heroic Heart</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

You gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Perception checks, skill checks, and saves.

**Corruption Flaw** You take a –1 penalty to attack rolls.

<title level="2">Healing Grace</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Positive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=128" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

You gain [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) equal to half your level. You can cast [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) once as an innate spell with a level equal to half your level rounded up.

**Corruption Flaw** Reduce all healing you would receive or grant with a spell by half your level.

<title level="2">Magical Resilience</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

Armor or shield only. You gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws and AC against spells. If you're 5th level or higher, you can cast [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) once as an innate spell. The spell level is equal to 1 lower than half your level rounded up (2nd level if you're 5th or 6th level, and so on).

**Corruption Flaw** You take a –1 penalty to saving throws and AC against spells.

<title level="2">Planar Bond</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

Armor or shield only. When you manifest the essence form, choose one damage type: acid, chaotic, cold, electricity, evil, fire, good, lawful, negative, positive, or sonic. You gain resistance equal to your level + 2 to damage of the selected type.

**Corruption Flaw** You gain weakness 1 to all damage.

<title level="2">Planar Pain</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

Weapon only. When you manifest the essence form, choose one damage type: acid, chaotic, cold, electricity, evil, fire, good, lawful, negative, positive, or sonic. Attacks with the weapon deal this type of damage instead of their physical damage with a +2 status bonus to the damage.

**Corruption Flaw** When you deal damage with a weapon or unarmed attack, you take 2 damage of the last type you chose for planar pain, even if the damage type normally wouldn't harm you, such as good damage if you aren't evil.

<title level="2">Pull of Stasis</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

Weapon only. Any time you hit with the soulforged weapon, the target takes a –10-foot penalty to its Speeds for 1 round. On a critical hit, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) for 1 round instead.

**Corruption Flaw** You take a –10-foot penalty to all your Speeds.

<title level="2">Reflecting Spirit</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

Armor or shield only. You gain a +2 status bonus to AC against physical ranged attacks. If an enemy's physical ranged attack misses you, you can use your reaction to immediately attempt a ranged Strike against the attacker using the projectile that missed.

**Corruption Flaw** You have weakness 5 to physical ranged attacks.

<title level="2">Resolute Defiance</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 237

Shield only. The shield gains a +2 status bonus to its Hardness and gains temporary Hit Points equal to your level + 2 that last until the essence effect ends. If you don't have the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction, you gain it while your shield is manifested.

**Corruption Flaw** When you take damage while [Raising a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98) or use Shield Block, attempt a DC 5 flat check. If you fail, the shield is Dismissed if it's your soulforged armament or Dropped if it's a different shield.

---

<a id="archetype-126"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 122

Just as Golarion's merchants scour busy marketplaces for newfound goods, scholars of magic congregate in teahouses, debate at symposia, and haunt the back rooms of esoteric shops to swap secrets of their trade. In such meetings, a different kind of magic may strike: the spark of innovation! The mixing of magical techniques produces fascinating and unpredictable results. As one of these innovators, sometimes called a spell trickster, you have a knack for pioneering magical techniques and discovering new effects from spells most novice spellcasters take for granted. Whether your unique abilities are the result of weeks of experimentation or a secret passed to you by a traveling practitioner, you delight in surprising others with your tricks.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">The Fruits of Research</title>

While magic can spring from many sources, from wizard tutors to self-taught savants, the art of the spell trickster often springs from sophisticated magical research. The magical academies in Golarion have no claim to magic as a whole but can often teach lesser-known variants of a spell to their students. At the Magaambya academy in the Mwangi Expanse, for instance, initiates study multiple traditions of magic, adapting the techniques of harnessing magical essence from one tradition to create new methods of casting spells in another. The Arclords of Nex have spent thousands of years honing spells in both wartime and peace, demonstrating a fine control over the arcane by effortlessly changing their magic to suit their whims. The return of New Thassilon brought thousands of magical dabblers and scholars, each with their own unique tricks and each eager to see what new spell variants have developed in their long absence.

 This isn't to say that spell tricksters come solely from high academia. A sorcerer might demonstrate aberrant powers in her bloodline magic, hinting at a background more complex than a single eldritch influence acting upon her. An oracle might grope at a divine power that they poorly understand and cast a spell in a unique manner simply because they were never taught otherwise. A witch's patron or a whimsical deity might grant a favored servant a special power for whatever strange motives such beings might possess. Magic in Golarion isn't entirely predictable, no matter how many practitioners wish that it was so. While most spellcasters follow predictable patterns in their art, there are always exceptions.

 The rules in this section are presented as part of an archetype, meant for a character dedicated to the art of innovating magic—but you don't have to limit yourself to this premise. At the GM's discretion, a spell trickster feat could be made available to a character as a class feat without the character taking the archetype. In most cases, this option should only be offered as a reward or story element that the character, GM, or group has dedicated a significant amount of time to developing—a character who wishes to partake in these options without GM permission or involvement should simply take the spell trickster archetype. These feats could be used to represent the payoff from extended magical research; finding forgotten or forbidden lore in a lost corner of Golarion; pleasing a god, patron, or other notable power; a magical plane or artifact exerting its influence; or any other number of situations that an adventurer might encounter while exploring. Keep in mind, however, that these feats were created and balanced to be part of an archetype. If allowing spell trickster feats as general class feats begins to negatively impact the game, the players should be willing to walk the decision back and rebuild characters as necessary.
</aside>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 122

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
Able to cast spells; Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

Your experience with magic and its traditions lets you specialize in the casting of certain spells, customizing familiar spells to create novel effects. Whenever you gain a feat from this archetype, you either learn to modify the effects of a single spell, or you change one of the modifications from a previous feat. Each time you Cast the Spell corresponding to the feat you chose, you decide whether to cast its normal or modified version. You can only apply one modification to a spell at a time, even if you know more than one modification for that spell. Besides modifications mentioned in the feat, the spell functions as normal.

 Choose up to two 4th-level spell trickster archetype feats for which you meet the spell-casting prerequisite. You gain those feats, ignoring their level prerequisite.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the spell trickster archetype. The two feats you gain from taking the dedication don’t count toward this total.

<title level="2">Spell Trickster Dedication leads to...</title>
[Agile Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3369), [Animate Net](/Feats.aspx?ID=3376), [Barrier Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=3370), [Confounding Image](/Feats.aspx?ID=3377), [Directed Poison](/Feats.aspx?ID=3393), [Disk Rider](/Feats.aspx?ID=3378), [Drenching Mist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3379), [Forceful Push](/Feats.aspx?ID=3371), [Lingering Flames](/Feats.aspx?ID=3385), [Obscured Terrain](/Feats.aspx?ID=3380), [Scattered Fire](/Feats.aspx?ID=3386), [Shining Arms](/Feats.aspx?ID=3372), [Siphoning Touch](/Feats.aspx?ID=3387), [Smoldering Explosion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3388), [Steal Vitality](/Feats.aspx?ID=3389), [Summon Ensemble](/Feats.aspx?ID=3373), [Surrounding Flames](/Feats.aspx?ID=3390), [Toppling Tentacles](/Feats.aspx?ID=3391), [Tracing Sigil](/Feats.aspx?ID=3374), [Uneasy Rest](/Feats.aspx?ID=3381), [Volatile Grease](/Feats.aspx?ID=3382), [Wild Lights](/Feats.aspx?ID=3375)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Agile Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3369) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 122

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177)

</column>

---

When you cast _mage hand_, you can modify its target to be a set of [thieves' tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=58). When you Cast the Spell in this way, the tools move up to 20 feet towards a device or lock. After you Sustain the Spell on future turns, you can use the tools to attempt [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) checks to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=69) or [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=70) within the spell's range, but you take a –2 penalty to your Thievery check. If you critically fail, the spell ends and you can't use this modification again for 24 hours.

<title level="2">Agile Hand leads to...</title>
[Larcenous Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3384)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Barrier Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=3370) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 122

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=280)

</column>

---

When you cast _shield_, you can modify the spell to create a solid barrier you can use for cover, but not for blocking. You can't use the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction when the spell is modified in this way, but you (and only you) can spend an action to [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=90) to gain standard cover from it.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Forceful Push](/Feats.aspx?ID=3371) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=15" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 122

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177)

</column>

---

When you cast _mage hand_, you can modify its target to be 1 creature. If you do, replace its standard effects with the following: You push your foe telekinetically. Make a spell attack roll against the target's Fortitude DC. On a success, you [push](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) the target 5 feet away from you. On a critical success, you push the target 10 feet away from you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Shining Arms](/Feats.aspx?ID=3372) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 122

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=171)

</column>

---

When you cast _light_, you can modify its target to be 1 melee weapon, either unattended or possessed by you or a willing ally, and modify its duration to be 1 minute. If you do, add the following to its effects: When a creature wielding the weapon critically hits a foe, you can Dismiss the Spell as a reaction, causing the foe to be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round. After you use this reaction, you can't use this modification again for 10 minutes.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Summon Ensemble](/Feats.aspx?ID=3373) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_summon instrument_](/Spells.aspx?ID=721)

</column>

---

When you cast _summon instrument_, you can modify its duration to be sustained, up to 1 minute. When you do, you summon a number of instruments equal to your spellcasting ability modifier that hover around you and play of their own accord. Once per turn when you Sustain the Spell, choose an opponent within 30 feet who can hear your performance. The target must attempt a Will save against the spell's DC; on a failure, it becomes distracted by your performance and becomes [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) for 1 round. The target is then temporarily immune for 24 hours.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tracing Sigil](/Feats.aspx?ID=3374) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_sigil_](/Spells.aspx?ID=286)

</column>

---

When you cast _sigil_, you can modify the spell to add the following to its standard effects: The target leaves a magical trail that you and others can try to follow. You and other creatures can attempt to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) the target, substituting an [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check (whichever matches the magical tradition of your sigil spell) for the [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) check. Much like Tracking with Survival, this must take place somewhere the target has been and follow the trail; it doesn't allow anyone to find the target from a distance. You can only have a single target marked with a modified sigil in this way. If you use this ability again on a second target, the _sigil_ spell on the first target ends, and your mark fades.

<title level="2">Tracing Sigil leads to...</title>
[Beacon Mark](/Feats.aspx?ID=3383)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wild Lights](/Feats.aspx?ID=3375) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_dancing lights_](/Spells.aspx?ID=58)

</column>

---

When you cast _dancing lights_, you can modify its duration to be 1 minute and modify its standard effects to create a single floating light in the shape of a Tiny creature, instead of up to four floating lights. The creature hovers over your head unless you spend a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait to direct the light to move up to 30 feet, in which case it remains there until you direct it again. If you direct it back to your head, it hovers there and follows you again until you direct it elsewhere. If the light ever moves beyond 120 feet of you, it winks out immediately.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Animate Net](/Feats.aspx?ID=3376) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_animate rope_](/Spells.aspx?ID=667)

</column>

---

When you cast _animate rope_, you can modify its target to be 1 [net](/Equipment.aspx?ID=681). If you do, replace the spell's standard effects with the following: You cause a net to animate and throw itself at a Medium or smaller creature within 20 feet of the net. Attempt a spell attack roll against the target's Reflex DC. On a success, the target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) and takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79); on a critical success, it's also [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until it Escapes. The Escape DC is equal to your spell DC as long as the spell lasts. Once the spell ends, the Escape DC returns to the normal DC for a net (usually 16), and a creature adjacent to the target can Interact to remove the net.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Confounding Image](/Feats.aspx?ID=3377) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_mirror image_](/Spells.aspx?ID=197)

</column>

---

When you cast _mirror image_, you can modify its duration to be sustained up to 1 minute and modify its range to 30 feet. If you do, replace the spell's standard effects with the following: You create an illusory duplicate of yourself that appears in an unoccupied square within range. The image takes up space and has a reach of 5 feet, and your allies can flank with the image. It doesn't have any other attributes a creature would normally have other than an AC equal to your spell DC and saving throw modifiers equal to your spell DC – 10. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, or if you ever move more than 30 feet from it, the spell ends. Creatures can move through its space without hindrance. When you Sustain the Spell, you can move the image to an unoccupied square within range.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Disk Rider](/Feats.aspx?ID=3378) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_floating disk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=124)

</column>

---

When you cast _floating disk_, you can modify its duration to be sustained, up to 10 minutes. If you do, add the following heightened entry to its effects.

**Heightened (3rd)** The disk can hold up to 10 Bulk. The spell no longer ends if you ride atop the disk (though it does if any other creature rides atop it, including if the creature is riding on you). If you are riding the disk, it changes its capacity to hold you, plus additional Bulk equal to the maximum you could carry without being [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=12). If you ride atop the disk, you can direct it to move along the ground up to 30 feet or your Speed, whichever is slower, each time you Sustain the Spell. While you ride atop it, the disk can move over liquids as long as it ends its movement on solid ground. If it ends its movement on a surface that can't support it, the spell ends.

<title

The area within the fog is difficult terrain for creatures that can't see through fog or mist. You can Dismiss the cloud.

</title>

</column>

---

When you cast _grease_, you can modify its target to be 1 creature. If you do, replace the spell's standard effects with the following: You splash the target with combustible grease. The target must attempt a Reflex save.

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.<br />
**Success** The target is splattered with grease and gains weakness 2 to [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) until the end of your next turn. The target or an adjacent creature can rub off the combustible grease with an Interact action, ending the effect.<br />
**Failure** As success, except the weakness to fire lasts for 1 minute.

---

**Heightened (+2)** The weakness increases by 1.

When you cast _sigil_, you can modify the spell to add the following heightened entry.

 **Heightened (4th)** You attune yourself to the marked target. While the spell lasts, you can spend a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=43), and [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) traits, to attempt to locate the target, learning the direction to the target as long as you are within 1 mile of it. If the target is a creature or a creature is in possession of the target object, the creature can attempt a Will saving throw against your spell DC. If it succeeds, your attempt to locate the target fails and you can't attempt this again for 1 day. You can only have a single target marked with a _sigil_ modified in this way. If you Cast this Spell again on a second target, the _sigil_ spell on the first target ends, and your mark fades.

When you cast [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), you can remove its duration, modify its range to 20 feet, and modify its target to be an attended object within the spell's Bulk limit that wouldn't be time-consuming to remove. Add the following to the spell's standard effects: If the creature attending the object is willing to have you take the item, _mage hand_ carries the item to you. If the creature is unwilling, you must attempt to [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68) the target object with a [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check. The usual restrictions on attempts to Steal an object apply, including the restrictions that you can't steal objects that would be extremely noticeable or time-consuming to remove (like worn shoes or armor or actively wielded objects) and you can't Steal from a creature in combat or otherwise on guard. On a successful Steal check, the _mage hand_ carries the item to you, and on a critical failure, you can't use this modification again for 1 hour. If you're a master in Thievery, you can attempt to Steal from a creature in combat or otherwise on guard, though if you do so, the spell's casting time increases by 1 action.

 **Heightened (+1)** The damage is increased by 1d6 and the persistent fire damage is increased by 2.

Sticky black tentacles attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) each creature in the area. Attempt spell attack rolls against the Reflex DCs of each affected creature. Creatures treat the spell's area as difficult terrain.

<a id="archetype-32"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 6" pfs="Standard">[Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 114

Those who train under the Master of Spells concern themselves with all matters related to magic. Though not all members of the School of Spells are spellcasters, those who would become Spellmasters of the highest rank and influence have at least some spellcasting capabilities.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Pathfinder Society Archetypes</title>

The following archetypes are uncommon, but are available to members of the Pathfinder Society. Qualifying characters with the [Pathfinder agent archetype](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=13) can select one of these dedication feats even if they have not gained three feats from the Pathfinder agent archetype, and each of these archetypes’ feats fulfills the [Pathfinder Agent Dedication’s](/Feats.aspx?ID=871) special requirement despite not being from the Pathfinder agent archetype.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 114

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence 14, Wisdom 14, or Charisma 14; ability to cast focus spells; member of the Pathfinder Society affiliated with the School of Spells

**Access**
A character who is a member of the Pathfinder Society has access to this option.

</column>

---

As a Spellmaster, you are adept at identifying magic. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus when you [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24) with a skill in which you are trained or better. If you have the [Wayfinder Resonance Tinkerer](/Feats.aspx?ID=875) feat, you can change the cantrip you chose for that feat each day during your daily preparations.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Spellmaster archetype.

<title level="2">Spellmaster Dedication leads to...</title>
[Absorb Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1138), [Communal Sustain](/Feats.aspx?ID=2245), [Familiar Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=2241), [Glyph Expert](/Feats.aspx?ID=2242), [Master's Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2247), [Mobile Magical Combat](/Feats.aspx?ID=2248), [Recover Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2243), [Spellmaster's Resilience](/Feats.aspx?ID=1137), [Spellmaster's Ward](/Feats.aspx?ID=2244), [Surreptitious Spellcaster](/Feats.aspx?ID=1135), [Ward Casting](/Feats.aspx?ID=1136)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Familiar Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=2241) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

</column>

---

You can use your magic to transform into a small creature of a type that commonly serves as a spellcaster's familiar, potentially allowing you to safely scout for your party while retaining a degree of spellcasting ability. You gain the [_familiar form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=832) focus spell. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Glyph Expert](/Feats.aspx?ID=2242) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

</column>

---

You've learned to recognize the telltale writings and other signs that indicate the presence of magical traps. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find magical traps, to AC against attacks made by magical traps, to saves against magical traps, and to checks to [Disable](/Actions.aspx?ID=69) magical traps. Even if you aren't [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519), you get a check to find magical traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap. 

You're also adept at avoiding the effects of traps that feature magical writing, such as runes, glyphs, ancient script, or other forms. When you attempt a saving throw against the effects of these traps, if you roll a success, you get a critical success instead. If you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Surreptitious Spellcaster](/Feats.aspx?ID=1135) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 114

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

</column>

---

You’ve learned that it pays for a Pathfinder to be able to cast spells without being noticed. You gain the [Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=640) wizard class feat, though it’s not a wizard feat for you. You also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to Conceal a Spell and to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to conceal verbal components.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Recover Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2243) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

**Requirements**
An enemy's action disrupted your attempts to Cast a Spell since the beginning of your last turn.

</column>

---

You recover the energy of a recently disrupted spell, allowing you to cast it again as long as you do so immediately before the energy dissipates. You regain the use of a spell that was disrupted since the beginning of your last turn, but you must immediately Cast the Spell again with your next action or else you lose the spell; as normal for metamagic, this must be on the same turn that you use Recover Spell. You can change the area, targets, and other variables, including the number of actions used to Cast the Spell if the spell allows, such as when casting [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) or [_magic missile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=180).

    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spellmaster's Ward](/Feats.aspx?ID=2244) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

</column>

---

You can create a number of powerful shielding runes that bolster your defenses against damaging spells by absorbing the worst of the energy to keep you safe. You gain the [_spellmaster's ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=833) focus spell. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ward Casting](/Feats.aspx?ID=1136) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134); [Steady Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=194)

**Trigger**
You attempt a flat check for Steady Spellcasting, but you haven’t rolled yet.

</column>

---

You carefully ward your spell by drawing from a mantle of magical energy you prepared to protect your casting, increasing your chance of retaining the spell. You reduce the DC of the flat check for Steady Spellcasting from 15 to 10.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Communal Sustain](/Feats.aspx?ID=2245) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

once per round

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

</column>

---

Choose one spell with a sustained duration that one of your allies has in effect. You must be within 30 feet of the chosen ally. The ally can Sustain the Spell once as a free action, triggered at the start of their next turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spellmaster's Resilience](/Feats.aspx?ID=1137) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 114

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

</column>

---

Your experience with a specific type of harmful magic makes you more resistant to it. Choose a magical tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal). You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells and effects with that tradition’s trait and resistance 5 to all damage from spells and effects with that tradition’s trait. The effect must have actually been cast or created with that tradition, rather than simply being on that tradition’s spell list.

<title level="2">Spellmaster's Resilience leads to...</title>
[Spellmaster's Tenacity](/Feats.aspx?ID=2246)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Absorb Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1138) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 114

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134); spell repertoire or ability to prepare spells

**Trigger**
You critically succeed at a saving throw against a foe’s spell, and that spell is of a level you can normally cast.

</column>

---

You absorb a spell and store it in your body. If you are a spontaneous spellcaster, you can cast the triggering spell once during the next 10 minutes, even if it’s not on your spell list as if it were in your repertoire. If you are a prepared spellcaster, you can replace one of your prepared spells of the same level with the absorbed spell, but you must cast the absorbed spell within 10 minutes or you lose that spell slot for the day. You cast the spell at the same spell level as the spell you absorbed, but the spell is of your magical tradition and uses your spell DC, spell attack roll, and other statistics to determine its effects.

<title level="2">Absorb Spell leads to...</title>
[Retain Absorbed Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2249)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster's Resilience](/Feats.aspx?ID=1137)

**Trigger**
You critically fail at a saving throw against a foe's spell, and that spell was cast or created with the tradition of magic you selected with the [Spellmaster's Resilience](/Feats.aspx?ID=1137) feat.

</column>

---

You call upon the power of your spells to protect you from the worst of the magic headed your way. You fail your saving throw instead of critically failing. For 1 minute, increase the circumstance bonus to saving throws from the Spellmaster's Resilience feat to +2, and increase the resistance to damage it grants to 10.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Master's Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2247) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The trigger for Master’s Counterspell should begin with “A creature Casts a Spell that you have prepared or is in your repertoire...” to provide a trigger for spontaneous spellcasters as well as prepared spellcasters._

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134); master in spell attack rolls and spell DCs

**Trigger**
A creature Casts a Spell that you have prepared, and that spell was cast or created with a tradition of magic in which you have master proficiency in spell attack rolls and spell DCs.

</column>

---

When a foe Casts a Spell and you can see its manifestations, you can use your magic to disrupt it. If you're a prepared caster, you can expend a prepared spell to counter the triggering creature's casting of a spell. If you're a spontaneous caster, you can expend a spell slot. The level of the prepared spell or spell slot must be at least as high as the triggering spell's level. You lose your prepared spell or spell slot as if you had Cast the Spell. You then attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the triggering spell, and you take a –2 penalty to your counteract check; for prepared casters, the GM might waive the penalty if the spell you're expending to counterspell is especially appropriate—such as countering with the same spell, or using a [_cone of cold_](/Spells.aspx?ID=47) to counteract a [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mobile Magical Combat](/Feats.aspx?ID=2248) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134)

**Requirements**
You're wielding a melee weapon and have Cast a Spell requiring at least 1 action this turn.

</column>

---

You dart around the battlefield, casting spells while you carefully make melee attacks with your weapon. Stride once. If you end your movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, you can make a melee Strike against that enemy. You can use Mobile Magical Combat while [Burrowing](/Actions.aspx?ID=93), [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94), or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Retain Absorbed Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2249) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[Absorb Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1138)

</column>

---

When you absorb a spell using the [Absorb Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1138) reaction, you utilize secret, techniques that allow you to retain the power and knowledge necessary to cast the spell repeatedly—potentially for a greater period of time. If you're a spontaneous caster, you can cast the triggering spell up to three times instead of once. If you're a prepared spellcaster, you can replace up to three of your prepared spells of the same level with the absorbed spell instead of one. Either way, you can choose to retain the absorbed spell for the next hour instead of the next 10 minutes; if you choose to extend the absorption to an hour, you can't use Absorb Spell again until one hour after the spell is absorbed.

<a id="archetype-394"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 102

You may or may not cast spells, but you’ve always possessed an uncanny knack for attuning yourself to the ebb and flow of the mystical currents that power them. Thanks to specialized training or natural aptitude, you’ve honed this gift into the ability to exert a modicum of control over magical spells cast nearby, allowing you to reshape and repurpose their energies to suit your own designs. You might use this talent for any number of purposes: to enhance the spells cast by you or your allies, to weaken and confound magic-wielding enemies, or even just to covertly humiliate rival spellcasters foolish enough to cross you.

As a spellshifter, you carry a special implement called a conduit, a seemingly mundane tool or object that you use to tap into the magical vibrations that suffuse the world around you. Only you can use this conduit, and every spellshifter’s conduit is unique. Yours might represent something distinctive about your personality, your relationship to magic, or the circumstances under which you first discovered your powers.

Spellshifters aren’t widely known in many parts of the world, and individuals with the innate potential to become one are sometimes regarded by distrustful spellcasters as jinxes whose mere presence might cause magic to malfunction or behave unpredictably. Past experience with these sorts of superstitions might drive you to actively conceal your powers from those who might fear them, or it might motivate you to seek out any opportunity to flaunt them openly, refusing to be cowed by the prejudice of others.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 102

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)

</column>

---

You can exert your will over magical spells cast in your vicinity, potentially altering or controlling their effects. You accomplish this through the use of a spellshifting conduit, a magical object of your choice that has light Bulk and can be held in one hand. If your conduit is lost or destroyed, you can train yourself to use a new one by spending 10 minutes attuning yourself to it. You gain the Shift Spell action and the Share the Burden spellshift.

**Shift Spell** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Requirements** You are within the affected area of an ongoing spell, or you can physically touch an object or creature under the effects of a spell, and you are holding your conduit; **Effect** Choose a spellshift and attempt an [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check against the DC of the spell (or the spell DC of the spellcaster if the spell does not normally have a DC). The caster immediately becomes aware that you’re trying to shift their spell and intuitively knows the potential effects of the shift, but not the result of your skill check. A willing caster can allow you to achieve one degree of success higher than the result of your check. The effects of the check are dependent on the chosen spellshift. Regardless of the result, the spell becomes immune to Shift Spell for 24 hours. 

**Spellshift—Shift Burden** You share the burden of a spell, allowing you to share control with the caster. If [Sustaining](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) a spell with this spellshift causes a creature to attempt a saving throw, it is attempted against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, make the attack using your Arcana modifier instead of the spell’s normal spell attack modifier.

**Critical Success** If the spell is sustainable, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell. For the remainder of the spell’s duration, you can Sustain the spell as though you were the caster.<br />
**Success** If the spell is sustainable, you can Sustain the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell.

<title level="2">Spellshifter Dedication leads to...</title>
[Analyze Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9356), [Dismantle Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9359), [Elemental Subsitution](/Feats.aspx?ID=9357), [Enhance Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9361), [Reactive Spellshift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9360), [Redirect Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9362), [Subtle Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9358)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Analyze Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9356) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

</column>

---

Your intuitive understanding of magic allows you to read the energy of a spell in the air. You gain the Analyze Magic spellshift.

**Spellshift—Analyze Magic** Once you’ve homed in on a spell or magical effect, you can study its unique magical signature to immediately understand exactly what it does.

**Critical Success** You learn information about the spell or effect as if you had critically succeeded at a skill check to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) using the appropriate skill for its magical tradition.<br />
**Success** You learn information about the spell or effect as if you had succeeded at a skill check to Identify Magic using the appropriate skill for its magical tradition.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Elemental Subsitution](/Feats.aspx?ID=9357) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

</column>

---

You can tamper with the elemental energy of a spell. You gain the Elemental Substitution spellshift.

**Spellshift—Elemental Substitution** Raw elemental energy is the fuel powering some of the most iconic spells of destruction ever devised, and you’ve discovered a method for realigning the magical pathways through which that energy flows into the material world.

**Critical Success** If the targeted spell inflicts [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage, you change its damage type to your choice of one of acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage. If the effect has a duration, it inflicts damage of its new type for 1 minute, then returns to normal.<br />
**Success** As critical success, except if the effect has a duration, it inflicts damage of its new type until the beginning of your next turn, then returns to normal.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Subtle Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9358) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

</column>

---

You’ve learned how to hide your meddling from the casters of spells you’re shifting. If your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check when Shifting a Spell is greater than its caster’s [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) DC, you can prevent the caster from learning the effects of the shift you’re attempting to apply. On a critical success, they don’t become aware that you’re applying a shift at all (although the effect of the shift might still give you away).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Dismantle Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9359) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Your innate power can shut down other magic. You gain the Dismantle Spell spellshift.

**Spellshift—Dismantle Spell** You attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) a spell or at least suppress its effect for a time.

**Critical Success** The spell is counteracted if its rank is no more than 1 higher than half your level rounded up.<br />
**Success** The effects of the spell are suppressed until the start of your next turn. If the spell has a duration that is measured in rounds, its duration is extended by 1 round. If the spell does not have a duration, it targets the same creature or area as though it had just been cast at the start of your next turn.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Reactive Spellshift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9360) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

**Trigger**
A creature within 30 feet casts a spell.

**Requirements**
You are holding your conduit.

</column>

---

You can reflexively shift a spell even as it’s being cast. You attempt to Shift the triggering Spell even if you do not meet the other requirements to Shift Spell. On a success, the spellshift applies to the spell’s effects as appropriate for the chosen spellshift. After you choose your spellshift, but before you attempt your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check, the caster can voluntarily let their spell be [disrupted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236). Regardless of the outcome, the caster then becomes immune to your Reactive Spellshift for 10 minutes.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

</column>

---

You attune your senses to the magical frequencies generated by an allied spellcaster, allowing you to amplify or modify their spells to suit the needs of the moment. Select one willing ally within 30 feet that you can see and choose one of the following spellshape feats: [Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4997), [Nonlethal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=5027), [Reach Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4577), or [Widen Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4715). The target gains the benefits of the feat on their next turn as though they had taken the [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513) action themselves; this requires them to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) as their first action on their turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Redirect Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9362) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394)

**Prerequisites**
[Spellshifter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9355)

</column>

---

You can alter the flow of magic around you, moving a spell effect from one target to another. You gain the Redirect Magic spellshift.

**Spellshift—Redirect Magic** Through sheer force of will, you can direct a spell’s energies away from its caster’s intended target.

**Critical Success** You change a single target of the spell to another viable target within 30 feet of you (even if it would be outside of the spell’s normal range). You can’t use this spellshift to affect a creature twice with the same spell. If the spell had an initial saving throw, the new target must attempt it, possibly achieving a different result than the original target of the spell. The DC for the spell becomes your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) DC instead of the original caster’s spell DC.<br />
**Success** As critical success, but if the target succeeds at any required saving throw, they are unaffected, and the spell does not change targets.

<a id="archetype-122"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Spellshot](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=122)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Guns &amp; Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 140

Spellshots aren't ordinary [gunslingers](/Classes.aspx?ID=20). They come from a tradition of ancient secrets and principles, which they temper with modern innovation and perspective. Spellshots combine magical power into the art of gunplay to create a distinct and mystical way known only to spellshots, enigmatic and unavailable to other gunslingers in the world at large. The first to identify themselves as spellshots tied their magical traditions to the history of the Star Code and the Crowned Regents in Arcadia. Ancient, reclusive crafters known as the Crowned Regents created star guns, the legendary magical firearms that shot white-hot blasts of energy. Wielders of star guns became bound together by the Star Code—a set of cultural expectations that defined how one should behave while using these powerful weapons. You can find more information about star guns, the Crowned Regents, and the Star Code in _Guns &amp; Gears_.

 Most spellshots continue to come from Arcadia, as the stories describing the relevant skills and training to become one have been passed down over the generations. Many gunslingers who grow up in this region hear of these tales early in their lives, and they develop the techniques to channel magical energy through their firearms in imitation of the Regents' arcane methods. While Arcadia is home to the vast majority of the world's spellshots, the techniques have slowly spread to other regions. However, spellshots remain particularly rare in the Inner Sea region due to the unique history of guns there and their connection to the Grand Duchy of Alkenstar, which exists in a magic-dead region of the Mana Wastes.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="3">Way Of The Spellshot (1st)</title>

You've learned the intricacies of magic and technology, blending the two together with deadly results. You combine a knowledge of arcane theories with a strong connection to your chosen weapon that allows you to manifest unique effects, though your knowledge doesn't extend as far as actual spellcasting. You can imbue energy into your weapon and conjure bullets from thin air. As you progress, you eventually learn to phase bullets through walls or even to teleport yourself along the path of your bullets. You must select Spellshot Dedication as your 2nd-level class feat.

 **Prerequisites**: You must be a gunslinger.

 **Spellshot Adjustments**: Instead of choosing a way from the options listed in the gunslinger class, you have the way of the spellshot. It has the following way skill, slinger's reload, and deeds. You gain these abilities at the same levels as normal for the class. You use Intelligence for your class DC.

 **Way Skill** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)

 **Slinger's Reload** Thoughtful Reload

 **Deeds** _Initial_ Energy Shot; _Advanced_ Recall Ammunition; _Greater_ Dispelling Bullet

You cast arcane spells like a [wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=39), gaining a [spellbook](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2753) with four common [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) cantrips of your choice. You gain the Cast a Spell activity. You can prepare two cantrips each day from your spellbook. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for spellshot archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are arcane spells. You become trained in Arcana; if you were already trained in Arcana, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. This counts as the wizard archetype for the benefits of [Basic Wizard Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5109).

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat other than [Beast Gunner Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3229) until you've gained two other feats from the spellshot or beast gunner archetypes.

[Basic Wizard Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5109) <actions string="" />

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 223

You combine your own magic with that of your magical crossbow or firearm. You gain the Spell-Woven Shot activity.

**Spell-Woven Shot** <actions string="Three Actions" />  **Requirements** You are wielding a loaded magic firearm or magic crossbow; **Effect** You Cast a Spell that takes 1 or 2 actions to cast and requires a spell attack roll. The effects of the spell do not occur immediately but are imbued into the required weapon. Make a Strike with that weapon. Your spell flies with the ammunition, using your attack roll result to determine the effects of both the Strike and the spell. This counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty, but you don’t apply the penalty until after you’ve completed the Spell-Woven Shot.

You can aim your bullets not just in three normal dimensions, but in additional dimensions as well, removing all obstacles between you and your target. Attempt a crossbow or firearm [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against a foe who’s [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=84) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) to you (but not [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96)). The ammunition travels to your target in a straight line, passing through any non‑magical barriers or walls in its way, though magical barriers and force effects stop the bullet. The shot ignores all [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372), the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition, the hidden condition, and circumstance bonuses to AC from shields. It has a +4 status bonus to hit creatures wearing any type of armor. The Strike’s damage can’t be reduced with a [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction using a non‑magical shield.

On a success, if the target was within 120 feet, you and all your gear are teleported to an open space of your choice within 10 feet of the target.

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Spirit Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=274)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 92

Warriors can draw powers from the joy and the sadness in their hearts, spiritual gifts and burdens they can share and give to others. They cultivate experiences from their adventures to nurture and grow their spiritual power, learning to channel it through martial arts techniques tailored to their style and personality. Once they’ve created a martial art that combines a favored weapon and specialized unarmed techniques, spirit warriors learn to channel spirit energy through their limbs and weapons. Spirit warriors are typically found in the Forest of Spirits, the Chuyokai Forest, and the Valashmai Jungle.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

You’re a warrior who trains your spirit and body to work in perfect harmony, enhancing your attacks with your spiritual energy while fighting with a ferocious martial technique that combines blade and fist. The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6 instead of 1d4, and your fist gains the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait. You don’t take the normal –2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack with your fist or any other unarmed attacks. You gain the Overwhelming Combination action.

**Activate—Overwhelming Combination** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([flourish](/Traits.aspx?ID=606))   **Requirements** You’re wielding a one-handed melee weapon or a melee weapon with the agile or finesse trait; **Effect** Make two [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against a target within your reach, one with the required weapon and one with your fist [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack. If both hit the same target, combine their damage for the purposes of its [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty to each Strike normally.

<title level="2">Spirit Warrior Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cutting Heaven, Crushing Earth](/Feats.aspx?ID=7024), [Flowing Palm Deflection](/Feats.aspx?ID=7025), [Gods' Palm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7028), [Intercepting Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=7031), [Kaiju Defense Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=7021), [Sacred Wilds Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=7022), [Sheltering Pulse](/Feats.aspx?ID=7029), [Spirit of the Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7026), [Sword of Sealing](/Feats.aspx?ID=7032), [Sword-light Wave](/Feats.aspx?ID=7027), [Transcendent Deflection](/Feats.aspx?ID=7030), [Tricksterbane Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=7023)

You’ve sworn an oath to defend the helpless from dangerous titanic beasts, including [kaiju](/Traits.aspx?ID=383) that roam the surface of Golarion. Attacks made as part of your Overwhelming Combination ability gain a +4 circumstance bonus to damage against a creature at least 2 sizes larger than you, or +6 if you have master proficiency with the weapon you used. You also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws and DCs against kaiju hazards. You gain the following edict. 

**Edict** You must do everything within your power to protect others from massive creatures they can’t defend themselves from; in the event the victims are evil or actively trying to harm you or other innocents, you don’t have to save them.

You’ve sworn an oath to protect the holy places within nature and the spirits that dwell within, from ancient trees to primordial wild guardians. You can use [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on animals and to make very simple [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) of them. In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks to Make an Impression when interacting with a [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=547), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599), or [kami](/Traits.aspx?ID=354). You gain the following edict. 

**Edict** You must aid any animal or nature spirit in need unless it violates your other tenets or puts someone else at risk of immediate harm.

You’ve sworn an oath to ferret out and destroy malevolent shapechangers who pose as mortals with evil intent. You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to detect a shapechanged creature’s disguise, and a +2 circumstance bonus to attempts to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about shapechangers. Whenever you use Overwhelming Combination against a shapechanged creature, you attempt to counteract one polymorph effect on that creature. The counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) check modifier is your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus with the weapon used to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) as part of your Overwhelming Combination. You gain the following edict.

**Edict** You must reveal and slay evil or predatory shapechangers you discover or encounter, as long as you have a reasonable chance of success.

Your skill in combining fist and blade has grown into a seamless art where each attack makes an opponent more vulnerable to the next. As long as you have invested and are wearing a set of [handwraps of mighty blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086), you also apply their runes to a single weapon you’re wielding that can be used with your Overwhelming Combination ability. You gain the following benefits.
<ul><li>When you successfully Strike an opponent with this weapon, it’s [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to the next Strike you make against it with a fist unarmed attack before the end of your next turn.</li><li>When you successfully Strike an opponent with your fist unarmed attack, it’s off-guard to the next Strike you make against it with a one-handed, [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), or [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602) melee weapon before the end of your next turn.</li></ul>

Your spiritual power pierces both body and soul, pinning your foe in place. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a one-handed, [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), or [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602) weapon, or your fist unarmed attack. On a successful hit, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or your spell DC, or become [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81). The target can end this immobilization with a successful [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) attempt using the higher of your class DC or your spell DC as the Escape DC.

**Prerequisites**
Dexterity 16; Trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1); Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3); trained with at least one of the following weapons: [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=12), [bo staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=17), [halfling sling staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=78), or any weapon in the [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14) or [polearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11) group (referred to in this archetype as “your staff”)

</column>

---

When you [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) while wielding your staff, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to any [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check required and add 5 feet to the distance you can Leap vertically and horizontally. You can [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) even if you don’t have a free hand, provided you are wielding your staff. Finally, when you roll a success on a check to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) while wielding your staff, you get a critical success instead.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the staff acrobat archetype.

<a id="archetype-205"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Stalwart Defender](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=205)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

**Source** [Highhelm](/Sources.aspx?ID=204) pg. 110

The military history of the [dwarves](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=1) is a story of largely defensive combat and tactics, whether it be as simple as guarding a camp during the Quest for Sky or a protracted siege, such as at the Sky Citadel of Kraggodan. The martial discipline of the stalwart defender arose over the course of centuries to become an iconic dwarven warrior, capable of holding their ground against overwhelming odds and not ceding an inch of stone.

 To be a stalwart defender is to stand with the resilience of a mountain. When danger arrives you face it unflinchingly, allowing your enemy's blows to glance off you like wind whistling past granite. This mindset comes naturally to dwarves, while other ancestries typically need specialized training to attain the determination needed for such a style.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

Such feats are marked with a \*.

**Prerequisites**
trained in light armor

**Access**
You are a  dwarf  or have undergone defender training in a dwarven settlement such as Highhelm.

</column>

---

You have completed your initial training in the ways of a stalwart defender. You gain the Tenacious Stance action. 

 **Tenacious Stance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=152)) **Requirements** You are wearing armor; **Effect** You steady yourself, as tough and immutable as stone. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to half your level (minimum 1) and a +2 circumstance bonus to DCs against being [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) and [Tripped](/Actions.aspx?ID=40). However, you no longer negate your armor check penalty or Speed penalty for having a high Strength while in this stance. After you leave Tenacious Stance, you lose any remaining temporary Hit Points from the stance, and you become temporarily immune to gaining temporary Hit Points from Tenacious Stance for 1 minute.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you take two other feats from the stalwart defender archetype.

<title level="2">Stalwart Defender Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cracked Mountain](/Feats.aspx?ID=4181), [Crushing Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=4175), [Gathering Moss](/Feats.aspx?ID=4180), [Gravel Guts](/Feats.aspx?ID=4176), [Mountain Skin](/Feats.aspx?ID=4173), [Rupture Stomp](/Feats.aspx?ID=4178), [Stalwart Song](/Feats.aspx?ID=7697), [Stone Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=4182), [Tunnel Wall](/Feats.aspx?ID=4174), [Unshaken in Iron](/Feats.aspx?ID=4179), [Upset Balance](/Feats.aspx?ID=4177)

As a stalwart defender, you rely on your martial training and your tried-and-true armor to face any danger without flinching. Your mountain-like resilience and courage draw strength from the centuries-old traditions of dwarven song. You bring to mind—and possibly give voice to—a cherished dwarven song of inspiring heroism, granting you a +2 circumstance bonus to the saving throw.

Emulating the great defenders throughout dwarven history, you close your mind to the sensation of pain, becoming as resolute as stone itself. You gain resistance 10 to all damage. This effect lasts until the end of your next turn or immediately upon being critically hit.

<a id="archetype-275"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype 2" pfs="Standard">[Starlit Sentinel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=275)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 94

Though the zodiac is known throughout Tian Xia for subtly watching over the continent, sometimes the 12 constellations find more direct action necessary. When a grave threat arises, a zodiac constellation might shine on an everyday student or worker, granting them the power to transform into a powerful alter ego to repel those threats. Though most of these starlit sentinels act covertly when the world is asleep, some become well known either as urban legends or outright celebrities, though usually only as their alter ego. Some might find themselves pulled between the dual pressures of an unassuming civilian identity working in a market by day, and the defender of that same market from rampaging oni or qi-stealing jiang-shi under the light of the stars. Due to a quartet of well-known female sentinels operating out of Goka, many have come to believe that the zodiac chooses only girls as its champions, but the heavens care little for such mortal concerns and are equally likely to grant their power to those of any gender. Starlit sentinels are rare, even in Tian Xia, and individual sentinels are unique; a new sentinel empowered by a given constellation won’t awaken as long as the previous sentinel of that constellation is active.

</column>

</column>
