<a id="archetype-200"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype " pfs="">[Ursine Avenger Hood](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=200)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 183

Some items inherit their magic not through an intentional spell or ritual but through generations of use and belief, slowly accumulating power and intent from those around them. The [_Ursine Avenger Hood_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2368) is such an item. After defeating a powerful [cave bear](/Monsters.aspx?ID=48), the Ulfen hunter Baruk shaped the bear's head and fur into a helm and cape for himself. Baruk later fell in battle against a [linnorm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=69), successfully slaying the beast before succumbing to its death curse. His helm, soaked in the blood of man and linnorm and saturated with the magic of the linnorm's curse, was claimed by Baruk's daughter, who often told stories about the helm giving her a bear's strength and ferocity, though it was unclear at the time whether this was a boast.

 Over many generations, the magic of the hood was proven true, and more than that, the magic continued to grow and evolve with ever-more-ursine attributes. As the belief and power of each new wearer soaked into the hood, the artifact's potential has continued to grow. Now, those who bond with the generational artifact will discover that the _Ursine Avenger Hood_ continues to grow in power alongside them.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

>

<traits>

<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />

<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 183

**Archetype** [Ursine Avenger Hood](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=200)

---

You draw the _[Ursine Avenger Hood](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2368)_ over your head and its fur over your arms, assuming an ursine form that has traits of your original form as well as that of a bear. In your ursine form, you gain a jaws [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage and a claws unarmed attack that deals 1d6 slashing damage and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) trait. Both unarmed attacks are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group. You lose the ability to speak complex sentences while transformed and can only communicate through grunts and gestures; this prevents you from using effects that require a shared or spoken language until you revert back to your non-hybrid form. You can use this action while transformed to remove the hood and return to your original form.

<a id="archetype-201"></a>

<title level="1" right="Archetype " pfs="">[Gelid Shard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=201)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 184

The Varki wizard T'aak Chamin once traveled from the Lands of the Linnorm Kings northward, past the Winterwall Glacier and deep into the frozen wastes of the Crown of the World. T'aak was seeking immortality without the risk of undeath, and he followed the hints and clues of ancient legends that spoke of “the frozen immortals,” and of ancient magics of ice crafting that were once commonly traded between these rumored immortals and the Erutaki people, who share ancestral roots with the Varki.

 Little is known of T'aak's journeys in the northern wastes, though all accounts that record anything of the wizard and his trek indicate that the man who returned was different in many ways than the man who first traveled north. T'aak spoke of beings known as saumen kar, of a “great whale” sealed beneath the ice, and of strange corruptions. An account left by his wife mentions that T'aak often awoke screaming about “malignant sludge” and a “disease clawing at the ancient gates.” Despite all this, T'aak's primary quest did result in at least one notable accomplishment: the crafting of the first [_gelid shard_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2369).

 _Gelid shards_ are arcane focuses of refined magical cold in physical form. Unfortunately for their creator, _gelid shards_ do not grant immortality, though mortal creatures bonded to them do often have slightly longer lifespans thanks to the preserving cold that inundates and surrounds them.

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

You learn to cast arcane [spontaneous spells](/Rules.aspx?ID=2224), and you gain a spell repertoire with the [_frostbite_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1539) and [_frost’s touch_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1274) (see below) cantrips. You’re trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC. Your key spellcasting attribute is Charisma.

<title level="1" right="Archetype " pfs="">[Splinter of Finality](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=317)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 124

During the events of the [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99), the [_final blade_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094) known as _Silent Lenore_ was overwhelmed by a surge of psychic energy that shattered it into 13 fragments. While many _final blades_ since recovered have been rendered inert and harmless by means of the [blunt the final blade](/Rituals.aspx?ID=69) ritual, the remnants of _Silent Lenore_—and perhaps some other _final blades_ still unaccounted for—were recovered in secret and crafted into powerful talismans of cruelty. 

The _splinter of finality_ is an archetype artifact, a type of powerful item that’s described [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=1961).

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

[Click here for more rules on using this archetype.](/Rules.aspx?ID=1961)

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 124

**Archetype** [Splinter of Finality](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=317)

**Requirements**
You have a hand free and aren’t already wielding a _spectral dagger_.

</column>

---

By touching the [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772) in your neck, you conjure a _spectral dagger_ into your hand that resembles the splinter wrapped in a crude hilt. This weapon acts like a [_+1_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) [_dagger_](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358), and each successful [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with it deals 1 additional [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. If the attack is a critical hit, this damage increases to 1d6. If the _spectral dagger_ ever leaves your hand, it vanishes and you must spend an action to conjure it again. If this occurs as the result of you making a ranged thrown Strike with the dagger, you resolve the attack before the weapon vanishes.

You can increase the power of your _spectral dagger_ with runes like you can other weapons, transferring the rune from a runestone or other weapon by meditating over the rune as a downtime activity that takes 1 day.

<title level="2">Spectral Dagger leads to...</title>
[Dread Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7705), [Guillotine Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7712), [Hungry Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=7709), [Lethal Edge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7708), [Soul Bleed](/Feats.aspx?ID=7706), [Soul Oubliette](/Feats.aspx?ID=7713)

When you successfully [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with your _spectral dagger_ and damage a foe with the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition, they can’t reduce their frightened condition below 1 before the end of your next turn.

When you score a critical hit with your _spectral dagger_, you deal 1d6 [persistent spirit damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). If the target wasn’t already taking persistent spirit damage when you scored the critical hit, you gain temporary Hit Points equal to the spirit damage dealt by the attack that last until the beginning of your next turn.

Your brush your fingers across your [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772), momentarily creating a metaphysical vortex from which mortal spirits struggle to escape. For the next minute, [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) treat all squares within 30 feet of you as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and living creatures within the same area die from the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition at dying 5 rather than dying 4. As it comes close to tasting a living soul, the _splinter of finality_ is empowered. If a living creature’s dying value increases while within your Soul Well, your _spectral dagger_ deals one additional weapon die of damage until the end of your next turn.

When the terrified are struck by your spectral weapon, they feel the anguish of every life taken by _Silent Lenore_. You apply one of the following effects, which lasts until the end of your next turn.
<ul><li>The target can’t use reactions.</li><li>The target is [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1.</li></ul>

---

Once your _spectral dagger_ has tasted an enemy’s soul, your [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772) becomes increasingly relentless in its attempts to claim the soul. Your _spectral dagger_ gains the effects of a [_keen_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843) property rune that applies only to Strikes against the target of the required Strike. This effect lasts for 10 minutes or until that target dies, whichever comes first.

---

You wreathe yourself in the tatters of all the souls claimed by your blade. Until the start of your next turn, you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 10 to all damage except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), and [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), doubled if the source of the damage is non-magical. If you slay a significant foe not immune to spirit damage with your _spectral dagger_ while under this effect, its duration increases until the end of your next turn.

Your [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772)  has reached the apex of its death-dealing potential. Whenever you critically succeed at an attack roll against an enemy and use Lethal Edge, add the following effects to the list you can choose from. 
<ul><li>The target is cursed and can’t benefit from circumstance or status bonuses. This is a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) effect.</li><li>The target gains [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 10 to [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage.</li></ul>

---

The echoes of the [_splinter of finality's_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772) original purpose resonate through the artifact. For the next minute, your _spectral dagger_ gains the benefits of a [_vorpal_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2853) rune. When you use Snicker-Snack with your _spectral dagger_, the DC of the Fortitude save is 37, your class DC, or your spell DC, whichever is higher.

---

Your mortal strike wrenches the soul from your victim’s body and imprisons it in your [_splinter of finality_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3772), with the effects of [_seize soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1664). The _splinter of finality_ can only hold one soul at a time, but you can release a trapped soul as a free action. If you don’t free a soul willingly, it escapes automatically after 24 hours. However, if you touch the _splinter of finality_ to an unbroken final blade while a soul is trapped within, the soul is transferred to the [_final blade_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094) and imprisoned indefinitely. 

While your _splinter of finality_ contains a trapped soul, you gain [fast healing](/Rules.aspx?ID=2322) 15.
